d5ebb86c74a79761718f03dc.title: 17 simply smashing things to do in London next month – from food festivals to live music, stunning exhibitions, floating museums, and more
d5ebb86c74a79761718f03dc.author: Sam Barker
d5ebb86c74a79761718f03dc.content:
![the famous st pauls cathedral of london during sunset](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18173758/shutterstock_2458359623-1024x683.jpg) 
As August and the summer weather slowly come to a close, we’re turning our eyes to September, and all that’s in store for us in London. But fret not – the summer isn’t quite over yet. After all, it’s not officially autumn until late September!
You don’t quite need to head inside to make buckets of hot chocolate just yet. And while we can probably expect the temperatures to drop, there are still a few summer-y days in store. Regardless of the weather, with everything going on, there’ll be no pleas to ‘wake me up when September ends’. Here’s our rundown of simply smashing things to do in London this September.
![a crowd of festival attendees at the Siren Stage at Waterworks 2023](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/09183210/230916_WATERWORKS_2023_RobJones_%40hirobjones_%40khromacollectiveIMG_5531-1024x683.jpeg)
While festival season pretty much draws to a close in August, there are still a few events to enjoy in the city if you love live music. Check out the following festivals to wring the most out of 2026’s summer of fests:
🎶 Waterworks Extended (September 12-13): the cancelled festival will instead take the form of a massive 36-hour-long party at The Cause.
🎵 HowTheLightGetsIn London 2026 (September 19-20): the world’s largest philosophy & music festival.
![people milling about in front of a stage emblazoned with a sign for celebrasia](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/22163650/celebrASIA-at-Battersea-Power-Station-c-Brendan-Bell-2-1024x683.jpg)
Cekebrasia returns this September with an enormous celebration of South East Asia. The FREE-to-visit culture and food festival features a huge range of vendors, attractions, live performances, and activations that celebrate the incredible diversity of food, culture, and creativity across the 11 ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) member countries.
Visitors can expect to find over 35 food and drink vendors, an artisan market with more than 50 traders, live music, craft workshops, cooking classes, and more.
![two people playing in a huge ball pit with dark pink walls at Bubble Planet](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/19172251/Bubble-Planet-16-1024x683.jpg)
Bubble Planet is a wild and wonderful immersive experience that surrounds visitors with a seemingly never-ending world (planet?) of bubbles. As you make your way through themed rooms, you’ll explore fantastical landscapes and even step aboard a hot air balloon flight simulator. It’s a feast for the senses, and a true joy to experience
Celebrate Black culture and creativity
![people milling about trafalgar square on a sunny day at the 'Black on the Square' celebration](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/05130233/BlackOnTheSq_0147MRES-1024x683.jpg)
Black on the Square is a FREE annual event in London’s Trafalgar Square that celebrates and highlights Black culture and creativity. It’s a chance to acknowledge and celebrate “the people and communities who contribute to the capital’s creativity”. All are welcome to enjoy the food, entertainment, workshops, activities, stalls, and more.
Find out more here.
Feast on meat at Meatopia
![a food vendor at meatopia, stood at a stand with a large boat behind them, carving meat to portion into servings for festival attendees](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18102252/September-01-2024-untitled-shootEV1A3198-1024x683.jpg)
Meatopia is a love letter to BBQ, where hungry Londoners can feast on meat to their heart’s content. Going strong since 2013, when it crossed the pond from New York, where the festival was founded, Meatopia offers up 4 days of delicious food from “some of the very best live-fire chefs from UK, Europe and the World”.
Find out more and grab your tickets here.
![London Eye as seen from up high with the House of Parliament and River Thames behind it](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/23095652/London-Eye-Rebrand-Drone-Photography-39-1024x767.jpg)
Think the London Eye is only for tourists? Think again! Many people, even local Londoners, probably don’t know that you can spot some real gems from up there – things you had no idea you could see from the heart of London.
This summer, book yourself a ticket for a ride in one of the capsules and look out for these lesser-known sights, including the centuries-old Cleopatra’s Needle, two hidden rooftop gardens, a couple of castles, and much more.
![The exterior of Senate House (left), the St Pancras clocktower (right)](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/15092417/Copy-of-FACEBOOK-SPLIT-IMAGE-34-1024x576.jpg)
The London Open House Festival returns to London this September, giving us mere mortals the chance to cross the threshold of some of the city’s most exclusive establishments. Hundreds of sites across the city will be throwing open their (usually firmly locked) doors for the occasion, including the likes of:
🏦 OXO Tower
👀 Old Royal Naval College
🏦 English National Ballet
👀 Senate House
🏦 St Pancras Chambers and Clock Tower
👀 BBC Broadcasting House
and many more!
![Sabrage acctress dressed in fancy dress with gloves surrounded by bottles of bubbly](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/30094930/She-doesnt-just-walk-the-walk-she-walks-on-bottles-%F0%9F%8D%BE-Welcome-to-the-stage-Kylie-%F0%9F%A5%82-Sabrage-j-2-1024x802.jpg)
If you’re after a high-octane night out, bouncing over to Sabrage is well-advised. The acclaimed spectacle melds circus and acrobatic skills with a wardrobe of striking outfits and burlesque performance. Grab a cocktail and some southern bar bites and sit back to enjoy the show – it’s only in town for a limited time!
![The Bayeux Tapestry on display at a museum](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/20153925/Bayeux-Tapestry-%C2%A9-Bayeux-Museum-2-min-1024x682.jpg)
The Bayeux Tapestry will return to the UK for the first time in almost 1000 years this September. It’s part of what is expected to be the British Museum’s most popular exhibition ever.
The Bayeux Tapestry is an elaborately embroidered cloth, telling the tale of the Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings. Spanning a whopping 70 metres, it will find a temporary home at the British Museum, courtesy of a loan agreement made with the Bayeux Museum in Normandy.
![Jack White at his art studio ahead of debut exhibition in London](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/17174727/Jack-White-art-studio-1024x683.jpg)
The arrival of the Bayeux Tapestry isn’t the only exciting exhibition coming to London this September. Here are our picks of the best exhibitions to see in London:
💜 Amar Kanwar (September 23, 2026 – January 31, 2027): Serpentine North Gallery – a site-specific installation showcasing Kanwar’s blend of filmmaking, largely exploring the legacies of decolonialisation and the partition of India and Pakistan.
❤️ Marilyn Monroe: A Portrait (Ends September 6): National Portrait Gallery – portraits of the Hollywood icon created by some of the most renowned photographers and artists in the world.
🖤 Modern Toss: “Having an exhibition yeah?” (Ends September 6): The Drawing Room – two decades of work by cartoonists Modern Toss, with 100 pieces, including token-operated swearing machines, big stone heads, large-scale paintings, and more.
🤍 Jack White: THESE THOUGHTS MAY DISAPPEAR (Ends September 13): Newport Street Gallery – Jack White of White Stripes, and, well, Jack White fame, launched his debut visual art exhibition at Damien Hirst’s Newport gallery.
💚 Waldmüller: Landscapes (Ends September 20): The National Gallery – “Discover the breathtaking landscapes of one of Austria’s greatest painters, Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller”
 Trans is Human (Ends September 27): Queer Britain – portraits by renowned photographer Mariano Vivanco that celebrate “thirteen inspiring, familiar and very ordinary transgender people from across the UK.”
 James McNeill Whistler (Ends September 27): Tate Britain – see the infamous ‘Arrangement in Grey and Black No.1’, also known as ‘Whistler’s Mother’ at Europe’s largest retrospective of James McNeill Whistler in 3 decades.
![Various boats moored at a central London marina](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/06101459/PTAIT_20230909_7353-HR-1024x684.jpg)
The Classic Boat Festival returns to St Katharine Docks this September – and it’s completely free to visit! A fleet of beautifully preserved vintage vessels will splash down at central London’s only marina for two days’ worth of maritime merriment. This year, the boats to see and explore include the likes of Dunkirk Little Ships, historic steam tugs, and Thames Sailing Barges.
![a performer leading a parade, twirling brightly coloured cloth around, with an enormous tiger puppet visible in the air behind her](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/03172545/Brick-Lane-Curry-Festival-procession-15_1-1024x683.jpg)
A one-day-only curry festival will fill Brick Lane with flavour, live performances, a parade, giant puppets, and more this September. It’s free to attend, and it’s promising to be “bigger, better and spicier” than before.
Marvel at the Big London Tattoo Show
![a fire performer dancing at the london tattoo show](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/29122113/DSC_2720-1024x731.jpg)
The Big London Tattoo Show returns for its 5th iteration this September – and it’s bigger than ever before. As the UK’s biggest and best tattoo festival, attendees can expect a wealth of artists, demonstrations, live performances and more. The show will feature over 500 artists, live graffiti demonstrations, BMX stunt shows, free fairground rides, and more.
Find out more here.
![Patrick Carney of The Black Keys performs onstage at the 2024 iHeartRadio ALTer EGO Presented by Capital One at the Honda Center on January 13, 2024 in Anaheim, California.](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/05145539/GettyImages-1931289073-1024x683.jpg)
London’s reputation as one of the greatest live music cities in the world is well-earned. From tiny venues showcasing up-and-coming stars to enormous stadium shows, there are countless gigs taking place on any given night in the capital. Here are a few to check out this September:
- The Black Keys (September 1): Brixton Academy
- Geese (September 1-3): Troxy
- The Neighbourhood (September 4): Wembley Arena
- Arijit Singh (September 5): Tottenham Hotspur Stadium
- Hilary Duff (September 10, 15): The O2
- Evanescence (September 13): The O2
- St. Etienne (September 18): The Roundhouse
- Judas Priest (September 21): Hammersmith Apollo
- Death Cab For Cutie (September 25-26): Troxy
- First Aid Kit (September 29): Royal Albert Hall
See a dazzling spectacle on the West End
![text-based poster for RENT the musical with bright neon text](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18162507/RENT-poster-1024x570.jpg)
London is a world-class theatre destination thanks to its iconic West End. Broadway, who? Find out why this city is so famous for its theatrical productions at these shows this September:
NEW OPENINGS
💖 My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?) (September 16 – October 3): Apollo Theatre – “autobiographical story of West End Musical Theatre star and social-media sensation Rob Madge, as they set out to recreate [a homemade childhood Disney] parade.”
🤣 Hay Fever (September 22 – December 12): Wyndham’s Theatre – Christine Baranski makes her West End debut alongside Richard E. Grant in this eternally relatable Noël Coward comedy.
🧚 Into the Woods (Opens September 22): Noël Coward Theatre – classic fairytales collide as this Sondheim and Lapine classic transfers to the West End.
🎸 Rent (September 26, 2026 – March 27, 2027): Duke of Yorks Theatre – the iconic rock-opera-musical from Jonathan Larson returns to the West End, starring Stranger Things’ Gaten Matarazzo.
ENDING SOON
📜 Cyrano de Bergerac (Ends September 5): Noël Coward Theatre – the Royal Shakespeare Company production transfers to the West End following a sold-out run.
💉 Trainspotting the Musical (Ends September 5): Theatre Royal Haymarket – the cult book-turned-film gets the stage musical treatment.
🪄 Now You See Me Live (Ends September 6): London Coliseum – “World-class illusionists unite for a limited London spectacle” inspired by the film of the same name.
🤫 THE TRUTH a comedy by Florian Zeller (Ends September 12): Apollo Theatre – award-winning and -nominated comedy legends helm this play where two couples navigate a web of hidden truths.
🧠 Arcadia (Ends September 12): Duke of York’s Theatre – the same country house sees two similar stories of genius unfolding, separated by two centuries.
📚 Death Note: The Musical (Ends September 12): Barbican – the acclaimed manga gets a hotly-anticipated musical adaptation for just 50 shows.
🥃 Abigail’s Party (Ends September 19): Harold Pinter Theatre – “Tamzin Outhwaite stars as one of the most iconic characters in British theatre – the unforgettable Beverly in Mike Leigh’s ferocious black comedy of suburban life in the 1970s.”
💔 How The Other Half Loves (Ends September 19): The Old Vic – “Three marriages, two homes, and one terrible alibi meet … [this] comedy on sex, class, and domestic partnerships gone wild.”
🎭 The Oresteia (Ends September 19): Bridge Theatre – “A contemporary family wakes up in a Greek myth and can’t seem to find a way out of their hellish destiny.”
🎤 I’m Every Woman – The Chaka Khan Musical (Ends September 27): Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre – Alexander Burke takes on the role of Chaka Khan.
Or explore the city’s boundary-pushing theatre
![actor Josh O’Connor standing on tarmac in a dark, empty scene, bathed in golden light with his eyes closed](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18171552/GoldenBoy_Artwork_Website-1024x410.jpg)
The West End isn’t all that London’s theatre scene has to offer! Instead, at London’s off-West End shows, you’ll find some ground-breaking, boundary-pushing theatrical art being made. Check out these productions to see the future faces of the theatre world:
🚘 Thelma & Louise: A New Musical (September 3 – October 24): Young Vic (Main House) – the iconic film gets a new musical treatment.
💭 Darkling (September 5 – October 24): Bush Theatre – a young girl in Bhopal, India, in 1984, dreams of more from life as a giant factory rises over her town.
😨 Bigfoot Ripped My Dog In Half I Saw It (September 7 – 26): Soho Theatre – “Two teenagers perform fake Bigfoot sightings in their Appalachian town until a neighbour’s dog turns up torn to pieces.”
🥊 Golden Boy (September 8 – October 31): Almeida Theatre – Emmy and Golden Globe winner Josh O’Connor stars in this revival of Clifford Odets’ “knockout American classic.”
👻 The Turn of the Screw (September 11 – October 10): Arcola Theatre: world premiereof a production based on “the seminal ghost story by Henry James”
🍷 Table 17 (September 17 – October 24): Kiln Theatre – two exes attempt to hash things out after 7 years of not speaking, to find out whether they should give love a second chance.
✍️ Tru (September 19 – November 14): Menier Chocolate Factory – Jesse Tyler Ferguson stars as acclaimed author Truman Capote, alone in his New York apartment after the publication of an excerpt from his tell-all novel Answered Prayers.
Get the pints in for Oktoberfest
![A group of men raising steins of beer at the German Gymnasium in King's Cross, each kitted out in lederhosen and stood behind a table of German delicacies](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/05142340/EV-GermanGym-15Aug23-0788-DB-2-1024x733.jpg)
Despite the name, Oktoberfest traditionally starts in September, not October. Instead, the weeks-long celebration ends in October. Regardless, it’s a spirited celebration of great beer, great food, and great (depending on who you ask) brass bands. Plenty of London venues are honouring the traditional dates with celebrations through September. Head here for pints a-plenty:
🍺 DAS HARVEST FEST at Villages Brewery (September 11 & 12) – while not technically an Oktoberfest event, this celebration of the harvest (and lager) from Hop Burns & Black and Villages is in the same spirit as the other celebrations.
🍻 Albert’s Schloss (September 19 – October 25) – over a month of sudsy Bavaraian celebration and feasting awaits you at this enormous bier palace in the middle of London.
🍺 German Gymnasium (September 18 – October 23) – “Bavarian Spezialitäten, German beers, live Oompah performances and a season of celebrations in the heart of King’s Cross.”
🍻 Bermondsey Bierkellar (September 19 – October 31) – “Bigger. Louder. Unforgettable. London’s wildest Oktoberfest returns.”
d5ebb86c74a79761718f03dc.summary: London offers a wide variety of events, festivals, and exhibitions throughout September. Highlights include music events like Waterworks Extended and the London Open House Festival, alongside cultural celebrations such as Black on the Square and celebrASIA. Additionally, major exhibitions like the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum and the Classic Boat Festival provide diverse entertainment options for visitors.
key_points: The Bayeux Tapestry returns to the UK for the first time in almost 1,000 years for an exhibition at the British Museum.
The London Open House Festival allows public access to exclusive buildings and historical sites across the city.
Free cultural events like celebrASIA, Black on the Square, and the Classic Boat Festival take place during September.
Numerous live music gigs and festivals are scheduled, including Waterworks Extended and HowTheLightGetsIn London.

7b9a7a67a223b22152fb70f6.title: 17 simply smashing things to do in London next month – from food festivals to live music, stunning exhibitions, floating museums, and more
7b9a7a67a223b22152fb70f6.author: Sam Barker
7b9a7a67a223b22152fb70f6.content:
![the famous st pauls cathedral of london during sunset](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18173758/shutterstock_2458359623-1024x683.jpg) 
As August and the summer weather slowly come to a close, we’re turning our eyes to September, and all that’s in store for us in London. But fret not – the summer isn’t quite over yet. After all, it’s not officially autumn until late September!
You don’t quite need to head inside to make buckets of hot chocolate just yet. And while we can probably expect the temperatures to drop, there are still a few summer-y days in store. Regardless of the weather, with everything going on, there’ll be no pleas to ‘wake me up when September ends’. Here’s our rundown of simply smashing things to do in London this September.
![a crowd of festival attendees at the Siren Stage at Waterworks 2023](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/09183210/230916_WATERWORKS_2023_RobJones_%40hirobjones_%40khromacollectiveIMG_5531-1024x683.jpeg)
While festival season pretty much draws to a close in August, there are still a few events to enjoy in the city if you love live music. Check out the following festivals to wring the most out of 2026’s summer of fests:
🎶 Waterworks Extended (September 12-13): the cancelled festival will instead take the form of a massive 36-hour-long party at The Cause.
🎵 HowTheLightGetsIn London 2026 (September 19-20): the world’s largest philosophy & music festival.
![people milling about in front of a stage emblazoned with a sign for celebrasia](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/22163650/celebrASIA-at-Battersea-Power-Station-c-Brendan-Bell-2-1024x683.jpg)
Cekebrasia returns this September with an enormous celebration of South East Asia. The FREE-to-visit culture and food festival features a huge range of vendors, attractions, live performances, and activations that celebrate the incredible diversity of food, culture, and creativity across the 11 ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) member countries.
Visitors can expect to find over 35 food and drink vendors, an artisan market with more than 50 traders, live music, craft workshops, cooking classes, and more.
![two people playing in a huge ball pit with dark pink walls at Bubble Planet](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/19172251/Bubble-Planet-16-1024x683.jpg)
Bubble Planet is a wild and wonderful immersive experience that surrounds visitors with a seemingly never-ending world (planet?) of bubbles. As you make your way through themed rooms, you’ll explore fantastical landscapes and even step aboard a hot air balloon flight simulator. It’s a feast for the senses, and a true joy to experience
Celebrate Black culture and creativity
![people milling about trafalgar square on a sunny day at the 'Black on the Square' celebration](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/05130233/BlackOnTheSq_0147MRES-1024x683.jpg)
Black on the Square is a FREE annual event in London’s Trafalgar Square that celebrates and highlights Black culture and creativity. It’s a chance to acknowledge and celebrate “the people and communities who contribute to the capital’s creativity”. All are welcome to enjoy the food, entertainment, workshops, activities, stalls, and more.
Find out more here.
Feast on meat at Meatopia
![a food vendor at meatopia, stood at a stand with a large boat behind them, carving meat to portion into servings for festival attendees](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18102252/September-01-2024-untitled-shootEV1A3198-1024x683.jpg)
Meatopia is a love letter to BBQ, where hungry Londoners can feast on meat to their heart’s content. Going strong since 2013, when it crossed the pond from New York, where the festival was founded, Meatopia offers up 4 days of delicious food from “some of the very best live-fire chefs from UK, Europe and the World”.
Find out more and grab your tickets here.
![London Eye as seen from up high with the House of Parliament and River Thames behind it](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/23095652/London-Eye-Rebrand-Drone-Photography-39-1024x767.jpg)
Think the London Eye is only for tourists? Think again! Many people, even local Londoners, probably don’t know that you can spot some real gems from up there – things you had no idea you could see from the heart of London.
This summer, book yourself a ticket for a ride in one of the capsules and look out for these lesser-known sights, including the centuries-old Cleopatra’s Needle, two hidden rooftop gardens, a couple of castles, and much more.
![The exterior of Senate House (left), the St Pancras clocktower (right)](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/15092417/Copy-of-FACEBOOK-SPLIT-IMAGE-34-1024x576.jpg)
The London Open House Festival returns to London this September, giving us mere mortals the chance to cross the threshold of some of the city’s most exclusive establishments. Hundreds of sites across the city will be throwing open their (usually firmly locked) doors for the occasion, including the likes of:
🏦 OXO Tower
👀 Old Royal Naval College
🏦 English National Ballet
👀 Senate House
🏦 St Pancras Chambers and Clock Tower
👀 BBC Broadcasting House
and many more!
![Sabrage acctress dressed in fancy dress with gloves surrounded by bottles of bubbly](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/30094930/She-doesnt-just-walk-the-walk-she-walks-on-bottles-%F0%9F%8D%BE-Welcome-to-the-stage-Kylie-%F0%9F%A5%82-Sabrage-j-2-1024x802.jpg)
If you’re after a high-octane night out, bouncing over to Sabrage is well-advised. The acclaimed spectacle melds circus and acrobatic skills with a wardrobe of striking outfits and burlesque performance. Grab a cocktail and some southern bar bites and sit back to enjoy the show – it’s only in town for a limited time!
![The Bayeux Tapestry on display at a museum](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/20153925/Bayeux-Tapestry-%C2%A9-Bayeux-Museum-2-min-1024x682.jpg)
The Bayeux Tapestry will return to the UK for the first time in almost 1000 years this September. It’s part of what is expected to be the British Museum’s most popular exhibition ever.
The Bayeux Tapestry is an elaborately embroidered cloth, telling the tale of the Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings. Spanning a whopping 70 metres, it will find a temporary home at the British Museum, courtesy of a loan agreement made with the Bayeux Museum in Normandy.
![Jack White at his art studio ahead of debut exhibition in London](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/17174727/Jack-White-art-studio-1024x683.jpg)
The arrival of the Bayeux Tapestry isn’t the only exciting exhibition coming to London this September. Here are our picks of the best exhibitions to see in London:
💜 Amar Kanwar (September 23, 2026 – January 31, 2027): Serpentine North Gallery – a site-specific installation showcasing Kanwar’s blend of filmmaking, largely exploring the legacies of decolonialisation and the partition of India and Pakistan.
❤️ Marilyn Monroe: A Portrait (Ends September 6): National Portrait Gallery – portraits of the Hollywood icon created by some of the most renowned photographers and artists in the world.
🖤 Modern Toss: “Having an exhibition yeah?” (Ends September 6): The Drawing Room – two decades of work by cartoonists Modern Toss, with 100 pieces, including token-operated swearing machines, big stone heads, large-scale paintings, and more.
🤍 Jack White: THESE THOUGHTS MAY DISAPPEAR (Ends September 13): Newport Street Gallery – Jack White of White Stripes, and, well, Jack White fame, launched his debut visual art exhibition at Damien Hirst’s Newport gallery.
💚 Waldmüller: Landscapes (Ends September 20): The National Gallery – “Discover the breathtaking landscapes of one of Austria’s greatest painters, Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller”
 Trans is Human (Ends September 27): Queer Britain – portraits by renowned photographer Mariano Vivanco that celebrate “thirteen inspiring, familiar and very ordinary transgender people from across the UK.”
 James McNeill Whistler (Ends September 27): Tate Britain – see the infamous ‘Arrangement in Grey and Black No.1’, also known as ‘Whistler’s Mother’ at Europe’s largest retrospective of James McNeill Whistler in 3 decades.
![Various boats moored at a central London marina](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/06101459/PTAIT_20230909_7353-HR-1024x684.jpg)
The Classic Boat Festival returns to St Katharine Docks this September – and it’s completely free to visit! A fleet of beautifully preserved vintage vessels will splash down at central London’s only marina for two days’ worth of maritime merriment. This year, the boats to see and explore include the likes of Dunkirk Little Ships, historic steam tugs, and Thames Sailing Barges.
![a performer leading a parade, twirling brightly coloured cloth around, with an enormous tiger puppet visible in the air behind her](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/03172545/Brick-Lane-Curry-Festival-procession-15_1-1024x683.jpg)
A one-day-only curry festival will fill Brick Lane with flavour, live performances, a parade, giant puppets, and more this September. It’s free to attend, and it’s promising to be “bigger, better and spicier” than before.
Marvel at the Big London Tattoo Show
![a fire performer dancing at the london tattoo show](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/29122113/DSC_2720-1024x731.jpg)
The Big London Tattoo Show returns for its 5th iteration this September – and it’s bigger than ever before. As the UK’s biggest and best tattoo festival, attendees can expect a wealth of artists, demonstrations, live performances and more. The show will feature over 500 artists, live graffiti demonstrations, BMX stunt shows, free fairground rides, and more.
Find out more here.
![Patrick Carney of The Black Keys performs onstage at the 2024 iHeartRadio ALTer EGO Presented by Capital One at the Honda Center on January 13, 2024 in Anaheim, California.](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/05145539/GettyImages-1931289073-1024x683.jpg)
London’s reputation as one of the greatest live music cities in the world is well-earned. From tiny venues showcasing up-and-coming stars to enormous stadium shows, there are countless gigs taking place on any given night in the capital. Here are a few to check out this September:
- The Black Keys (September 1): Brixton Academy
- Geese (September 1-3): Troxy
- The Neighbourhood (September 4): Wembley Arena
- Arijit Singh (September 5): Tottenham Hotspur Stadium
- Hilary Duff (September 10, 15): The O2
- Evanescence (September 13): The O2
- St. Etienne (September 18): The Roundhouse
- Judas Priest (September 21): Hammersmith Apollo
- Death Cab For Cutie (September 25-26): Troxy
- First Aid Kit (September 29): Royal Albert Hall
See a dazzling spectacle on the West End
![text-based poster for RENT the musical with bright neon text](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18162507/RENT-poster-1024x570.jpg)
London is a world-class theatre destination thanks to its iconic West End. Broadway, who? Find out why this city is so famous for its theatrical productions at these shows this September:
NEW OPENINGS
💖 My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?) (September 16 – October 3): Apollo Theatre – “autobiographical story of West End Musical Theatre star and social-media sensation Rob Madge, as they set out to recreate [a homemade childhood Disney] parade.”
🤣 Hay Fever (September 22 – December 12): Wyndham’s Theatre – Christine Baranski makes her West End debut alongside Richard E. Grant in this eternally relatable Noël Coward comedy.
🧚 Into the Woods (Opens September 22): Noël Coward Theatre – classic fairytales collide as this Sondheim and Lapine classic transfers to the West End.
🎸 Rent (September 26, 2026 – March 27, 2027): Duke of Yorks Theatre – the iconic rock-opera-musical from Jonathan Larson returns to the West End, starring Stranger Things’ Gaten Matarazzo.
ENDING SOON
📜 Cyrano de Bergerac (Ends September 5): Noël Coward Theatre – the Royal Shakespeare Company production transfers to the West End following a sold-out run.
💉 Trainspotting the Musical (Ends September 5): Theatre Royal Haymarket – the cult book-turned-film gets the stage musical treatment.
🪄 Now You See Me Live (Ends September 6): London Coliseum – “World-class illusionists unite for a limited London spectacle” inspired by the film of the same name.
🤫 THE TRUTH a comedy by Florian Zeller (Ends September 12): Apollo Theatre – award-winning and -nominated comedy legends helm this play where two couples navigate a web of hidden truths.
🧠 Arcadia (Ends September 12): Duke of York’s Theatre – the same country house sees two similar stories of genius unfolding, separated by two centuries.
📚 Death Note: The Musical (Ends September 12): Barbican – the acclaimed manga gets a hotly-anticipated musical adaptation for just 50 shows.
🥃 Abigail’s Party (Ends September 19): Harold Pinter Theatre – “Tamzin Outhwaite stars as one of the most iconic characters in British theatre – the unforgettable Beverly in Mike Leigh’s ferocious black comedy of suburban life in the 1970s.”
💔 How The Other Half Loves (Ends September 19): The Old Vic – “Three marriages, two homes, and one terrible alibi meet … [this] comedy on sex, class, and domestic partnerships gone wild.”
🎭 The Oresteia (Ends September 19): Bridge Theatre – “A contemporary family wakes up in a Greek myth and can’t seem to find a way out of their hellish destiny.”
🎤 I’m Every Woman – The Chaka Khan Musical (Ends September 27): Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre – Alexander Burke takes on the role of Chaka Khan.
Or explore the city’s boundary-pushing theatre
![actor Josh O’Connor standing on tarmac in a dark, empty scene, bathed in golden light with his eyes closed](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/18171552/GoldenBoy_Artwork_Website-1024x410.jpg)
The West End isn’t all that London’s theatre scene has to offer! Instead, at London’s off-West End shows, you’ll find some ground-breaking, boundary-pushing theatrical art being made. Check out these productions to see the future faces of the theatre world:
🚘 Thelma & Louise: A New Musical (September 3 – October 24): Young Vic (Main House) – the iconic film gets a new musical treatment.
💭 Darkling (September 5 – October 24): Bush Theatre – a young girl in Bhopal, India, in 1984, dreams of more from life as a giant factory rises over her town.
😨 Bigfoot Ripped My Dog In Half I Saw It (September 7 – 26): Soho Theatre – “Two teenagers perform fake Bigfoot sightings in their Appalachian town until a neighbour’s dog turns up torn to pieces.”
🥊 Golden Boy (September 8 – October 31): Almeida Theatre – Emmy and Golden Globe winner Josh O’Connor stars in this revival of Clifford Odets’ “knockout American classic.”
👻 The Turn of the Screw (September 11 – October 10): Arcola Theatre: world premiereof a production based on “the seminal ghost story by Henry James”
🍷 Table 17 (September 17 – October 24): Kiln Theatre – two exes attempt to hash things out after 7 years of not speaking, to find out whether they should give love a second chance.
✍️ Tru (September 19 – November 14): Menier Chocolate Factory – Jesse Tyler Ferguson stars as acclaimed author Truman Capote, alone in his New York apartment after the publication of an excerpt from his tell-all novel Answered Prayers.
Get the pints in for Oktoberfest
![A group of men raising steins of beer at the German Gymnasium in King's Cross, each kitted out in lederhosen and stood behind a table of German delicacies](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/05142340/EV-GermanGym-15Aug23-0788-DB-2-1024x733.jpg)
Despite the name, Oktoberfest traditionally starts in September, not October. Instead, the weeks-long celebration ends in October. Regardless, it’s a spirited celebration of great beer, great food, and great (depending on who you ask) brass bands. Plenty of London venues are honouring the traditional dates with celebrations through September. Head here for pints a-plenty:
🍺 DAS HARVEST FEST at Villages Brewery (September 11 & 12) – while not technically an Oktoberfest event, this celebration of the harvest (and lager) from Hop Burns & Black and Villages is in the same spirit as the other celebrations.
🍻 Albert’s Schloss (September 19 – October 25) – over a month of sudsy Bavaraian celebration and feasting awaits you at this enormous bier palace in the middle of London.
🍺 German Gymnasium (September 18 – October 23) – “Bavarian Spezialitäten, German beers, live Oompah performances and a season of celebrations in the heart of King’s Cross.”
🍻 Bermondsey Bierkellar (September 19 – October 31) – “Bigger. Louder. Unforgettable. London’s wildest Oktoberfest returns.”
7b9a7a67a223b22152fb70f6.summary: London offers a wide variety of events, festivals, and exhibitions throughout September. Highlights include music events like Waterworks Extended and the London Open House Festival, alongside cultural celebrations such as Black on the Square and celebrASIA. Additionally, major exhibitions like the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum and the Classic Boat Festival provide diverse entertainment options for visitors.
key_points: The Bayeux Tapestry returns to the UK for the first time in almost 1,000 years for an exhibition at the British Museum.
The London Open House Festival allows public access to exclusive buildings and historical sites across the city.
Free cultural events like celebrASIA, Black on the Square, and the Classic Boat Festival take place during September.
Numerous live music gigs and festivals are scheduled, including Waterworks Extended and HowTheLightGetsIn London.

0e4c40c16fc5d44d3052f752.title: Thunderstorm warning for UK after record-breaking heatwaves
0e4c40c16fc5d44d3052f752.author: Tom McArdle
0e4c40c16fc5d44d3052f752.content:
![A red brolly](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498838259_17871302700850_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqYP-yEHEhjtPCwS59j6sPb1PAFSRU2fbP_NGNfbzcbEA.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![A red brolly](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498838259_17871302700850_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqYP-yEHEhjtPCwS59j6sPb1PAFSRU2fbP_NGNfbzcbEA.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Thunderstorms are set to strike swathes of Britain after weeks of record-breaking temperatures.
The Met Office issued a yellow warning for thunder and heavy rainfall, covering the East Midlands, the North East, the North West, and Yorkshire and Humber, as well as parts of Wales and Scotland, from 7pm on Wednesday evening until 10am on Thursday morning.
Forecasters said that the stormy weather was likely to trigger travel disruption and flash flooding, as well as damage to homes and power cuts.
The cooler and wetter conditions come after the UK’s fifth heatwave of the summer, during which the hottest day of the year was recorded in Kew Gardens, west London, on Thursday, when temperatures reached 38.1C.
On Wednesday, London experienced substantial rain for the first time in nearly two months.
The Met Office had predicted that parts of the country would experience the “first meaningful rain for a long time” after the record-breaking dry weather left many areas facing water shortages.
Provisional data from the forecaster’s weather tracker showed rain sweeping in from the west before falling in London for several hours in the early hours of Wednesday.
The website showed rain hitting most of the city, where there had been no significant rainfall in some areas for all of July and August.
Weeks of hot, dry weather have led to several hosepipe bans and wildfires. More than 27 million people across England have had hosepipe use restricted.
On Monday, Wessex Water announced a hosepipe ban for the first time since the summer of 1976. The water firm said the temporary prohibition for its 1.4 million customers in Bath, Somerset, Dorset and Wiltshire would come into effect from midnight on Tuesday.
It said its water supply network was facing record demand because of hot conditions and no significant rain forecast.
Five heatwaves have hit Britain this year, with this summer set to beat that of 1976 and become the hottest ever. More than 70 per cent of England is in drought.
Water bosses warned that longer-term forecasts suggested that any respite offered by the rain would not end the widespread restrictions on use, which were based on longer-term forecasts.
On Tuesday, Thames Water told customers to take shorter showers after warning that reservoir levels were lower than usual.
The utility, which has 16 million customers, said its London reservoirs were 74 per cent full at the end of last month. The average at this time of year is 87 per cent.
The heatwaves have increased the water demand. Thames said customers across London and the Thames Valley used around 100 million litres more than normal each day during July’s hot weather.
![Brighton had some long-awaited rain on Wednesday](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498835930_17871302960770_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
![People on a pier in waterproof jackets, with the sea behind](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498835787_17871303717300_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Aidan McGivern, a Met Office meteorologist, said Wednesday would be a “very showery day” across Britain.
He added: “I suspect many people across England and Wales will at least enjoy the feel of some rain falling out of the sky during the next few days, but it’s not going to solve the drought situation overnight because we’re not expecting huge amounts, and it will be highly variable because a lot of it will come in the form of showers.”
On Wednesday, highs of 25C in London, 20C in Cardiff, 19C in Manchester and 16C in Glasgow were expected, according to the weather service.
0e4c40c16fc5d44d3052f752.summary: The Met Office has issued a yellow thunderstorm warning for parts of Britain following weeks of record-breaking heatwaves and dry weather. The incoming stormy weather threatens to cause travel disruption, flash flooding, and power cuts, but is unlikely to immediately resolve ongoing drought and water shortage issues. The recent hot conditions, including the UK's fifth heatwave of the summer, have triggered hosepipe bans affecting over 27 million people across England.
key_points: The Met Office issued a yellow warning for thunder and heavy rainfall across parts of England, Scotland, and Wales.
The UK experienced its fifth heatwave of the summer, with Kew Gardens recording a high of 38.1C.
Weeks of dry weather resulted in hosepipe bans for more than 27 million people across England, including a restriction announced by Wessex Water.
Over 70 per cent of England is currently in drought, and water bosses warned that incoming rain will not immediately end restrictions.
Forecasters predict the stormy weather could cause travel disruption, flash flooding, home damage, and power cuts.

On Wednesday, highs of 25C in London, 20C in Cardiff, 19C in Manchester and 16C in Glasgow were expected, according to the weather service.

The recent hot conditions, including the UK's fifth heatwave of the summer, have triggered hosepipe bans affecting over 27 million people across England.

d3880b72dbd6ad525b60bdec.title: Trump hits pause on Canada tariffs threat, and hints at revival of Keystone XL oil pipeline project
d3880b72dbd6ad525b60bdec.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
d3880b72dbd6ad525b60bdec.content:
Canada has temporarily avoided a bruising 50% US tariff, reaching a Tuesday-evening agreement with Trump administration officials hours before a hike that would have affected $20bn worth of goods was set to take effect.
Donald Trump posted late on Tuesday on social media that he had paused the tariffs for three days “based on the fact that Canada and the USA, subject to the finalization of documents, have a DEAL!”
After Trump’s announcement, Canadian prime minister Mark Carney said “substantial progress” had been made towards a trade deal but more work was needed.
“While we continue this work, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent and more competitive economy at home,” Carney said.
The duties would have affected a range of Canadian exports including wine and hockey sticks.
In the same social media post, Trump said the controversial Keystone XL pipeline project “may be awoken from the grave” without giving further details or suggesting whether it was linked to the tariffs deal.
Keystone XL, which was proposed in 2008 to bring oil from Canada’s western tar sands to US refiners, was halted in 2021 by owner TC Energy after Joe Biden revoked a key permit needed for a US stretch of the 1,200-mile (1,930km) project. It became a flashpoint in US-Canada relations, amid opposition from US landowners, Native American tribes and environmentalists.
North American oil pipelines, including Dakota Access and Enbridge Line 3, have faced steady opposition from environmental groups, amid concerns about spills.
Tuesday’s 11th-hour deal comes amid a contentious past year for the two countries, with the longstanding alliance strained by tit-for-tat tariffs and online broadsides in which Trump has mused about turning Canada into a US state.
In February 2025, the White House hit Canada with a 25% tariff, citing what it regarded as inadequate progress in curbing cross-border illegal immigration and drug trafficking.
In retaliation, Canada announced a reciprocal levy, calling the US’s actions “unwarranted and unreasonable”. The country’s leadership also countered the Trump administration’s claims, maintaining that it had launched a robust border protection plan and that less than 1% of fentanyl and illegal crossings came from Canada.
Tensions flared again in July 2026 when the White House announced the 50% tariffs, saying that it sought to hold Canada accountable for discrimination against US-produced cars, alcohol and dairy products.
In recent days, top officials from the two countries were engaged in “intense and delicate” talks, Carney told reporters on Monday.
Historically, Canada and the US have been strong trading partners. In 2024, trade between the countries was estimated to be roughly $909bn, according to the office of the US trade representative.
The latest proposed US levy has stoked concern about financial devastation and untenable export costs among Canadian business owners, the CBC reported.
Certain goods formerly protected from import taxes under the Trump-negotiated United States-Mexico-Canada (USMCA) deal were not shielded from the latest round of tariffs.
d3880b72dbd6ad525b60bdec.summary: Canada temporarily avoided a 50% US tariff after reaching a preliminary agreement with the Trump administration hours before the duties were set to take effect. Donald Trump announced a three-day pause on the tariffs pending document finalization and also hinted that the halted Keystone XL oil pipeline project might be revived. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted that substantial progress was made toward a trade deal, though additional work remains.

Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that substantial progress was made toward a trade deal.
Donald Trump hinted that the Keystone XL oil pipeline project might be revived.
The avoided tariffs would have affected $20bn worth of Canadian goods, including wine and hockey sticks.

1c5d881e6e23c3a702e4cc8d.title: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and Red Driving School investigated over hidden fees
1c5d881e6e23c3a702e4cc8d.author: Lauren Almeida
1c5d881e6e23c3a702e4cc8d.content:
The UK’s competition watchdog has launched investigations into Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and Red Driving School over concerns that all three companies displayed misleadingly low prices to their customers.
The Competition and Markets Authority’s investigations are part of a broader clampdown on “drip pricing”, an illegal practice that makes a product appear cheaper by not including all mandatory fees.
The regulator said it had opened investigations into the companies amid concerns that customers had not been shown the total price up front when buying train and coach tickets, holidays or driving lessons.
“The first price customers see should be the price they pay,” said Emma Cochrane, the executive director for consumer protection at the CMA. “Clear pricing helps people compare offers confidently and choose the option that works best for them.
“Unexpected mandatory charges make this much harder, which is why the CMA initially put these firms on notice over concerns about their pricing practices and is now opening formal investigations.”
Trainline said in a statement to the stock exchange that it had “proactively engaged with the CMA over several months” and was “taking steps to enhance the presentation of certain fees”. Shares in the business, which is the only one of the three companies that is listed on the stock exchange, fell by as much as 14% in early trading on Wednesday.
Virgin Atlantic said mandatory fees were “indicated at multiple stages” when customers were booking trips but it was reviewing the concerns and would cooperate with the regulator.
Red Driving School said it valued transparency in its customer interactions and was engaging with the CMA.
after newsletter promotion
The CMA’s investigations have been launched using its new consumer protection powers, which were granted last year. These powers allow the regulator to decide whether consumer laws have been broken, rather than having to go through the courts. If the CMA finds there has been an infringement of the law, it can order businesses to pay compensation to affected customers and can fine companies up to 10% of their global turnover.
Earlier this year the CMA ordered the ticket seller StubHub to pay out nearly £1.5m in customer refunds and penalties for drip pricing. It also fined the AA £4.2m and ordered it to repay more than £760,000 to learner drivers over drip pricing.
Andy Burnham has also promised to end “rip-off” business practices. Writing in the Guardian this month, the prime minister said his government would step in wherever it could, as he seeks to put the cost of living at the heart of his premiership.
1c5d881e6e23c3a702e4cc8d.summary: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority has launched formal investigations into Trainline, Virgin Atlantic, and Red Driving School over concerns regarding misleading drip pricing. The watchdog suspects the companies displayed lower initial prices by failing to include mandatory fees upfront. Utilizing new consumer protection powers, the CMA can now fine rule-breaking companies up to 10% of their global turnover and order compensation without going to court.
key_points: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic, and Red Driving School are being investigated for suspected drip pricing.
The practice involves showing misleadingly low initial prices by omitting mandatory fees.
The CMA is using new consumer protection powers that allow it to bypass courts and issue fines.
Companies found in violation can face fines of up to 10% of their global turnover and orders to pay customer compensation.

1749630ee60ff9d57d6cf1e1.title: This fix-it-yourself smartphone is designed to outlast an iPhone – it’s basic but brilliant
1749630ee60ff9d57d6cf1e1.author: Jon Mundy
1749630ee60ff9d57d6cf1e1.content:
The phone’s replaceable battery also comes at a cost. Fairphone has used a small 4,415mAh battery – anything less than 5,000mAh can be considered tiny these days.
If you keep your usage fairly light, then Fairphone’s claim of two-day stamina is achievable. Put it through its paces with regular use, however, and the battery will drop much faster. In my battery test, it lasted for 21 hours and 52 minutes – ten hours shorter than Google’s keenly priced Pixel 10a.
The photos I took failed to excite me, too. Supply plenty of light, and it can capture adequate shots, but they’re not particularly rich with detail. Night shots are poor, with the AI-boosting night mode introducing a lot of grain and noise. The ultrawide camera isn’t too bad, with Fairphone’s image processing occasionally producing pictures with a nicely balanced tone.
Selfies from the front camera are more in line with expectations, with good detail and natural skin tones. 4K resolution video is available, which I would expect from a £600 phone.
It respects your time and your privacy
Fairphone offers a rather confusing choice of software when buying. There’s either Android 16 from Google, or something called “/e/OS” supplied by a company called Murena. The latter is a so-called “de-Googled” software that strips out all the tracking and data collecting you would get from Android.
It’s something I would have liked to have tested, given the novelty of what it promises, but I was sent the Android model for review. There isn’t much to say about this version, as it’s much like the software you’ll find on countless other phones.
1749630ee60ff9d57d6cf1e1.summary: The Fairphone is a fix-it-yourself smartphone priced at £600 that features a replaceable 4,415mAh battery, offering up to two days of light use but falling short under regular demands. Its camera performance is generally underwhelming, producing basic daylight shots, poor night photos, and decent selfies, alongside 4K video capability. Buyers can choose between standard Android 16 software or a privacy-focused, de-Googled operating system called /e/OS supplied by Murena.
key_points: The phone features a small 4,415mAh replaceable battery that lasts for nearly 22 hours of regular use.
Camera quality is mixed, offering adequate daylight photos and good selfies, but poor, grainy low-light shots.
It is available with either standard Android 16 software or a privacy-focused 'de-Googled' operating system called /e/OS from Murena.
The device supports 4K resolution video recording, as expected for a £600 phone.

1eecdad77f7f3bd263ef4d92.title: Christian metal band Demon Hunter sue Netflix over KPop Demon Hunters name
1eecdad77f7f3bd263ef4d92.author: Annabel Rackham
1eecdad77f7f3bd263ef4d92.content:
![Picture of Ryan Clark, who is the lead singer of metal band Demon Hunter. He is crouched on stage wearing a black vest and camouflage trousers and is holding a microphone.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/36a6/live/1eeb64e0-9bc2-11f1-ae8a-8d57110c5ba6.jpg)
Ryan Clark of Demon Hunter on stage at the Louder Than Life Music Festival in 2019
- Published
Christian metal band Demon Hunter are suing Netflix in a trademark lawsuit over the streamer's hit film Kpop Demon Hunters.
The US group, who have been releasing music and touring for 25 years, said Netflix's plan for a global concert tour, along with the movie and merchandise, means there is "almost complete overlap" with their offerings.
Filed on Tuesday by the band's company Hyde Lane, the complaint claims Netflix Studios and live promoter AEG Presents have caused "substantial confusion" among consumers.
They included email evidence from someone who allegedly spent $500 on tickets for a Demon Hunter concert in New York, thinking it was a child-friendly Kpop show for their small children.
![Picture of the animated band HUNTR/X, which is made up of performers Ejae, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami who appear as cartoon characters in matching bolero jackets, A-Line skirts and an assortment of colourful wigs in pink and purple.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/93ba/live/8ddf7b30-9bb7-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Kpop Demon Hunters is Netflix's most-watched original title to date
Other examples cited include a television producer who reportedly contacted the band's management thinking they were related to Kpop Demon Hunters, and social media posts incorrectly tagging Demon Hunter when discussing the film.
The five-piece Seattle band, who play "aggressive yet emotionally stirring heavy metal" according to AllMusic, external, released their 12th album in September 2025 and have 350,000 monthly listeners on Spotify.
By comparison, the KPop Demon Hunters cast have 27 million monthly listeners on the streaming platform.
The legal complaint said: "The brand that Hyde Lane has carefully built over the course of the past quarter century now faces an existential crisis, thereby necessitating the filing of this action and the granting of the requested relief from this Court."
The metal band have asked the court to stop Netflix using the KPop Demon Hunters name for recorded music, live shows and merchandise, and to award unspecified damages.
The band's company registered "Demon Hunter" as a trademark for recorded music and merchandise in 2022, and have applied for a trademark in relation to live music.
Netflix has registered "Kpop Demon Hunters" as a trademark for a number of merchandise uses, with other applications pending.
What started as a 2025 animated film following K-pop girl group Huntr/X, Kpop Demon Hunters has grown into a worldwide phenomenon, with music releases and extensive merchandise, with a global live tour expected to begin in 2027.
It is the most-watched original title in Netflix history and won best animated film and best original song for Golden at the 2026 Golden Globes and Oscars.
A sequel to Kpop Demon Hunters is also in the works, while Netflix is reportedly considering, external other follow-up projects such as a television series and stage musical.
The BBC has contacted Demon Hunter, Netflix and AEG Presents for comment.
1eecdad77f7f3bd263ef4d92.summary: Christian metal band Demon Hunter is suing Netflix and live promoter AEG Presents in a trademark lawsuit over the streamer's hit film Kpop Demon Hunters. Filed by the band's company Hyde Lane, the complaint argues that Netflix's use of the name causes substantial consumer confusion with the band's 25-year-old offerings. The metal group is seeking unspecified damages and an injunction to stop Netflix from using the name for recorded music, live shows, and merchandise.
key_points: Christian metal band Demon Hunter filed a trademark lawsuit against Netflix Studios and AEG Presents.
The lawsuit claims Netflix's 'Kpop Demon Hunters' brand causes substantial consumer confusion with the band.
Demon Hunter's company registered the 'Demon Hunter' trademark for recorded music and merchandise in 2022.
The band is asking the court to stop Netflix from using the name for music, shows, and merchandise, and to award unspecified damages.

91d14db3ef28b24bcd481978.title: Nick Kyrgios provisionally suspended from tennis after testing positive for cocaine
91d14db3ef28b24bcd481978.author: Amy Lofthouse
91d14db3ef28b24bcd481978.content:
![Nick Kyrgios watches on during January's Australian Open](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/9430/live/d82d7ee0-9ba7-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Nick Kyrgios has won one and lost three of his four singles matches this year
- Published
Nick Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended from tennis after testing positive for cocaine.
The Australian submitted a sample during the Mallorca Open on 22 June that was later found to contain benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.
Former world number 13 Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended, external since 4 August.
The International Tennis Integrity Agency said Kyrgios could appeal against the provisional suspension "but has not done so to date".
In a post on Instagram, Kyrgios said he made "a huge mistake" and takes "full responsibility" for it.
Under the suspension, Kyrgios cannot play, coach at or attend Grand Slams or any events sanctioned by the men's and women's tennis tours pending the outcome of a tribunal.
Kyrgios could be banned for up to four years - but if he can prove he took the drug outside of a competition, the maximum ban he would face is three months.
The 31-year-old has played just four singles matches this season, having struggled with knee and wrist injuries in recent years.
He last played in the men's doubles at Wimbledon, where he and partner Alexander Bublik lost in the first round.
In a lengthy statement on Instagram, Kyrgios said the last few years of injuries had taken "a huge toll on me, both mentally and physically".
"My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do," he wrote.
"Coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.
"None of that excuses what I did."
Kyrgios said he would be stepping away from social media and public life for the next 28 days to "focus on getting myself right".
Cocaine is classified as a stimulant and substance of abuse on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list.
Reduced sanctions apply for athletes who test positive for the substance out of competition.
However, Kyrgios' sample was submitted during a tournament in which he played singles, ultimately losing in the first round to Adam Walton.
"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me," Kyrgios added.
"Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself."
Kyrgios has long been a controversial figure in tennis.
His behaviour on court has been widely criticised and he has been given numerous large fines for smashing racquets, making audible obscenities and arguing with the umpire.
In 2023, he admitted assaulting an ex-girlfriend two years earlier. He avoided a criminal conviction.
He was criticised further for making a series of comments which have been considered misogynistic.
In 2024 he shared a post from controversial influencer Andrew Tate. He later said he had gone "to all lengths" to distance himself from the self-proclaimed misogynist.
Kyrgios was also critical of the handling of two high-profile anti-doping cases involving top players Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek, calling them "disgusting" for tennis.
Kyrgios has won seven ATP Tour singles titles and reached the Wimbledon final in 2022, losing in four sets to Novak Djokovic.
He and compatriot Thanasi Kokkinakis won the Australian Open men's doubles title together in 2022.
Kyrgios has also spoken about his struggles with mental health, saying he "genuinely contemplated" suicide and spent time in a psychiatric hospital in London after losing at Wimbledon in 2019.

12d55741927484f274b7a94f.title: Astronomers discover a giant, rocky 'mega-Earth' 23 times more massive than our planet
12d55741927484f274b7a94f.author: Samantha Mathewson
12d55741927484f274b7a94f.content:
![A small Earth is illustrated next to a large blue world.](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/qnXj4xKhNsjzUZs5FLDy2M.jpg) 
Astronomers have discovered an unusually massive, dense exoplanet that challenges conventional ideas about how rocky planets form.
Called GJ 523b, the exoplanet is about 2.5 times wider than Earth but packs roughly 23 times our planet's mass into that relatively compact size. Worlds this large and dense are sometimes referred to as "mega-Earths," an informal term for unusually massive, predominantly rocky planets. GJ 523b's high density suggests it contains relatively little atmosphere despite being large enough that astronomers would normally expect it to have accumulated a substantial gaseous envelope, according to a statement from the University of Wisconsin–Madison.
"This isn't what we expected at all," Max Kroft, lead author of the study, said in the statement. "Dense planets like this aren't uncommon, but they're usually small rocky planets similar to Earth or Mercury. This planet is two and a half times bigger than the Earth."
GJ 523b was initially identified as a candidate by NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), which searches for periodic dips in starlight caused when planets cross, or transit, their host stars. Researchers followed up with observations from the ground-based WIYN 3.5-meter Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona, using a spectrograph to measure the planet's gravitational tug on its star.
Combining those observations, the team calculated that GJ 523b has a mass about 23.5 times that of Earth, a radius 2.55 times larger and a density of about 126.82 grams per cubic inch. It circles its star every 17.75 days. The planetary system is also relatively young, at an estimated nearly 170 million years old, according to the study.
That combination of size, mass and youth poses a puzzle for planet formation models. Planets begin by building cores of rock and metal, which can then pull in hydrogen and helium from the disk of gas and dust surrounding a young star. In our own solar system, giant planets such as Jupiter and Saturn are thought to have begun rapidly accumulating their massive gaseous envelopes once their growing cores reached roughly 20 times Earth's mass.
GJ 523b is already about 23 times Earth's mass, putting it beyond that threshold. Yet instead of developing into a gas-rich world, its unusually high density suggests it has relatively little gas and remains predominantly rocky — raising the question of why it followed such a different path.
"The question is, why didn't this planet do that, if it's 20 times the size of Earth?" Kroft said in the statement.
One possibility is that GJ 523b initially formed with a thick atmosphere that was later stripped away. Another is that it formed through a collision between two planets, creating a larger rocky world while blasting much of their gaseous envelopes into space, according to the statement.
Astronomers have used the term "mega-Earth" for more than a decade to describe exceptionally massive rocky worlds, though it has never represented a formally established class of exoplanets. Finding more examples like GJ 523b could help reveal whether these unusual worlds are rare exceptions or part of a broader population.
"It's hard to infer things about planet formation in general from a sample size of one," Kroft said in the statement. "We're not going to get to 10,000 of these overdense planets, but if we can get to 20 or 30, maybe some trends might pop out."
The findings have been submitted to The Astronomical Journal and are currently available on the preprint server arXiv and have not yet been peer reviewed.

47dd9394f412cab574a0ff20.title: Deaf patient given wrong jab due to sign language error, report says
47dd9394f412cab574a0ff20.author: Beth Rose; Emma Tracey
47dd9394f412cab574a0ff20.content:
![Close-up of a person receiving an injection in the upper arm, with a healthcare worker holding a syringe and supporting the arm. The image focuses on the vaccination procedure in a clinical setting, with the background softly blurred.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/a8a3/live/e8eb51e0-9b24-11f1-9a2c-6d6ac3827d20.jpg)
- Published
A deaf woman was given the wrong vaccine because she was not provided with a British Sign Language (BSL) interpreter at her doctor's surgery, a report says.
The Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman (PHSO) said disabled people were being let down by inaccessible communications.
It said the patient, Samantha, had booked a flu jab but was instead given a Covid vaccine after staff failed to show her a BSL video which would have highlighted the error. She said the experience had had a "profound impact" on her.
The Department of Health and Social Care said the "deeply upsetting stories" were "completely unacceptable" and NHS and social care organisations had a duty to make services accessible.
The PHSO investigates complaints about UK government departments, public organisations and the NHS in England.
It said public services were legally required to support people with their accessible communication needs, which might be due to a disability, neurodivergence or English not being their first language.
Samantha had booked her flu and Covid jabs for separate weeks and showed a nurse a note on her phone which said she was there for the "flu jab only", the PHSO said.
Despite that, the practice said it believed it had correctly established Samantha wanted the Covid vaccine and had got her consent through her grandmother, even though she had early-stage dementia and was not in the treatment room.
Following an investigation, the PHSO recommended the surgery should apologise and pay Samantha Â£450. It has also since signed a contract with a sign language interpreting company.
The NHS Northamptonshire Integrated Care Board said it was "very sorry" about Samantha's experience, and that it expected practices to make "reasonable adjustments to support effective communication".
The PHSO said it had found disabled people risked not getting vital information about their healthcare, finances or employment because of a lack of accessible formats such as large print or audio materials.
Since April 2020, it said it had concluded 623 investigations related to reasonable adjustments, of which 496 were upheld or partly upheld.
The report also highlighted the case of Alan Graham, who was deaf and was being treated for heart failure at University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Trust.
When an interpreter was not available, hospital staff asked his teenage grandson to interpret for the family and tell Graham's deaf daughter that he might die.
![Alan Graham pictured holding a fish. He is wearing a khaki hat and fisherman's jacket. He has a grey beard and wears circular silver framed glasses](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/062f/live/0a9fb2e0-9b16-11f1-b792-a710e56a11dc.jpg)
Alan Graham was being treated for cancer in Birmingham when his grandson was asked to interpret serious news to the family
Following an ombudsman investigation, the trust apologised and said "we did not get things right".
They said new measures had been introduced to help deaf patients, including strengthening awareness and accessibility arrangements to ensure patients' communication needs were better met.
"We remain committed to learning from this and to providing inclusive, compassionate care for all our patients," they said.
Following the report by the ombudsman, NHS England said it was "completely unacceptable for those who are deaf or have visual loss to face barriers to accessing or understanding the healthcare they need".
It added it had recently refreshed its standards setting out how services should provide safe and effective care for those with communication needs.
The PHSO said that while it was not a regulator, it could order public organisations to pay financial compensation if it upheld a complaint.
Rebecca Hilsenrath, its chief executive, said: "When people feel they are not listened to and that their needs are not met, they lose trust in the very services designed to support them."
In its report, the PHSO highlighted North Cheshire and Mersey NHS Foundation Trust as a good example of providing effective communication, after it worked with local advocacy groups and deaf people to improve its service for deaf patients who reported feeling excluded.
The trust has provided guides for patients on how to access interpreting and translation services, increasing the use of interpreters by 50% in one year.
47dd9394f412cab574a0ff20.summary: A Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman report revealed that a deaf woman named Samantha was given the wrong vaccine after being denied a British Sign Language interpreter at her surgery. The report highlighted multiple cases where disabled patients faced inaccessible communications, including a hospital asking a teenager to interpret his grandfather's critical medical news. The ombudsman recommended apologies and compensation in the investigated cases, prompting calls from health authorities for better accessibility and reasonable adjustments.
key_points: A deaf patient booked a flu jab but received a Covid vaccine instead due to a lack of a BSL interpreter.
The PHSO report found disabled people are frequently let down by inaccessible communications in public services.
In another highlighted case, a deaf patient's teenage grandson was asked to interpret critical end-of-life information.
The surgery involved in Samantha's case was recommended to apologize and pay £450, and has since hired a sign language interpreting company.

728a994c0440beada77a106f.title: Zendaya And Tom Holland Just Revealed Their Favourite London Restaurants
728a994c0440beada77a106f.author: Amelia Morgan
728a994c0440beada77a106f.content:
![](https://www.thehandbook.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1920,height=1120,fit=cover,q=80,format=webp/https://files.thehandbook.com/uploads/2026/08/zendaya-1.jpg)
Hollywood’s favourite couple has officially spoken. According to appetiteapp.uk, these are Zendaya and Tom Holland‘s go-to London restaurants, and the list doesn’t hold back. From must-try Indian spots to cult-favourite pubs, here’s where the couple actually eats.
Jamavar
Jamavar in Mayfair is the Michelin-starred jewel of London’s Indian dining scene, with dishes drawing on royal Mughal cooking as well as coastal South Indian flavours. Think slow-cooked biryanis and tandoor classics alongside coconut and curry-leaf specialities from Kerala. Led by chef Surender Mohan, it’s the kind of grand, palace-inspired spot that suits a date night as much as a celebration.
Where: 8 Mount St, London W1K 3NF
Website: www.jamavar.com
![](https://files.thehandbook.com/uploads/2026/08/jamavar-onam-4-1-scaled.jpg)
The Devonshire
The Devonshire on Denman Street is Soho’s ultimate two-in-one: a proper, no-frills pub downstairs with a legendary pint of Guinness, and a wood ember grill restaurant upstairs serving dry-aged Scottish beef, langoustines and hand-dived scallops. It’s the rare spot that works equally well for a casual pint or a full-blown special-occasion dinner.

e554c3b4238cffa0a48fc5c7.title: Train investigators find track defect on approach to site of Lewes derailment, initial report says
e554c3b4238cffa0a48fc5c7.author: Live Reporting Edited by Neil Connor
e554c3b4238cffa0a48fc5c7.content:
![A shot of the train tracks, and one section is slightly bent. There is a white square around this section to more clearly point it out.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/8/19/ebb9f385-7bdb-4770-bc7f-ee79af8231a5.jpg.webp)
A track "irregularity" has been found on the rails where a train came off the tracks in Lewes last week, investigators have said.
The Rail Accident Investigation Branch has released its initial report, external into the derailment which took place on Thursday 13 August, the hottest day of the year. The derailment threw three carriages off the track and onto their side, injuring 30 people, two of whom are still in hospital.
Investigators said there was evidence of previous "track maintenance activity" in the area and there had been several reports of "rough riding" from passengers on other trains in the same location.
In a joint statement after the report was released, Lucy McAuliffe, Network Rail's route director for Sussex, and John Whitehurst, chief executive of Greater Thameslink Railway, said they were "very sorry that this happened on our railway" and promised to "carefully consider any recommendations arising from the investigation".
The next steps of the investigation will look at how the track was inspected and maintained, and the effectiveness of any measures designed to address risks of operating trains in hot weather.
We're closing our coverage but you can read our full report here.

29e90f4cf6e1ce11f39437df.title: Israel confirms it opened fire on vehicle carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza
29e90f4cf6e1ce11f39437df.author: Yolande Knell
29e90f4cf6e1ce11f39437df.content:
![Hind Rajab smiles at the camera.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/755/cpsprodpb/a318/live/339ec150-9bc9-11f1-98c6-93bfcdb08681.jpg)
- Published
The Israeli military has confirmed for the first time that it opened fire on a vehicle carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six members of her family in Gaza City during the war in Gaza.
The Palestinian child initially survived the attack in January 2024 that killed several family members, but her body was recovered days later along with her relatives.
After the attack, Hind managed to answer a telephone call from the Palestinian Red Crescent Society, which lasted hours. An ambulance it sent to reach her â in a move coordinated with the Israeli army - was then shelled, killing two paramedics.
In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that following a review it would be opening a criminal investigation.
"Due to alleged failures in the coordination of the movement of the Palestine Red Crescent ambulance, it has been decided to initiate a criminal investigation of the incident by Military Police Criminal Investigation Division", it said.
The IDF initially stated that none of its troops were in the area at the time of Hind's killing. However, that suggestion was soon questioned.
The IDF later said it had "conducted raids on terror targets" with forces operating in neighbourhoods in Gaza City, including Tel al-Hawa, where Hind was located.
Hind's killing was internationally condemned after a desperate recording of her speaking to paramedics was broadcast around the world.
She and her family were trying to flee the Israeli invasion of their neighbourhood in Gaza City, when their vehicle came under Israeli fire.
Hind's pleas for someone to rescue her ended when the phone line was cut amid the sound of more gunfire.
The story was made into an Oscar-nominated film called The Voice of Hind Rajab.
The UN cited her case in a commission of inquiry, accusing Israel of war crimes, which it denies.
Aside from the criminal investigation into Hind and her family, the IDF also said it would investigate the killing of 15 Palestinians, including medics and a UN worker near Rafah in southern Gaza last year.
In three other cases, involving the killing of seven World Central Kitchen employees in Deir al-Balah two years ago, and four employees of MÃ©decins Sans FrontiÃ¨res (MSF), who were killed in two incidents, the IDF said it had not found grounds for criminal investigations.
The IDF is under pressure to show it investigates itself to try to stave off international legal action, most notably from the International Criminal Court.
It aims to counter accusations that it has committed war crimes and that there is impunity for its forces.
Correction: The initial version of this story and breaking news notification said Hind Rajab was aged six. The copy was updated after it was later confirmed she was aged five

Although Hind initially survived the shooting, she and an ambulance sent to rescue her by the Palestinian Red Crescent Society were subsequently killed. Following a review, the Israel Defense Forces announced it is opening a criminal investigation into the incident.
key_points: The IDF confirmed it fired on the vehicle carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and her family.
An ambulance sent to rescue Hind was shelled, resulting in the deaths of two paramedics.
The IDF announced a criminal investigation will be conducted by the Military Police Criminal Investigation Division.
The UN previously cited Hind's case in a commission of inquiry, accusing Israel of war crimes.
