4caa94c34fb53e1c22031948.title: National Lottery replaces chief executive to drive turnaround
4caa94c34fb53e1c22031948.author: James Warrington
4caa94c34fb53e1c22031948.content:
![Andria Vidler](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498837750_17871293516130_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Andria Vidler](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498837750_17871293516130_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
The National Lottery is to replace its chief executive in an effort to draw a line under a catalogue of technical troubles and missed growth targets.
Andria Vidler, the chief executive of Allwyn UK, will leave next month after almost three years in the role. She will be replaced on an interim basis by Phil Walker, a former William Hill executive.
Ms Vidler, a veteran media executive who previously led record label EMI and publisher Centaur Media, took up the role at Allwyn in October 2023, shortly before the start of its 10-year licence to run the National Lottery.
Allwyn, which is controlled by Karel Komárek, the Czech billionaire, emerged victorious in a fierce competition to win the licence, ending three decades of control by previous operator Camelot.
He successfully runs lotteries around the world and has pledged to invest in and modernise Britain’s prize draw.
Allwyn swept in with a promise to boost money for charitable donations from almost £18bn to £38bn – equivalent to £3.8bn a year – over the coming decade.
But its handling of the National Lottery has been hampered by a number of setbacks, including delays to a major upgrade of ageing IT systems.
Allwyn has also been tied up by a lengthy legal battle between Richard Desmond and the Gambling Commission. The controversial entrepreneur sued for £1.3bn over the regulator’s decision not to award him the lottery licence.
A High Court judge comprehensively dismissed the claim in April, leaving Mr Desmond on the hook for around £70m in legal fees.
However, the wrangling has been a significant factor in the National Lottery so far falling short of its pledges on good causes under Allwyn.
The Telegraph revealed last month that Lisa Nandy, the Culture Secretary, had named the National Lottery among a number of proposed targets for nationalisation under Andy Burnham.
Ministers have also launched the first review of how the money from National Lottery ticket sales is spent in more than two decades as Ms Nandy said the model was “showing its age”.
The appointment of Mr Walker as interim chief executive will equip Allwyn with more direct experience of the gambling sector.
![Phil Walker](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498837579_17871292985150_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqskTk5DlCpGZkDMRo1CxemHdR78eTBj0hwdfFRfV9oOU.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
He has held a number of senior roles at William Hill over the past six years, including as managing director for UK and Ireland.
Allwyn has also launched the search for a permanent successor to Ms Vidler, who will remain at the company in an advisory capacity until the end of October.
Justin King, the Allwyn UK chairman, said: “Since Andria joined us, she has led from the front through an intense period of change, helping to complete the much-needed and long-overdue transformation of The National Lottery.
“With the major transition milestones delivered, now is the right time to look to the future and build on the solid foundations that have been laid.”
4caa94c34fb53e1c22031948.summary: The National Lottery's operator Allwyn is replacing chief executive Andria Vidler with former William Hill executive Phil Walker on an interim basis next month. The leadership change comes in an effort to drive a turnaround following technical troubles, legal battles, and missed growth targets under Vidler's tenure. Vidler will remain in an advisory capacity until the end of October while Allwyn searches for a permanent successor.
key_points: Andria Vidler is stepping down as chief executive of Allwyn UK after nearly three years in the role.
Phil Walker, a former William Hill executive, will take over as interim chief executive next month.
The leadership shake-up follows technical troubles, delayed IT upgrades, and missed growth targets for charitable donations.
Allwyn is also searching for a permanent successor while Vidler stays on in an advisory capacity until the end of October.

f3c7fd7e0a9a1d73d77fead6.title: Hogging weights, loud grunting and sweaty benches: 11 gym dos and don’ts from fitness experts
f3c7fd7e0a9a1d73d77fead6.author: Madeleine Aggeler
f3c7fd7e0a9a1d73d77fead6.content:
I like to think of myself as a fairly laid-back person. Other people’s behavior is not my business. There is one notable exception: my gym nemesis.
He brings his computer to the gym and takes work conference calls at full volume. He has four to six pairs of dumbbells around him at all times – then doesn’t put them away. Intellectually I understand he is a fragile, flawed human like the rest of us, but in my gut I sometimes wonder if he arrived here from another galaxy.
Life is full of unspoken rules, and the gym is no different. The heavy weights, sweaty people and mysterious machines can make it daunting to figure out how to behave. So we asked fitness experts for their thoughts on gym etiquette – their biggest pet peeves as well as the behaviors that might seem intimidating, but are actually fine.
Good gym etiquette is less about following a long list of rules than it is simple respect, says Mathew Forzaglia, a fitness professional and educator. “Respect the equipment, respect other people’s time and space, and respect the shared environment,” he says.
Gym no-nos
Don’t leave a mess
Whether it’s leaving a bench covered in your sweat, or not re-racking weights after you use them, failing to clean and reset equipment after you use it is not only a hygiene issue, it’s potentially unsafe.
Leaving out heavy plates or dumbbells “creates an accessibility issue for people who physically can’t move the weight someone else abandoned”, says Amanda Katz, a New York City-based personal trainer and run coach.
As for wiping off your sweat, “it’s common courtesy and takes just a few seconds”, says Forzaglia. “No one wants to lie down on a bench covered in someone else’s sweat.”
Don’t hoard equipment
If you’re planning to do a complex circuit training routine that involves having access to six machines at once, save it for a home workout or tweak it to be more sequential.
“You can’t claim the cable machine and the leg press and three sets of dumbbells,” says Laura Girard, certified personal trainer, strength coach and founder of The Energy Academy in New York City. “Learn to share.”
Don’t offer unsolicited advice
It can feel intoxicating to think you know better than others. Spot someone across the gym doing deadlifts with what you think is bad form, and it might be tempting to go over and give them a few tips. Don’t.
“Unless someone is in immediate danger, I don’t think it’s appropriate to offer coaching to strangers,” says Katz. Most of us are not fitness professionals, and even if we are, we don’t know why someone might be training the way they are. “There are countless reasons an exercise might look different than expected – from injury rehabilitation to a coach’s programming,” says Katz.
Other people’s bodies and how they train them are not your business. “Never assume you know somebody’s goals or body better than they do,” says Girard.
Don’t be loud
Whether it’s playing your pump-up playlist sans headphones, grunting loudly through exercises – or, as I encountered in my gym just the other week, a man shouting “LET’S GO!” before every set of shoulder shrugs – being loud is not fair or pleasant for your fellow gym-goer.
“Everyone deserves their own playlist and to not have their nervous system frayed by a random shout when they’re already doing something vulnerable and uncomfortable,” says Girard.
Don’t scroll or talk on your phone
Resting between sets is normal and fine – more on this later. But monopolizing a machine because you’re scrolling social media, answering emails or taking calls is not.
“The gym is for training,” says Forzaglia. “If you need to catch up on your phone, step outside for a minute.”
Don’t show up late to a group class
“I understand that life happens and sometimes you’re running late,” says Jessie Diaz-Herrera, co-founder and fitness instructor at Power Plus Wellness in New York City. But walking into a class 15 or 20 minutes late can be extremely disruptive to other participants, and potentially present a safety issue “if the instructor has already gone through the warm-up or explained the movements”, she says.
Gym OKs
Do talk to people
While unsolicited advice is never welcome, this doesn’t mean you have to completely ignore other people at the gym.
after newsletter promotion
“Most people at the gym are either also new, or love the gym and would be happy to chat your ear off,” says Girard. As long as you don’t interrupt someone in the middle of a set, Girard says it’s “totally OK to approach for a quick form check or help with equipment”. (But wait for a go-ahead or an invitation from them to strike up a longer conversation.)
It’s also fine to politely ask someone how many sets they have left, or if you can work in between their sets, says Forzaglia.
“Most experienced gym-goers appreciate respectful communication,” he says. “I’d much rather someone ask than stand around waiting or skip an exercise because they felt uncomfortable speaking up.”
Do rest between sets
Although you shouldn’t disappear into your phone for long stretches, resting on or around equipment for a minute or two between sets of exercise is normal and expected.
“Rest is part of strength training and Hiit protocols, and most people understand that,” says Katz. “You don’t need to rush through your workout to look like you belong or keep your heart rate up unless it’s the intention of the session.”
Do use whatever equipment you need
There is no hierarchy that gives one gym member a greater right to equipment than another, whether in terms of experience or ability.
“You are no less deserving of a squat rack because you’re only squatting the bar,” says Girard.
Be a good neighbor and share space and equipment, Girard says, but don’t shut yourself out because you don’t think you’re advanced enough.
Do record yourself if you want to
Recording your workout is not inherently rude, says Diaz-Herrera. “A lot of people use videos to check their form, track their progress or create content,” she says. The important thing is to not intentionally film others.
If you think you might be in someone’s video and don’t want to be, Diaz-Herrera says it’s absolutely OK to ask whether you appear in frame, and if they mind moving the camera or cropping you out. “That’s not being difficult or making a big deal out of it,” she says. “It’s just communicating and respecting each other’s space.”
Do change gyms if you need to
If you don’t feel comfortable in a particular gym or fitness class, find another one.
“Remember not every space is the right fit and that’s OK,” says Katz. “A welcoming environment can make all the difference, so give yourself an opportunity to try another gym, class or community until you find one where you feel supported.”
And if the gym in general isn’t for you, that’s also fine.
“You don’t need to go to the gym to make fitness part of your life,” says Girard. “The gym is just a space where equipment lives, and it’s totally optional.”
f3c7fd7e0a9a1d73d77fead6.summary: Fitness experts share essential guidelines on gym etiquette, emphasizing that good behavior comes down to simple respect for shared space, time, and equipment. The advice outlines clear boundaries on what to avoid, such as hoarding weights, leaving messes, and making excessive noise, while also validating normal behaviors like resting between sets and recording workouts for form checks.
key_points: Always clean up your sweat and re-rack weights to maintain hygiene and safety.
Do not hoard multiple machines or sets of dumbbells for circuit training.
Avoid offering unsolicited advice or coaching to strangers.
Keep noise levels down and do not take phone calls or scroll excessively on machines.
It is acceptable to rest between sets, chat respectfully, and record your workout as long as you do not film others.

“You can’t claim the cable machine and the leg press and three sets of dumbbells,” says Laura Girard, certified personal trainer, strength coach and founder of The Energy Academy in New York City. “Learn to share.”
Don’t offer unsolicited advice
It can feel intoxicating to think you know better than others. Spot someone across the gym doing deadlifts with what you think is bad form, and it might be tempting to go over and give them a few tips. Don’t.
“Unless someone is in immediate danger, I don’t think it’s appropriate to offer coaching to strangers,” says Katz. Most of us are not fitness professionals, and even if we are, we don’t know why someone might be training the way they are. “There are countless reasons an exercise might look different than expected – from injury rehabilitation to a coach’s programming,” says Katz.
Other people’s bodies and how they train them are not your business. “Never assume you know somebody’s goals or body better than they do,” says Girard.
Don’t be loud
Whether it’s playing your pump-up playlist sans headphones, grunting loudly through exercises – or, as I encountered in my gym just the other week, a man shouting “LET’S GO!” before every set of shoulder shrugs – being loud is not fair or pleasant for your fellow gym-goer.
“Everyone deserves their own playlist and to not have their nervous system frayed by a random shout when they’re already doing something vulnerable and uncomfortable,” says Girard.
Don’t scroll or talk on your phone
Resting between sets is normal and fine – more on this later. But monopolizing a machine because you’re scrolling social media, answering emails or taking calls is not.
“The gym is for training,” says Forzaglia. “If you need to catch up on your phone, step outside for a minute.”
Don’t show up late to a group class
“I understand that life happens and sometimes you’re running late,” says Jessie Diaz-Herrera, co-founder and fitness instructor at Power Plus Wellness in New York City. But walking into a class 15 or 20 minutes late can be extremely disruptive to other participants, and potentially present a safety issue “if the instructor has already gone through the warm-up or explained the movements”, she says.
Gym OKs
Do talk to people
While unsolicited advice is never welcome, this doesn’t mean you have to completely ignore other people at the gym.
after newsletter promotion
“Most people at the gym are either also new, or love the gym and would be happy to chat your ear off,” says Girard. As long as you don’t interrupt someone in the middle of a set, Girard says it’s “totally OK to approach for a quick form check or help with equipment”. (But wait for a go-ahead or an invitation from them to strike up a longer conversation.)
It’s also fine to politely ask someone how many sets they have left, or if you can work in between their sets, says Forzaglia.
“Most experienced gym-goers appreciate respectful communication,” he says. “I’d much rather someone ask than stand around waiting or skip an exercise because they felt uncomfortable speaking up.”
Do rest between sets
Although you shouldn’t disappear into your phone for long stretches, resting on or around equipment for a minute or two between sets of exercise is normal and expected.
“Rest is part of strength training and Hiit protocols, and most people understand that,” says Katz. “You don’t need to rush through your workout to look like you belong or keep your heart rate up unless it’s the intention of the session.”
Do use whatever equipment you need
There is no hierarchy that gives one gym member a greater right to equipment than another, whether in terms of experience or ability.
“You are no less deserving of a squat rack because you’re only squatting the bar,” says Girard.
Be a good neighbor and share space and equipment, Girard says, but don’t shut yourself out because you don’t think you’re advanced enough.
Do record yourself if you want to
Recording your workout is not inherently rude, says Diaz-Herrera. “A lot of people use videos to check their form, track their progress or create content,” she says. The important thing is to not intentionally film others.
If you think you might be in someone’s video and don’t want to be, Diaz-Herrera says it’s absolutely OK to ask whether you appear in frame, and if they mind moving the camera or cropping you out. “That’s not being difficult or making a big deal out of it,” she says. “It’s just communicating and respecting each other’s space.”
Do change gyms if you need to
If you don’t feel comfortable in a particular gym or fitness class, find another one.
“Remember not every space is the right fit and that’s OK,” says Katz. “A welcoming environment can make all the difference, so give yourself an opportunity to try another gym, class or community until you find one where you feel supported.”
And if the gym in general isn’t for you, that’s also fine.
“You don’t need to go to the gym to make fitness part of your life,” says Girard. “The gym is just a space where equipment lives, and it’s totally optional.”

The advice outlines clear boundaries on what to avoid, such as hoarding weights, leaving messes, and making excessive noise, while also validating normal behaviors like resting between sets and recording workouts for form checks.
key_points: Always clean up your sweat and re-rack weights to maintain hygiene and safety.
Do not hoard multiple machines or sets of dumbbells for circuit training.
Avoid offering unsolicited advice or coaching to strangers.
Keep noise levels down and do not take phone calls or scroll excessively on machines.
It is acceptable to rest between sets, chat respectfully, and record your workout as long as you do not film others.

26490674d1389b5e629ce311.title: Frank Beard was the enigma at the heart of ZZ Top.
26490674d1389b5e629ce311.author: David Sinclair
26490674d1389b5e629ce311.content:
![ZZ Top’s Frank Beard posing for a photograph in the 1980s](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pfWUtmubJ7sf6SJ3GqyH8m.jpg) 
Frank Beard, who has died at the age of 77, spent much of his life sitting slightly apart from the mythology of ZZ Top. While Billy Gibbons and Dusty Hill transformed themselves into a pair of synchronised Texan mystics in shades, Stetsons and chest-length facial hair, Beard remained the odd one out at the back of the stage; headphones on, expression unreadable, laying down the immense, disciplined grooves that helped drive ZZ Top from hard-touring blues boogie trio to one of the most distinctive arena bands of the MTV era.
“I’m a seventh-generation Texan,” Beard said in the documentary That Little Ol’ Band From Texas. “I know that my father’s family came into Texas in 1836. I know that my grandmother, Bessie Dossett, walked behind a covered wagon in 1899 from Louisiana.”
That sense of lineage and place runs deep through ZZ Top. Beard grew up around Dallas and Fort Worth immersed in a working-class culture of blues, country, hot rods, beer joints and border-radio R&B. While still in his teens, he was playing clubs and frat parties when Dusty Hill and his big brother Rocky recruited him into their group, The Warlocks, later renamed American Blues. Long hair alone could provoke hostility in Texas at the time. They responded by dyeing their long hair blue.
 ![ZZ Top’s Frank Beard performing onstage in 1974](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TBb5WQJE6WmV7nziY4Cm7m.jpg) 
Speaking to Beard in person could be a pretty disorientating experience. He talked in a thick Texas drawl that could turn a simple sentence into slow-moving tar. The listener would also try to decode the dry humour, the deadpan timing and the absence of visible emotion behind it all.
While Gibbons projected mystical showmanship and Hill provided warmth and mischief, Beard came across as the band’s hardest member to read: laconic, watchful and faintly intimidating. In conversation, he made Lou Reed seem effusive.
ZZ Top’s longevity has obscured how hard-living the tres hombres really were in the 1970s and early 1980s. The trio emerged from the same broad culture that produced outlaw country, Southern rock excess, biker culture, psychedelia and serious narcotics consumption. Beard embodied all of that a lot more deeply than the latter-day cartoon version of the band suggests
“The first time I ever did any drug at all was [when] I injected LSD, and boy, I liked it,” Beard recalled much later. “I was looking for God. I became a seeker of truth. Then the pills came about just from the workload. And the heroin came about because I liked it. It’s a vacation of the mind. I liked it a lot.”
Sign up below to get the latest from Classic Rock, plus exclusive special offers, direct to your inbox!
When ZZ Top disappeared from the road for a couple of years after the Worldwide Texas Tour in 1977, Beard was largely the (unspoken) reason.
“I knew that I needed to kick heroin, I needed to stop doing cocaine. I had done it all, and I couldn’t go any further. So I went to a 12-step programme. I just wanted to get sober. I wanted to be like people I admired that could sit home and watch TV and go to bed, and that was, you know, OK [for them].”
![ZZ Top - La Grange (From](https://img.youtube.com/vi/9zKVnpUIJPY/maxresdefault.jpg) 
Sobriety coincided with the start of ZZ Top’s remarkable reinvention. As they emerged into the 1980s, songs such as Manic Mechanic (from Degüello) and Heaven, Hell Or Houston (from El Loco) took the band into a world of eccentric time changes and quirky special effects far removed from their blues roots.
By the mid-1980s Beard had become something close to ZZ Top’s internal clockwork mechanism. Wearing headphones onstage and locking himself to click tracks with near-military discipline, he anchored the band’s transformation from gritty Texas blues-boogie trio into a streamlined piece of rock futurism.
Gibbons likes to joke that Beard was listening to the football scores through the headphones. In reality, he was performing a far stranger role: human metronome, machine whisperer, the iron controller of momentum as they made the leap into the sleek MTV-era machine.
Songs such as Gimme All Your Lovin’, Legs and Velcro Fly fuse an R&B groove with electronic textures and mechanised precision, while Beard’s playing retained the heavy undertow of Southern blues beneath the modern production sheen.
His drumming remained rooted in the classic Texas shuffle, a deceptively subtle style in which the left hand carries a rolling triplet figure across the snare while the right maintains a steady pulse on cymbal or hi-hat. It requires looseness and absolute precision at the same time. ZZ Top’s grooves swing hard, but they never drift.
Beard understood how to generate impetus without losing control, whether underpinning the swampy lurch of La Grange, the mechanised stomp of Sharp Dressed Man or the syncopated riffing of Cheap Sunglasses. Even in the band’s most technologically ambitious moments, his playing retained a blues musician’s feel for weight, space and movement.
 ![ZZ Top posing for a photograph in 2016](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/x7aUf8eB8eSge9dcqjqW9m.jpg) 
Over the years, Beard became an increasingly self-contained presence on stage, enclosed behind the ornate, chrome-plated custom kits that perfectly reflect ZZ Top’s mixture of hot-rod excess, futuristic technology and inscrutable absurdity.
While Gibbons and Hill developed their telepathic visual double act out front, Beard appeared locked inside his own private rhythmic world, barely acknowledging the spectacle unfolding around him. The drummer often looked less like an entertainer than a man concentrating on keeping some complicated mechanical process under exact control.
During one Wembley Arena show in 2009, Beard chain-smoked his way through the performance and stalked off stage at the end without even glancing towards the crowd. The emotional insularity that once seemed cool and imperturbable could occasionally harden into something more detached. Yet the pulse beneath ZZ Top has never faltered.
Towards the end of That Little Ol’ Band From Texas, Beard reflected on the group’s extraordinary longevity and his position in the hierarchy with typical understatement and a momentary, almost childlike, innocence.
“I never wanted to quit ZZ Top,” he said. “And I never wanted to get fired.”

Contributor to Q magazine, Kerrang!, Mojo, The Guardian, The Independent, The Telegraph, et al. Formerly drummer in TV Smith’s Explorers, London Zoo, Laughing Sam’s Dice and others. 65dac6dcfc50b68d56dd8f90.title: Manchester United and Brighton closing in on deal for Carlos Baleba
65dac6dcfc50b68d56dd8f90.author: David Ornstein
65dac6dcfc50b68d56dd8f90.content:
Manchester United and Brighton & Hove Albion are closing in on a deal for midfielder Carlos Baleba.
United have made an offer of around £60million (€70m, $81m) plus £5m in add-ons which is felt to be below what Brighton would be seeking to sell.
Amicable talks continue with all parties working towards finding an agreement for the Cameroon international to move to Old Trafford.
Advertisement
The 22-year-old is currently working his way back to fitness after an ankle ligament injury but the issue is not considered serious or expected to keep him out long-term.
Midfield has been an area of significant focus for United in the transfer market this summer.
Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have already arrived from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively while a deal for Atalanta midfielder Ederson was also agreed before the club backed out over injury concerns surrounding the Brazil international’s knee.
They were also keen on Elliot Anderson before the England international opted to move to rivals Manchester City instead.
Should a move for Baleba progress he would join Tielemans, Santos, Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes as first-team options for head coach Michael Carrick.
Manuel Ugarte is currently sidelined with the knee injury he suffered during the World Cup with Uruguay while Mason Mount has also missed the final two games of pre-season.
Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in the summer of 2023 and has played 112 times for the south-coast club. Last season he made 35 appearances in total for the club, missing several due to his participation at the Africa Cup of Nations.
![How Carlos Baleba would fit at Manchester United and what else to know](https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2026/08/19091900/GettyImages-2261791761-e1787145568908-1024x681.jpg?width=400&quality=70) 
Why United have wanted Baleba
Analysis by Manchester United correspondent Laurie Whitwell
After United made significant work to explore a transfer for Baleba last summer, the midfielder had a difficult campaign with Brighton. But The Athletic reported in April how signing him was still highly plausible due to his impressive displays in his first two seasons in the Premier League and his underlying data.
United also watched him play for Cameroon during the Africa Cup of Nations, alongside Bryan Mbeumo, where Baleba was viewed as having a positive tournament across five matches. United rate his metrics as a good fit for the squad in terms of ground coverage, possession-winning and passing.
Given his left-footedness, Baleba could also potentially provide cover at left-back.
![](https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2026/08/19045943/Carlos-Baleba_player_roles_2025-26.png)
Last season Baleba was substituted off in 15 Premier League games, including at half-time on four occasions. It seems undeniable that United’s pursuit last summer turned his head, and his form at Brighton was partially affected. He also worked through some injury niggles. When appearing for Cameroon, he regained his confidence. Brighton staff supported him throughout.
Advertisement
Baleba completed 90 minutes only three times, but one of those was in the 3-0 win over Chelsea, when he played well, winning the ball in the penalty box from Robert Sanchez to set up Jack Hinshelwood for a big chance. He started the next three matches and came off the bench against United on the final day.
Last summer, when Baleba’s stock was high after two excellent seasons, United would have gone to £75m but Brighton wanted more than £100m. Now, United are set to strike a deal for significantly below that.

The 22-year-old Cameroon international is recovering from an ankle ligament injury that is not considered long-term.

70947dc6298e581738ba1da3.title: Sophie Adenot becomes first French woman to conduct spacewalk at ISS
70947dc6298e581738ba1da3.author: Nathan Joubioux; Gavin Blackburn
70947dc6298e581738ba1da3.content:
The goal of the six-and-a-half hour spacewalk is to replace a space-to-ground antenna on the orbital complex, according to NASA.
Sophie Adenot has become the first French female astronaut to venture outside the International Space Station (ISS) for a spacewalk on Tuesday, accompanied by American astronaut Anil Menon.
The spacewalk is scheduled to last six and a half hours, with the goal of replacing a space-to-ground antenna on the orbital complex, according to NASA.
Adenot, 44, is the second European woman to conduct a spacewalk, after Italian astronaut Samantha Cristoforetti's mission in 2022.
The French astronaut had been preparing for the operation for several days aboard the ISS, in orbit 400 kilometres above the Earth.
"A successful (spacewalk) starts long before the hatch opens and that's where my focus has been these past few days: rehearsing, preparing and focusing," Adenot said in a post on X on Sunday.
The antenna being replaced is key to high-speed communications and data transmission between the ISS and mission control in Houston, she added.
Flight engineer Jack Hathaway and station commander Jessica Meir are monitoring the spacewalkers and operate a robotic arm from inside the ISS, NASA said.
"While the spacewalkers are the ones out in the spotlight, (extravehicular activities) are very much a team effort and it's always a privilege to support the crew from within," Adenot wrote after the previous spacewalk, when she supported Meir and Menon.
An engineer by training and a former test pilot, Adenot became in February the second Frenchwoman in history to fly into space, after pioneer Claudie Haignere.
The last French person to walk in space was Thomas Pesquet, who did so six times over two stays aboard the ISS.

b7375f70eb1e3bb5571118ea.title: BBC’s Emma Barnett reveals she’s had hysterectomy ‘I never wanted to have’
b7375f70eb1e3bb5571118ea.author: Harriette Boucher
b7375f70eb1e3bb5571118ea.content:
BBC presenter Emma Barnett has revealed that she had to undergo a hysterectomy that she “didn’t want to have” as a result of her crippling endometriosis.
The 41-year-oldToday programme host said her symptoms became “a lot worse” in her final weeks of filming documentary Fighting Endometriosis, in which she discusses her life-long struggle with the condition.
Just two days before the documentary aired in June, Ms Barnett had to undergo a sudden and extensive endometriosis surgery, a hysterectomy to remove her womb and a gallbladder removal.
She wrote on Substack: “I felt blind-sided and robbed. Even though my care had been superb and doctors, utterly brilliant.
“But this was not the road I had envisioned for myself. I had the hysterectomy I never wanted to have.”
![Ms Barnett first revealed her diagnosis in 2024](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/05/29/11/03/565532.jpeg)
Ms Barnett has frequently spoken out about the debilitating pain she experiences from endometriosis, a condition where tissue grows outside the uterus and causes swelling, bleeding, and severe pain during a period.
She said she did not want or plan to have her recent surgery, but said the situation became “urgent and non-negotiable”.
“I didn’t want this procedure because it’s major surgery. It’s frightening and a hard recovery - something I am living now. I didn’t want it because I wanted there to have been medicine or treatment to help my endometriosis. It felt and feels too extreme.
“Is such major surgery what anyone would ‘choose’? Yes, I officially and legally consented to the procedures - in so much as you can know what you are letting yourself in for.”
Ms Barnett said she did not “buy into the idea that the womb is sacred and at the heart of being a woman. I am still very much a woman and me.
“I am grateful to it because somehow it managed to help me have two children. Having your womb removed without having children if you wanted them is a totally different situation - one I must acknowledge.”
![Endometriosis costs the UK economy £8.2bn a year](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/10/14/23/13082449-d089b217-2bf0-420e-8f16-e0c99a63d5fe.jpg)
Earlier this year, Ms Barnett spoke out about a “horrific” experience with endometriosis where she couldn’t “remember a single thing” about a radio broadcast after being hit with intense pain.
The presenter previously had a laparoscopy, a surgical procedure to surgically remove endometriosis, which she said was difficult to recover from, and provided no pain relief.
She returned to air on Wednesday morning after an 11-week recovery, which she described as “one of the most humbling experiences of my life.”
The cause of endometriosis is unknown and affects around one in 10 women, according to Endometriosis UK.
Some 1.5 million women in Britain suffer from the condition, which costs the UK economy £8.2bn a year in treatment, loss of work and healthcare costs.

The 41-year-old broadcaster stated that while the surgery was urgent and non-negotiable, it was a procedure she never wanted and left her feeling blindsided. Barnett has since returned to work following an 11-week recovery period.

953ca5e619801b7cb8c42a54.title: Must-see London art exhibitions closing in August 2026
953ca5e619801b7cb8c42a54.author: Anny Shaw
953ca5e619801b7cb8c42a54.content:
Must-see London art exhibitions closing in August 2026
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Dame Tracey Emin exhibition to launch at Tate Modern](https://cdn.ex.co/transformations-account/production/761715bb-261d-4032-af09-a493a82bd926/834a99c1-70e6-4159-89ad-86a66723986e/thumbnail-360.webp)
August is when the art world’s movers and shakers decamp to yachts and the Balearics, leaving London’s museums and galleries in a summer lull. The big autumn openings are still a few weeks away, but before everyone swaps the Med for Frieze week there are plenty of reasons to stay in town. Several of the year’s hottest exhibitions are entering their final days, from blockbuster surveys to quieter discoveries. Here are the ones worth catching before they vanish.
David Hockney: A Year in Normandie
Serpentine North Gallery until August 23
![Thomas Mupfupi Resting on a Pink and White Checkered Tablecloth](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/15/07/David-Hockney-art.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
David Hockney’s iPad pictures cannot be compared to the brilliance of his early paintings of turquoise swimming pools in Los Angeles, but there is something beguiling about the 90-metre-long frieze at the centre of this exhibition. Stitched together from 100 iPad paintings printed on to a single ribbon of paper, the epic work captures the changing seasons in Normandy and was inspired by the Bayeux Tapestry, which coincidentally goes on show at the British Museum on September 10. Hockney, who collaborated with the Serpentine on this presentation, died in June at 88. Due to a surge in public interest, opening times have been extended until 9pm on August 21 and 22.
Barbara Hepworth in Colour
Courtauld until September 6
Barbara Hepworth is usually associated with the cool, pale stone and polished wood of her abstract sculptures, but this illuminating show reveals an artist who had a far more nuanced relationship with colour. Deep blues, vivid reds, greens and yellows punctuate her carved forms and drawings where colour is deftly used to create the illusion of depth. Her move to St Ives in 1939 transformed these experiments: pale blue came to evoke the Cornish sky and sea, while taut red strings suggested the tension of wind, water and hills. Yet the roots of this palette predated Cornwall, in Hepworth’s encounters with Mondrian and European modernism.
A revealing rethink of a familiar artist.
Hurvin Anderson
Tate Britain until August 23
At first glance, Hurvin Anderson’s paintings look like celebrations of colour: lush greens, electric blues, purples and pinks conjure the tropical landscapes of Jamaica and Trinidad. But his retrospective also reveals something more complicated. Born in Birmingham to Jamaican parents, Anderson has spent three decades painting between Britain and the Caribbean. His pictures of the latter are repeatedly interrupted by fences, grilles and chicken wire, geometric devices that become visual and conceptual barriers. Darker, hazier paintings recall the Handsworth of his childhood — football in Handsworth Park, swimming pools and the makeshift barbershops that became social hubs for Caribbean immigrants. The result is a compelling examination of what it means to belong.
Summer Exhibition 2026
Royal Academy until August 23
![Gallery view of the Summer Exhibition at Royal Academy of Arts](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/15/32/Gallery-view-of-the-Summer-Exhibition-at-Royal-Academy-of-Arts-2026.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Much like shopping in your local charity shop, you must be prepared to rummage through the dross to find the gems in the RA Summer Exhibition of 1,851 works. Several comedians are trying their hand at art: Joe Lycett pictures Cilla Black in a rather unflattering light, while Harry Hill has two bizarre paintings of burning cars. Even more bizarre (but strangely pleasing) is a video of a man doing David Bowie karaoke. At the more established end of the spectrum, there are hits and misses, too. Try to ignore Ugo Rondinone’s LED rainbow sculpture spelling “the song is you” in the courtyard and head straight for Frank Bowling’s multi-coloured offering instead. Interconnectedness is the theme, according to artist Ryan Gander, who has co-ordinated this year’s show, though that feels more like a challenge than manifesto.
Zurbarán
National Gallery until August 23
Francisco de Zurbarán’s first major UK exhibition brings together more than 40 works, from monumental altarpieces to exquisitely observed still lifes. Most powerful are the intense, mystical works of the Baroque Spanish master’s early Seville years. Take, for example, The Crucifixion (1627), in which Christ’s pale, muscular body emerges from near-total darkness, an image so illusional early viewers thought it a sculpture. The Apparition of Saint Peter to Saint Peter Nolasco (1629), which portrays a dream-like scene of a crucified man falling through space, is stranger still. A remarkably modern take on deep, if unnerving, spirituality.
Tracey Emin: A Second Life
Tate Modern until August 31
![An artwork from Tracey Emin's Tate Modern EXHIBITION 2026](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/15/01/Tracey-Emin-Tate-Modern-EXHIBITION-2026.jpeg?trim=985,1095,1141,1006&quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Few artists can do it like Emin, who has attained icon status. Early appliqué blankets, spidery prints and show-stoppingly candid videos about why she never became a mother are hung alongside archival material: family photographs and handwritten poetry, offering a no-holds-barred window on to the artist’s suffering, pain and joy. My Bed (1998) also makes an appearance, writ large in contemporary art history but surprisingly delicate in real life.
Cecily Brown: Picture Making
Serpentine South Gallery until September 6
Cecily Brown’s first major UK institutional show in more than 20 years is a homecoming of sorts. Based in New York since 1994, the London-born painter turns to memories of the English countryside and nearby Kensington Gardens for a new series of landscapes, where trees, water, animals and figures emerge and dissolve among her gestural brushstrokes. But nature here is never entirely benign. Woodland idylls tip into something darker and more unstable; beauty seems perpetually on the verge of unravelling. Brown’s landscapes may be fantastical, but their sense of a natural world in flux feels unnervingly familiar viewed during a summer of extreme heat and wildfires.
Project a Black Planet
Barbican until September 6
Pan-Africanism is the sprawling subject of this ambitious exhibition, which brings together more than 250 works from Africa, the Caribbean, Brazil, North America and Europe, spanning a century. Paintings by El Anatsui, Claudette Johnson and Lynette Yiadom-Boakye sit alongside photography, film, posters, journals and archival material, tracing ideas of black identity, resistance, liberation and solidarity. It is a demanding show — its curatorial arguments can sometimes threaten to overwhelm the art — but there are moments of real power, particularly in Johnson’s charged self-portraits. Allow plenty of time: this is an exhibition to explore rather than skim.
953ca5e619801b7cb8c42a54.summary: London galleries and museums feature several notable art exhibitions closing in August and September 2026. The featured shows cover a wide variety of works, including David Hockney's Normandy frieze at the Serpentine North Gallery, Barbara Hepworth's color experiments at the Courtauld, and Francisco de Zurbarán's Baroque masterpieces at the National Gallery. Other highlighted exhibitions include displays by Hurvin Anderson, Tracey Emin, Cecily Brown, and the Royal Academy's Summer Exhibition.

The Courtauld's Barbara Hepworth exhibition explores the artist's use of deep blues, reds, greens, and yellows in her carved forms and drawings.
Tate Britain's Hurvin Anderson retrospective examines his paintings of tropical Caribbean landscapes alongside barriers like fences and grilles.
Francisco de Zurbarán's major UK exhibition at the National Gallery brings together over 40 works, including mystical early Seville pieces.
Tracey Emin's exhibition at Tate Modern includes appliqué blankets, personal videos, archival material, and her famous work My Bed.

82a52305d20766808f3a496f.author: Live Reporting Edited by Angus Thompson; Caitlin Doherty; With Writing

We can now bring you photos of Hassan El-Khawas, 55, Zeina Alayn, 37, and 14-year-old Sara El-Khawas, who died after getting into difficulty in the sea in Shoreham on Tuesday.

![Hassan El-Khawas](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/8/19/8cae7670-4b78-410c-ae27-3d3372175109.jpg.webp) Image source, Al-Arab in UK

![Zeina Alayn](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/8/19/08ac5e1b-8dbe-474e-882d-9506ed924637.jpg.webp) Image source, Al-Arab in UK
Zeina Alayn

826253359542388956fc1f16.title: US-led drills to end six days early, South Korea says, amid Trump push for Kim Jong-un talks
826253359542388956fc1f16.author: Raphael Rashid
826253359542388956fc1f16.content:
South Korea’s military has confirmed that joint military drills with the US will be cut short, days after Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon to scale back the exercises.
In a statement on Wednesday, South Korea’s joint chiefs of staff said at the request of the US side, the Ulchi Freedom Shield (UFS) exercise – which began on Monday would end on Friday, six days earlier than originally planned.
Separately, joint field training exercises, live outdoor drills held alongside the simulated command exercise, would also be “partially reduced”, though the two militaries were still working out the details, the statement said.
A Pentagon official later confirmed the US military was “substantially” reducing joint exercises with South Korea.
Trump said on Sunday he was “not happy” with US participation in the exercise, citing his “very good relationship” with the North Korean leader, Kim Jong-un, and describing the drills as costly and “hostile” toward Pyongyang.
South Korea’s foreign minister, Cho Hyun, told a parliamentary hearing on Wednesday that Seoul had been caught off guard by Trump’s directive.
“Our government officials, of course, and the US government officials hadn’t known about it in advance”, Cho said, when asked whether Seoul had been informed.
![US army soldiers conduct a training exercise on a river in Yeoncheon, South Korea, near the border with North Korea, on Tuesday.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ed0f98e8e5dc70502242d9bd495eeca42574d678/0_0_8640_5760/master/8640.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Ahead of Wednesday’s announcement, South Korean broadcasters KBS and MBC and the newspaper Kyunghyang reported, citing unnamed military sources, that the exercise’s second stage, a simulated counterattack against North Korea that Pyongyang has always denounced most sharply, would be scrapped entirely and bring the exercise to an early end.
Days before the exercise began, Lt Gen Scott Winter, deputy commander of the United Nations Command, the multinational body that oversees the armistice and contributes personnel to the exercise, described this year’s UFS exercise as “bigger and better than ever”.
The US military presence in South Korea dates back to the Korean war, which ended in an armistice rather than a formal peace treaty in 1953, meaning the two Koreas remain technically at war.
US troops have been stationed in South Korea ever since, and the country now hosts Camp Humphreys, the largest American military base outside the US. The two militaries train and operate together closely, including through large-scale annual exercises such as this week’s.
Previous cuts and cancellations to joint exercises, including in 1992, 1994 and after Trump’s first summit with Kim in 2018, were all decided before the drills began, rather than after they were already under way.
Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Trump was pushing aides to arrange a meeting with Kim as early as the northern hemisphere autumn, citing unnamed US officials.
The paper said Trump had privately discussed an in-person meeting to take place during his next trip to Asia, which could be in November when he is expected to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen, China.
![Trump meets with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un at the border of North and South Korea in 2019.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/8d4cd05294a5e8be4b529e5a6aca3d0ae2032f10/0_0_4252_2835/master/4252.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Earlier, a social media post from Trump showing an image of Kim surrounded by military officials, speaking into a telephone, captioned “Hey Donald, we cool … right?”.
Trump also told reporters Kim had “responded” to his overtures for talks, though he declined to give details.
Trump met Kim three times during his first term, including a brief crossing into North Korean territory at the demilitarised zone in 2019. Speculation about a renewed summit has grown since Trump shared an old photograph of the pair together on Truth Social last weekend.
Cheong Seong-chang, the vice-president of the Seoul-based Sejong Institute thinktank, said Trump could go further if talks with Kim resumed, potentially suspending the joint exercises altogether or reducing US troop numbers without consulting Seoul.
South Korea’s presidential office said this week it would continue to coordinate with Washington on the exercises as president Lee Jae Myung separately renewed calls for greater military independence.
826253359542388956fc1f16.summary: South Korea's military has confirmed that joint UFS drills with the United States will end six days early at the request of the US. The decision follows Donald Trump's order to scale back the exercises due to his relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and his push for potential talks. South Korean officials stated they were caught off guard by Trump's directive, which also involves partially reducing joint field training.
key_points: Joint US-South Korean military drills are ending six days early at the request of the US.
Donald Trump ordered the reduction citing his relationship with Kim Jong-un and describing the exercises as costly and hostile.
South Korea's foreign minister stated that government officials in Seoul were not informed in advance.
Reports indicate Trump is also pushing aides to arrange a potential in-person meeting with Kim Jong-un as early as autumn.

53fc54bd4d962a95c413fdab.title: Jump in energy bills drives inflation to 2.9% - the highest rate for four months
53fc54bd4d962a95c413fdab.author: Live Reporting Edited by Ben Hatton; With Reporting
53fc54bd4d962a95c413fdab.content:
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2024/11/21/efc4785b-e209-4310-bc20-65148f0cfca4.jpg.webp) Adam Goldsmith
Live reporter
![A close up of a smart meter](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/8/19/8865872b-1713-45a9-aef4-4702ae012814.jpg.webp) Image source, Universal Images Group via Getty Images
Today's inflation figures saw the UK's rate rise to 2.9% in the year up to July, up from 2.6% the month before.
It's been largely put down to a rise in energy bills, after energy regulator Ofgem's 13% increase in the price cap on household gas and electricity bills took effect on 1 July - which will add Â£221 to the typical household's annual bill.
Despite the change, each person will likely feel the impact on their own pocket differently, our cost of living correspondent writes.
That's because the ONS calculates the UK's monthly inflation rate by measuring the cost of 760 goods in an attempt to create a representative sample - how it impacts you will depend on the purchases you make.
And although the ONS says the UK has seen "the largest rise in gas prices for almost four years", the inflation rate for the price of food - 1.3% - is at its lowest for close to five years.
UK Chancellor John Healey insists the UK's economy is "resilient" in the face of continued pressure from the war in Iran, but shadow chancellor Mel Stride says prices are "accelerating once again" and criticises "Labour's mismanagement".
Our deputy economics editor writes that the inflation rate rise is more modest than some analysts had feared earlier in the year - she's looked at how today's figures could impact interest rates here.
We're closing our live coverage there, but we've more on today's inflation rate figures in our news story.
![Line chart of the UK's Consumer Price Index annual inflation rate,  from January 2020 onwards In the year to January 2020, inflation was 1.8%.  It then fell close to 0% in late-2020 before rising sharply,  hitting a high of 11.1% in October 2022. It then fell to a low of 1.7%  in September 2024 before rising again. In the year to July 2026,  prices rose by 2.9%](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/8/19/794d3232-fce6-4525-9343-bd4b51d70e91.png.webp)
53fc54bd4d962a95c413fdab.summary: The UK's annual inflation rate rose to 2.9% in the year up to July, reaching its highest level in four months. This increase was largely driven by a rise in energy bills following Ofgem's 13% increase in the household price cap on July 1. While gas prices saw their largest rise in nearly four years, food inflation fell to its lowest rate in close to five years.
key_points: UK inflation increased to 2.9% in the year to July, up from 2.6% the previous month.
The rise is mainly attributed to Ofgem's 13% energy price cap increase, adding £221 to typical annual household bills.
The ONS noted the largest rise in gas prices for almost four years.
Food price inflation dropped to 1.3%, its lowest rate in nearly five years.
Politicians disagreed on the figures, with Chancellor John Healey calling the economy resilient and shadow chancellor Mel Stride criticizing price acceleration.

2dc69b31899b42725b8a6f2e.title: ‘GTA VI’ Leaker Drops Even More New Footage, Reveals Motivations
2dc69b31899b42725b8a6f2e.author: Paul Tassi
2dc69b31899b42725b8a6f2e.content:
Last night, Rockstar was plagued by yet another leak of Grand Theft Auto VI footage, this time just a few months ahead of the game’s release in November. The leaker, known as Cyberleek, has released footage of gameplay and the map of GTA VI, content that Take-Two has been issuing takedowns for since its release, though the social media spread is largely uncontained.
Cyberleek has been vocal about the leak and has actually spelled out their motivations for doing it. In a statement, they said: “A digital copy cannot sell out. Yet publishers kept the preorder system and stripped away its only consumer benefit. Now gamers pay early and receive nothing in return except a countdown timer and a cosmetic skin."
This is in the wake of Take-Two announcing there would be no physical copies of GTA VI for consoles. Purchasing a box copy would contain nothing more than a code. The move is adjacent to Sony announcing it would produce no more physical games in 2028, but Rockstar’s move starts this year, which will net it a better return on its $80 game, on that will sell tens of millions of copies.
There may be alternative motivations here, as many of the releases contain watermarks promoting a specific cryptocurrency for purchase, suggesting the leaker is trying to get something out of this besides internet infamy.

Some are criticizing the footage for its quality; one clip shows Jason getting out of a car and beating to death a driver with a wrench, and the movement and visuals seem underwhelming to some. However, Cyberleek themselves have confirmed that the leaked footage is from 2023, and a whole lot of work has happened between now and this late-2026 release.
The leak has also produced new, previously unknown information like a fuel gauge on cars, and within the last few hours, a claim that GTA VI will feature a currency that can be traded for real-life money, similar to Roblox. Cyberleek promises more releases and screenshots are coming today. (Update: shortly after publication, another trove of leaks of gameplay footage, including a cutscene, have been uploaded).
The leaks hardly seem devastating to the game’s prospects, but it is sure to infuriate Rockstar, which has an extensive reveal of GTA VI gameplay and systems on Netflix and YouTube in just over a week. Everyone spreading and debating three-year-old clips with no context is certainly not what it wants to see.
There is an uneven history of leakers in all types of media getting caught or slipping away. One of the most famous cases is a man who uploaded an unfinished version of X-Men Origins: Wolverine online. He was eventually caught and sentenced to a year in federal prison.
This story is ongoing, and we will see what happens next with what may hit the internet soon. Reportedly a new leak has just been released within the last half hour. Rockstar has not yet issued a public s

The leaker cited motivations related to publisher preorder practices and the shift away from physical game discs, though watermarks in the footage suggest potential cryptocurrency promotion motives. The leaked clips date back to 2023, and while Take-Two is issuing takedowns, Cyberleek has promised further releases.
key_points: A leaker named Cyberleek released new GTA VI gameplay and map footage ahead of the November release.
Cyberleek stated the leaks were motivated by consumer grievances regarding digital-only preorders and the lack of physical discs.
Watermarks in the leaked material suggest the leaker may be attempting to promote a specific cryptocurrency.

734703744d57b2810b54ed0c.title: Diddy could face criminal charges linked to Tupac murder
734703744d57b2810b54ed0c.author: James Desborough; Ben Stockton
734703744d57b2810b54ed0c.content:
![Secret 2008 police recording allegedly captures a conspirator describing how Diddy offered money for the drive-by hit](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000430874899_17870668567790_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq9mmU6HeJmoR0vFje__daQIO2JF_w593QGlWaWVZxraI.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Secret 2008 police recording allegedly captures a conspirator describing how Diddy offered money for the drive-by hit](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000430874899_17870668567790_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq9mmU6HeJmoR0vFje__daQIO2JF_w593QGlWaWVZxraI.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Sean “Diddy” Combs could face charges linked to the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur following a new trial, legal sources have suggested.
Three decades after Shakur was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas at the height of his fame in 1996, Duane “Keffe D” Davis is on trial for allegedly plotting the killing as part of an escalating war between two LA gangs.
The prosecution’s case hinges on Mr Davis’s own claims to police, in documentary interviews and a memoir, that he sought out Shakur after his nephew was targeted as part of a rival gang feud.
They also allege that he was in the white Cadillac from which the fatal bullet was fired, and that he “tossed” the gun to the rapper’s killer.
During a secret recording made by police in 2008, Mr Davis apparently described how he and other members of the South Side Compton Crips gang hunted down and shot Shakur in 1996.
![Duane 'Keffe D' Davis is on trial for allegedly plotting the killing of Tupac Shakur](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000351363393_17870668446812_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqj_nX2DdWTX7ckysKuZpbVbLpjmIM3w15icwZHolBvr4.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
In that secret recording – which has been entered into evidence in his trial – Mr Davis also apparently alleged that Combs, currently serving a 50-month jail sentence for federal prostitution charges, offered him $1m (£750,000) to kill Shakur.
If prosecutors manage to convict Mr Davis, “it gives a green light to take action against Diddy,” a source close to the district attorney’s office told The Telegraph. Mr Davis is insisting the claims he made were to gain fame and notoriety – and are not true.
Prosecutors allege that Shakur was killed in retaliation for the rapper and his entourage beating up Mr Davis’s nephew Orlando Anderson earlier that night, and that Mr Davis’s bragging about his involvement in the killing of the rapper is true.
Combs has previously described the allegations as “pure fiction and completely ridiculous”.
The long-running feud between Combs and Shakur in the nineties largely stems from an armed robbery in which Shakur was shot.
![A 1996 photograph of rapper Tupac Shakur (left) and Marion 'Suge' Knight](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000498734476_17870668455004_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqSXtX2EsdetTn1-9sCCH2KzzpdJQGIQ8NllpFHeLjrN4.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
He believed he had been set up by Combs and his associates, with the situation only further escalated by the release of a single by Christopher Wallace – better known as the Notorious BIG – Who Shot Ya?
If a jury believes that Mr Davis was telling the truth about his role in the killing, his conviction could add credence to his claims about Combs’s involvement and apparent offer.
“The door remains open on what charges could be made against Diddy. But if the jury convicts Davis, then it gives a green light to take action against Diddy,” a Clark County district attorney’s office source said.
“The strategy has remained to not bring in matters relating to Combs’s alleged role in all of these matters at this stage, because it would likely confuse the case and perhaps a jury.”
Michael Sanft, Mr Davis’s defence attorney, argued during his opening statement on Monday that the reason his client wasn’t charged earlier over his admissions was that investigators knew “he was full of crap”.
At one point, he pulled up a slide which read, “Bull---t”.
“Keffe D was known to do [exaggerate],” Mr Sanft said.
Steve Wolfson, the district attorney, has not commented publicly on whether prosecutors would pursue charges against Combs following Mr Davis’s trial. Police have not indicated that he is a suspect in the killing and he denies any involvement.
While Combs is not expected to appear as a witness at the trial, his presence will still be felt in the courtroom.
Binu Palal, Clark County’s chief deputy district attorney, mentioned him during his opening statement on Monday, saying the hip-hop mogul hired Mr Davis for protection during visits to the West Coast. The question of whether Combs offered Mr Davis money to kill Mr Shakur was not raised.
At the time, Combs ran the New York-based Bad Boy Records and was a fierce competitor of Suge Knight, the record executive, and his LA-based Death Row Records, which represented Shakur.
![Tupac Shakur was killed in a drive-by shooting in Nevada at 25-years-old](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000001785923_17870668447180_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqTtIhv9mL4g2e1tMOv6CycFXpFRhyhN3l-ecmuOQXRhE.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The drive-by shootings of Shakur and, six months later, Bad Boy’s Notorious BIG – also sometimes known as Biggie Smalls – marked the peak of the West Coast-East Coast hip-hop rivalry in the 1990s. The killings became two of the most high-profile unsolved murders in the US.
During Mr Davis’s trial, the jury is expected to hear from several people linked to Combs, according to a witness list filed in the case.
They include his former business partner at Bad Boy Records and a former bodyguard, as well as rival Knight, who is currently serving a 28-year sentence for a hit-and-run.
Combs went on trial in 2025 over allegations of sex trafficking and racketeering. He faced up to life in prison but was acquitted of the most serious charges. He was sentenced to four years and two months in prison on lesser prostitution-related offences.
Legal experts said that, even if Mr Davis is found guilty, the idea of charging Combs could be attractive to an ambitious prosecutor.
Sam Mirejovsky, a Las Vegas attorney and partner at law firm Sam & Ash said this will be an even more attractive case after the perceived failure of the most recent attempts to prosecute Combs.
“You could have an enterprising federal prosecutor who wants a celebrity trial and who takes Combs to the woodshed feeling that perhaps he got off a little bit lighter last go around,” he said.
Phil Carson, a former FBI agent who worked on the investigation into the murder of Wallace, believes associates of Combs could also come forward with information now that some of his circles may have collapsed in the wake of his trial last year.
![A courtroom sketch of Sean 'Diddy' Combs during his 2025 sex trafficking trial](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000430206276_17870668457635_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwfSVWeZ_vEN7c6bHu2jJnT8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
“There are people out there that have information regarding the Tupac murder, and they were close to Tupac, and they’re close to Diddy, and if they have information that they could provide law enforcement to help them prosecute Diddy possibly and provide information regarding the Tupac murder,” he said.
Sam Bassett, a criminal defence attorney, said that while leads about any potential co-conspirators would probably have been extensively vetted before charges were brought against Mr Davis, the trial could bring new information to light.
“You often uncover new information beyond the law enforcement investigation as you’re talking to witnesses, getting them ready to testify,” he said.
Mr Mirejovsky said: “Combs has a giant target on his back.”
“The evidence, in my opinion, is a little light. But the incentive for a prosecutor – whether it be the state or the feds – to get involved is high,” he added.
“I wouldn’t want to be him.”
734703744d57b2810b54ed0c.summary: Sean "Diddy" Combs could potentially face criminal charges linked to the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur depending on the outcome of Duane "Keffe D" Davis's ongoing trial. A 2008 police recording entered into evidence alleges that Combs offered Davis $1 million to kill Shakur. Combs has previously denied all involvement, dismissing the allegations as pure fiction.
key_points: Duane "Keffe D" Davis is currently on trial for allegedly plotting the 1996 drive-by shooting of Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas.
A secret 2008 police recording features Davis allegedly claiming that Sean "Diddy" Combs offered him $1 million to carry out the murder.
Legal sources suggest that a conviction of Davis could pave the way for prosecutors to take legal action against Combs.
Combs has previously described the allegations connecting him to Shakur's murder as pure fiction and completely ridiculous, and police have not named him as a suspect.
Davis's defense attorney argues that his client's previous claims were mere exaggerations made to gain fame and notoriety.

9913819761d4a6c1321751f6.title: Man Utd's pursuit of Brighton's Carlos Baleba as a 'third midfielder'
9913819761d4a6c1321751f6.author: Simon Stone
9913819761d4a6c1321751f6.content:
![Carlos Baleba playing for Brighton and being challenged for the ball by Arsenal's Declan Rice](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/b1ab/live/efa17790-9bd2-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Carlos Baleba has made 112 appearances for Brighton since joining the club from Lille for Â£23.2m in August 2023
- Published
Manchester United's midfield reconstruction is nearing completion.
After signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa in the space of 24 hours of each other last month, there has been an element of 'will-they, won't-they' about the past five weeks.
At times, it felt the 'third midfielder' search has taken on a life of its own.
Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni was heavily touted, so too Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Roma's Manu Kone. In more recent days, the name of Fulham's Sander Berge has become more prominent. That of Bournemouth's Tyler Adams has never gone away.
United privately played down potential interest in Brighton's Carlos Baleba.
But in a sense, they didn't need to be actively interested in him. Most of the work was done 12 months ago.
Now the first offer has gone in; Â£60m, plus an additional Â£5m. It won't be enough.
Talks are continuing though and the expectation is the transfer will get done.
![Manchester United's new signings Andrey Santos (right) and Youri Tielemans (second right)](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/907/cpsprodpb/64dc/live/7a67f0c0-9bc9-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
New signings Andrey Santos (right) and Youri Tielemans (second right) started alongside each other in midfield for Manchester United against AC Milan in Wroclaw
It is impossible to assess the merits of the actual transfers until the individuals concerned have played often enough to evaluate how well they have done.
However, it is fair to accept United's data and recruitment department have succeeded in reshaping Michael Carrick's midfield.
It was known in January veteran Brazilian Casemiro would leave when his contract expired on 30 June. Ruben Amorim's exit had already seen skipper Bruno Fernandes move into a more advanced role.
With Manuel Ugarte not rated highly despite his Â£50.8m price tag, it meant United went into the summer with Kobbie Mainoo as the only experienced midfielder likely to play a prominent part in the 2026-27 season.
Mainoo's strength is taking the ball in tight spaces and progressing it up the pitch. Santos has screened the defence excellently in pre-season. Tielemans has composure, an excellent passing range, and is determined to increase his goals output.
What the defeat by AC Milan in Wroclaw at the weekend highlighted was a lack of energy; a player in the old box-to-box mould. Baleba's main strength is his ability to cover the ground quickly.
If the deal goes through, and when Baleba has recovered from an ankle injury sustained in pre-season that is expected to keep him out for another couple of weeks, Carrick will have variety and options, which also include Mason Mount, Scotland World Cup squad member Tyler Fletcher and, in extremis, Fernandes.
![Manchester United spent the summer of 2022 trying to sign Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong but eventually signed Casemiro instead](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/900/cpsprodpb/d973/live/f6f725c0-9bc9-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Manchester United spent the summer of 2022 trying to sign Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong but eventually gave up
The Baleba situation also highlights a strategic change.
In the past, United have almost trailed the players they want to sign, then spent ages trying to complete a deal â or not.
Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong was a case in point in 2022. Erik ten Hag felt certain he could do the deal even though United's recruitment staff were being told it was impossible.
It was well into August before the club admitted defeat; with defeats by Brighton and Brentford triggering the Â£70m deal for Casemiro.
This summer, there has been stealth behind their work. It suited them for talk around England's Elliot Anderson to obscure what they were thinking around initial midfield targets as they knew the Nottingham Forest man would be financially beyond their reach.
The Santos deal was wrapped up within a week. The Tielemans one was less than that.
There has been consideration given to Mount being the 'third midfielder' because of his exceptional form in the early part of pre-season.
However, although his early exit in the encounter with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg on 8 August was described as 'precautionary', Mount has still to return from the foot injury, which would only have heightened concerns around his injury record.
Baleba was supposedly off the radar as a third midfielder. Tchouameni, Scott, Kone, Berge and Adams were the ones being monitored. Now United have made their move, it would be a surprise if the transfer was not concluded swiftly.
Evidently, Old Trafford's recruitment plans are now being controlled to a far tighter degree than was previously the case.
Premier League proven - but a left-back still needed
Of the four players they signed in 2025, striker Benjamin Sesko and goalkeeper Senne Lammens were the only two who were not bought from Premier League clubs.
The ease with which Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha settled into their new surroundings must have played a part in shaping thinking at Old Trafford this summer.
Cunha and Tielemans had release clauses. Mbeumo and Santos did not, neither does Baleba.
There is an argument buying from Premier League clubs costs more because they are all relatively rich. The premium, in theory, limits the risk of players failing to settle. It seems Manchester United feel the extra is worth paying.
"We want more, we need more," Carrick stressed last week.
Baleba cannot be the end. It is accepted the need for a new left-back is acute.
No-one knows who it will be at this stage. But it is fair to assume there will be one.
9913819761d4a6c1321751f6.summary: Manchester United are nearing the completion of their midfield reconstruction after making an initial bid of £60m plus £5m for Brighton's Carlos Baleba to fill their 'third midfielder' role. The club has already added Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans this summer, altering their recruitment approach to be more stealthy and focused on Premier League-proven talent. Despite these additions, manager Michael Carrick acknowledges that further reinforcements, specifically a new left-back, are still required.
key_points: Manchester United have made a £60m plus £5m opening offer for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba, with expectations that the transfer will be completed.
United previously strengthened their midfield during the summer by signing Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.
The club's recent recruitment strategy has shifted toward stealth and acquiring players with Premier League experience to reduce settling-in risks.
Baleba is currently recovering from an ankle injury sustained in pre-season that is expected to keep him out for another couple of weeks.
Club officials and manager Michael Carrick accept that an acute need remains for Manchester United to sign a new left-back.

At times, it felt the 'third midfielder' search has taken on a life of its own.
Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni was heavily touted, so too Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Roma's Manu Kone. In more recent days, the name of Fulham's Sander Berge has become more prominent. That of Bournemouth's Tyler Adams has never gone away.
United privately played down potential interest in Brighton's Carlos Baleba.
But in a sense, they didn't need to be actively interested in him. Most of the work was done 12 months ago.
Now the first offer has gone in; Â£60m, plus an additional Â£5m. It won't be enough.
Talks are continuing though and the expectation is the transfer will get done.
![Manchester United's new signings Andrey Santos (right) and Youri Tielemans (second right)](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/907/cpsprodpb/64dc/live/7a67f0c0-9bc9-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
New signings Andrey Santos (right) and Youri Tielemans (second right) started alongside each other in midfield for Manchester United against AC Milan in Wroclaw
It is impossible to assess the merits of the actual transfers until the individuals concerned have played often enough to evaluate how well they have done.
However, it is fair to accept United's data and recruitment department have succeeded in reshaping Michael Carrick's midfield.
It was known in January veteran Brazilian Casemiro would leave when his contract expired on 30 June. Ruben Amorim's exit had already seen skipper Bruno Fernandes move into a more advanced role.
With Manuel Ugarte not rated highly despite his Â£50.8m price tag, it meant United went into the summer with Kobbie Mainoo as the only experienced midfielder likely to play a prominent part in the 2026-27 season.
Mainoo's strength is taking the ball in tight spaces and progressing it up the pitch. Santos has screened the defence excellently in pre-season. Tielemans has composure, an excellent passing range, and is determined to increase his goals output.
What the defeat by AC Milan in Wroclaw at the weekend highlighted was a lack of energy; a player in the old box-to-box mould. Baleba's main strength is his ability to cover the ground quickly.
If the deal goes through, and when Baleba has recovered from an ankle injury sustained in pre-season that is expected to keep him out for another couple of weeks, Carrick will have variety and options, which also include Mason Mount, Scotland World Cup squad member Tyler Fletcher and, in extremis, Fernandes.
![Manchester United spent the summer of 2022 trying to sign Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong but eventually signed Casemiro instead](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/900/cpsprodpb/d973/live/f6f725c0-9bc9-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Manchester United spent the summer of 2022 trying to sign Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong but eventually gave up
The Baleba situation also highlights a strategic change.
In the past, United have almost trailed the players they want to sign, then spent ages trying to complete a deal â or not.
Barcelona's Frenkie de Jong was a case in point in 2022. Erik ten Hag felt certain he could do the deal even though United's recruitment staff were being told it was impossible.
It was well into August before the club admitted defeat; with defeats by Brighton and Brentford triggering the Â£70m deal for Casemiro.
This summer, there has been stealth behind their work. It suited them for talk around England's Elliot Anderson to obscure what they were thinking around initial midfield targets as they knew the Nottingham Forest man would be financially beyond their reach.
The Santos deal was wrapped up within a week. The Tielemans one was less than that.
There has been consideration given to Mount being the 'third midfielder' because of his exceptional form in the early part of pre-season.
However, although his early exit in the encounter with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg on 8 August was described as 'precautionary', Mount has still to return from the foot injury, which would only have heightened concerns around his injury record.
Baleba was supposedly off the radar as a third midfielder. Tchouameni, Scott, Kone, Berge and Adams were the ones being monitored. Now United have made their move, it would be a surprise if the transfer was not concluded swiftly.
Evidently, Old Trafford's recruitment plans are now being controlled to a far tighter degree than was previously the case.
Premier League proven - but a left-back still needed
Of the four players they signed in 2025, striker Benjamin Sesko and goalkeeper Senne Lammens were the only two who were not bought from Premier League clubs.
The ease with which Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha settled into their new surroundings must have played a part in shaping thinking at Old Trafford this summer.
Cunha and Tielemans had release clauses. Mbeumo and Santos did not, neither does Baleba.
There is an argument buying from Premier League clubs costs more because they are all relatively rich. The premium, in theory, limits the risk of players failing to settle. It seems Manchester United feel the extra is worth paying.
"We want more, we need more," Carrick stressed last week.
Baleba cannot be the end. It is accepted the need for a new left-back is acute.
No-one knows who it will be at this stage. But it is fair to assume there will be one.

The club has already added Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans this summer, altering their recruitment approach to be more stealthy and focused on Premier League-proven talent. Despite these additions, manager Michael Carrick acknowledges that further reinforcements, specifically a new left-back, are still required.

United previously strengthened their midfield during the summer by signing Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.
The club's recent recruitment strategy has shifted toward stealth and acquiring players with Premier League experience to reduce settling-in risks.
Baleba is currently recovering from an ankle injury sustained in pre-season that is expected to keep him out for another couple of weeks.
Club officials and manager Michael Carrick accept that an acute need remains for Manchester United to sign a new left-back.
