Gone are the days of major technological and hardware upgrades from model to model, at least when it comes to the digital camera industry. Smartphones are no exception, and it seems that any annual changes we do see tend to be relatively minor now.
I feel like the Pixel 11 Pro series provides plenty of customization and control of my images if I want to be more hands-on, but is still simple enough to be usable for casual users to enjoy.
Pros
- Better telephoto camera and processor
- Generative AI is less in-your-face
- The color "Looks" are fun to use and very customizable
- Magic Capture is a useful feature with minimal fluff
- Many features and functions are much faster
Cons
- Battery life is virtually the same as last year
- The Pixel fully supports Nano Banana AI but using it through Gemini is convoluted
- Image quality improvements are largely incremental
As part of its yearly release cycle, Google has announced the Pixel 11 series of phones, and with the new Pixel 11 Pro XL in hand, I proceeded to test this latest model, not as a phone, but rather as a creative photographic tool. Sadly, the current memory crisis has inflated costs across the industry, and the Pixel 11 Pro XL is going to run you at least $1,299.
![A close-up, angled view of the back of a light gray smartphone featuring a prominent, horizontal, pill-shaped camera module with three lenses and a flash, and a white "G" logo centered on the body.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-XL-0006-800x533.jpg)
Google Pixel 11 Pro XL Review: How It Feels
Both the Pro and Pro XL phones run the same cameras and have the same options for storage and RAM. However, the XL version that I tested comes with a brand-new 6.8-inch screen that now peaks at a maximum of 3,600 nits of brightness. The body design is quite similar to last year’s, comes in four colors, and features a new camera bar design. External controls are, otherwise, almost identical to the 10 series. The weight hovers around eight ounces (226 grams), which does bring it down ever so slightly from last year’s model.
![A white smartphone with a prominent, pill-shaped camera module on the back lies on a light green, marbled surface.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-XL-0005-800x533.jpg)
![Two light blue smartphones stand side-by-side against a black background, labeled "Pixel 10 Pro XL" and "Pixel 11 Pro XL" respectively.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-vs-10-800x450.jpg)
The internal battery has also dropped slightly to a maximum of 5,115 mAh. In exchange, the Pixel 11 Pro XL features a more efficient main camera sensor and the new G6 Tensor processor, which reduces power demands. I’d say that overall power usage and longevity will be similar to what we had before, which is always disappointing when talking about battery life. It’s unclear why the battery got smaller.
We also see the return of the Google Pixel Snap magnetic attachment system, which works with MagSafe accessories and chargers. Wired charging is still around 45 watts, but the wireless charging speeds have been improved this time around.
![A smartphone screen displays a "Hi there" welcome message on a black background, resting on a light green marble surface.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-XL-0001-800x533.jpg)
![A silver smartphone with a prominent horizontal camera bar on its back stands upright against a pale green marble background.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Pixel-11-Pro-XL-0008-800x533.jpg)
Google Pixel 11 Pro XL Review: The Cameras
The ultra-wide camera returns from the last model with the same 48-megapixel Type 1/2.51 sensor and f/1.7 aperture. The main camera is also very similar, though as mentioned above, it is a more power-efficient design. It features a 50-megapixel Type 1/1.3 sensor, has a fixed f/1.68 aperture, and the image quality is very similar to what we have seen before.
![A close-up of a smartphone camera module next to text listing specifications: 48MP Quad Bayer, 12mm Equivalent FOV, f/1.7, and Type 1/2.51.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Ultrawide-800x450.jpg)
![A young girl in a baseball cap and Crocs stands on rocks by a river at sunset, holding a fly fishing rod.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/PXL_20260818_023611435.RAW-01.COVER_-601x800.jpg)
![A close-up of a camera lens with text below it reading: 50MP Quad Bayer, 24mm Equivalent FOV, f/1.68, Type 1/1.3.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Main-Camera-Fixed-800x450.jpg)
![A reflection of vibrant red autumn leaves and dark tree branches appears on the rippled, murky surface of a puddle.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/PXL_20260813_193213707.RAW-01.COVER-LOOKS-STANDARD-VANILLA-601x800.jpg)
The selfie camera is the same 42-megapixel f/2.2 camera as before.
The only major hardware change is with the telephoto camera, which gives a 5x zoom equivalent and is now mated to a larger Type 1/1.95 sensor. You still get an f/2.8 aperture on the lens and optical image stabilization to help capture the shot, too. I noticed a distinct improvement in low-light image quality as well as better overall detail reproduction. It’s always nice to see real hardware changes, and the new telephoto lens is a meaningful improvement.
![A young girl with long red hair and freckles looks toward the camera while holding a menu in a restaurant.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/PXL_20260813_224103239.PORTRAIT-PIXEL-11-PRO-Portrait-mode-Classic-601x800.jpg)
![Two side-by-side images show a wooden box labeled with Japanese calligraphy resting on a shelf above a set of patterned blue and white ceramic bowls.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Telephoto-Comparison-800x450.jpg)
The phone can push beyond to a digital 30x zoom equivalent, but the image quality is noticeably cropped. However, Google has also increased the Pro Zoom AI-generated 100x range to a further 120x range now. This technology takes the woefully poor resolution of a 120x zoom crop and digitally enhances it using generative AI. Beyond the ethical questions, the result is actually usable, especially if the final output is just social media. However, the generative enhancement can only effectively be applied to non-human subjects, and any text will be guessed at with nonsense shapes if the source writing is too small or otherwise undecipherable. An extra 20x zoom at this already far reach is an incredibly minor improvement, regardless of how you feel about the technology.

![A smartphone camera interface displays a view of a paved path through a wooded area, with zoom controls, exposure settings, and a shutter button visible on the screen.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Horizontal-Interface-800x450.jpg)
The other major addition is the new “Creator” menu, which has several social media-targeted features. Most notable of these is the Teleprompter tool, which will display text on screen and automatically scroll at your talking speed. This works great, but obviously requires that you use the selfie camera to maintain access to the display, and that is the Pixel 11 Pro’s weakest camera. Beyond that, the text won’t flip for horizontal orientation, so you need to shoot in vertical mode to see your script properly. That feels like a particularly bizarre omission.
![A man wearing a baseball cap records a video outdoors, with a teleprompter overlay of text visible on the right side of the screen.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Teleprompter-800x450.jpg)
There is also a “Speech Enhancement” tool which applies digital filters to remove background noise. It works quite well, and doesn’t introduce a lot of digital artifacts into the soundtrack. We also have some small display features, like “Audio Visualizer,” which displays your audio levels, which is hardly a breakthrough technology, and “Social Media Grid”, which helps you frame for both 16:9 and 9:16. Bear in mind, though: using either of those frames will result in a substantial crop.
![A smartphone camera interface displays a view of a person riding a bicycle on a paved path through a wooded area.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/Google-Pixel-11-Pro-Social-Media-Frame-800x450.jpg)
Google Pixel 11 Pro XL Review: Incremental Improvement
Many of this year’s improvements are incremental, which is what I’ve come to expect from smartphones and even full-size cameras in recent years. With a scant few exceptions, this has become the norm.
Most of the features that were introduced were pretty minor as well, although I can see how the Magic Capture function can be legitimately useful. It’s just a shame that the captured video has so many compromises.
Hardware changes are always positive and should be celebrated. The new telephoto camera is a much-needed improvement, and I liked the results. The new G6 Tensor processor also gave noticeably faster operation of image processing, and I really appreciated the lack of wait times to do high-res modes and Night Sight photography. Although low-light quality and portrait modes give very similar results to last year’s Pixel, the usable quality was already excellent, and the processing times are now far more convenient.
![A calm pond reflects a pastel sunset sky with pink and orange clouds, framed by grassy banks and silhouetted trees.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/PXL_20260815_025020467.NIGHT_.RAW-01.COVER_-800x601.jpg)
As far as the camera applications go, I was pleasantly impressed by the Pixel 11 Pro. I also appreciate the pull back on the AI-everything front, as minor as this change of direction might seem. The camera app feels more creative and less generative, and I support that move.
Unfortunately, the rising costs of memory and storage are going to hurt potential buyers here. Google is offering a 12GB of RAM version of the phone, which will be faster than last year’s phone by virtue of the improved processor, but the experience might not reflect that as the lower memory will slim the margins by which speed improves. To get a substantial improvement, you’ll need to go with the 16GB of RAM Pixel 11 Pro XL with 512GB of storage, and that starts at $1,419, and it goes up from there. As usual with smartphones across the board, I would only consider upgrading if you have a phone from at least a couple of generations back.
![A young girl in a baseball cap and Crocs fly fishes while standing on rocks in a river during a sunset.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/PXL_20260818_023620121.RAW-01.COVER_-800x601.jpg)
![Two weathered, metal utility boxes sit in a grassy area, with the smaller foreground box featuring a yellow "Caution: Buried Cable" sign and the larger background box displaying "Danger: High Voltage" warning labels.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/08/PXL_20260813_193158574.RAW-01.COVER-LOOKS-CLASSIC-601x800.jpg)
Are There Alternatives?
In North America, the main alternative will be the Samsung S26 Ultra, which will be a similar price for similar storage. I like the general camera capabilities, but Samsung is going hard and heavy towards integrated generative AI support within its camera app. If you want to play with AI, it is the more intuitive choice, but the Pixel feels more like a photographer’s phone. The Samsung S26 might also be a better video camera choice given its native 8K resolution and built-in support for log capture.
If you have access to other phone options and care about photography first and foremost, then I highly recommend the Xiaomi 17 Ultra.
Should You Buy It?
Yes, if only because North America has a limited number of high-end Android options that are easily available, and the Pixel feels like a more creative choice. If you are willing to bring in phones that your mobile carrier might not offer, you will find far more capable photographic options.
942e9fc955ebe6e242d99440.summary: The Google Pixel 11 Pro XL features minor external design updates, a new 6.8-inch screen reaching 3,600 nits, and a starting price of $1,299 due to industry-wide memory costs. Its primary hardware upgrade is a larger telephoto camera sensor delivering improved low-light performance and detail. Meanwhile, Google has shifted its generative AI features out of the main camera app and into a more convoluted process through the Gemini assistant.
key_points: The Pixel 11 Pro XL starts at $1,299 and features a 6.8-inch screen with a peak brightness of 3,600 nits.
The only major hardware upgrade is a new telephoto camera sensor providing a 5x zoom equivalent with better low-light quality and detail.
Battery capacity has dropped slightly to 5,115 mAh, though power efficiency from the G6 Tensor processor keeps longevity comparable to the previous model.
Magic Capture is a new video-based feature that extracts high-quality still images from recorded moments.
Generative AI tools like 'Reimagine' have been removed from the camera app and are now relegated to a more convoluted process via Gemini.

f6bd74a7eb06a38dd2e4c8e6.title: Adam Copeland Reveals Surprising Retirement Plan (AEW News)
f6bd74a7eb06a38dd2e4c8e6.author: Michael Hamflett
f6bd74a7eb06a38dd2e4c8e6.content:
![Adam Copeland](https://d2thvodm3xyo6j.cloudfront.net/media/2026/02/452a63dde9ec44d9057b3649577dee18.jpg) 
Adam Copeland has said he will retire in All Elite Wrestling.
Speaking to Ariel Helwani, the former multi-time WWE Champion said he had no desire to see out his career with the market leader, instead choosing to stay in his current role in AEW.
He said; “That’s where I want to retire. I know that may disappoint a lot of people, but I love it there. I love the company. I love the attitude. I love the exuberance. I love the drive. I love the excitement I see from the locker room. I don’t want to go anywhere else. I’m good. I did everything I could do there (WWE) and then some. And I think they got everything out of me and then some that they could have.”
'Cope' debuted for All Elite Wrestling at WrestleDream 2023, and (as of writing) has worked almost 50 matches for the company ever since. He's competed for the World Heavyweight Championship, has held the TNT Championship and is currently one half of the AEW World Tag Team Champions alongside former Edge & Christian partner Christian Cage. The pair are set to work a dream match against the Young Bucks at Wembley Stadium when the company presents All In: London on August 30th, which very much supports Copeland's point about still having new things to do. He spent three years with WWE following his remarkable return from injury at the 2020 Royal Rumble, main eventing a WrestleMania along the way before wrapping up his run in August 2023 with a win over a Sheamus on a special edition of SmackDown at the Scotiabank Arena in his hometown of Toronto.
f6bd74a7eb06a38dd2e4c8e6.summary: Professional wrestler Adam Copeland has announced that he intends to finish his career in All Elite Wrestling rather than return to WWE. In an interview with Ariel Helwani, Copeland expressed his love for AEW's locker room culture, attitude, and drive. Since debuting for AEW at WrestleDream 2023, he has held multiple championships and is currently a co-holder of the AEW World Tag Team Championship.

He praised AEW's locker room attitude, exuberance, and drive.
Copeland debuted for AEW in October 2023 and has wrestled nearly 50 matches for the company.

He currently holds the AEW World Tag Team Championship alongside Christian Cage.

61c680060f8b8b637d5bb676.title: Ollie Robinson branded 'exceptional' as he and Josh Tongue cut match ball in two after taking five-fers vs Pakistan
61c680060f8b8b637d5bb676.content:
Ollie Robinson branded 'exceptional' as he and Josh Tongue cut match ball in two after taking five-fers vs Pakistan
Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue asked the Headingley grounds staff to cut the match ball in two, after both players took five-fers on opening day of England's first Test vs Pakistan; watch day two live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am on Thursday
Wednesday 19 August 2026 23:04, UK
Ollie Robinson was branded 'exceptional' by team-mate Josh Tongue after both pace bowlers bagged five-wicket hauls as England bowled Pakistan out for 171 runs on day one of the first Test match at Headingley.
After Tongue snared Mohammad Abbas to wrap up Pakistan's first innings, he and Robinson walked off the field holding hands, discussing who between them would take the match ball home.
Instead, they opted to split the ball in half, employing the help of the grounds staff to cut the ball through its seam.
"It's not often you get half a ball," Robinson told the ECB. "So it's something we'll remember forever. It's quite unique."
At stumps on day one, England were left trailing the visitors by only 59 runs, with returning captain Joe Root and Jordan Cox set to return to bat in the morning with their side on 112-2, after Ben Duckett (15) and Emilio Gay (33) were both dismissed by Abbas and Mohammad Ali.
Robinson kickstarted proceedings in incredible fashion, pinning Azan Awais with the first ball of the Test match, before also snaring Shan Masood (5) lbw before rain stopped play.
He followed up by dismissing Abdullah Shafique (61), Saud Shakeel (5), and later got Khurram Shazad (14), to take the fifth five-fer of his Test career.
It followed his incredible seven-wicket haul at Lord's against New Zealand in June, his last Test appearance.
"Ollie Robinson was excellent," Tongue said. "As a bowling unit, we were very good. I'm glad that we bowled them out.
"It was similar to his performance at Lord's.
"He's an exceptional bowler when he hits his lines and lengths and he showed that today."
Broad: Robinson's bowling attributes are excellent
Robinson missed both of England's second and third Test defeats against New Zealand earlier this summer, and prior to that, had not played for England for over two years, after falling out of favour with selectors, due to injuries and fitness issues.
After taking his first two wickets on Wednesday afternoon, Sky Sports Cricket analyst Stuart Broad commended Robinson on his bowling abilities.
"He's an excellent bowler, and certainly when conditions suit him, he's someone who is a great exponent of movement and can hold an area for a long period of time," Broad told Sky Sports Cricket.
Broad believes England will benefit from Robinson's talents over the coming years, with Root's side set to tour South Africa in the winter, before welcoming Australia for the 2027 Ashes.
"The advantage for England and Robinson over the next year is that they'll go to South Africa, where he'll be a fine bowler," Broad said.
"He's got brilliant attributes: he makes the ball bounce and hits consistent areas.
"Then you're into an Ashes series, we don't know what the pitches will be like, but you know that if you get a pitch with a bit of movement, Robinson is your best bowler for extracting that movement.
"Then he'll be around 33 the next time the English summer comes around, and England have a choice of rebuilding a new bowling attack going forward, or they want to keep dipping Ollie Robinson in and out for pitches that suit him.
"There's no doubt that you get him on Lord's or a nipper with a brand new ball, he's our best bowler in those conditions."
Karthik: Tongue adapted to the conditions quickly
Tongue was equally impressive, as he secured his fourth Test match five-fer, first claiming the important wicket of Imam-ul-Haq (42), to end his 91-run partnership with Adbullah Shafique (61).
He later hit Salman Agha's (21) stumps and found himself on a hat-trick, just as tea was called, after he dismissed Ali Usman (0) lbw.
Tongue later snared Mohammad Rizwan (12) and later wrapped up the innings by bowling Abbas.
"Tongue is an awkward bowler to deal with," Dinesh Karthik told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast. "He's been bowling at his best in the last six to eight months. He has shown his ability to get good batters out when they're set, which is a good skill to have.
"Today, he has adapted the fastest among the three pacers on display. He has the extra pace and the awkwardness of his action, goes past the perpendicular, he has a lot of attributes that trouble a lot of right-handers.
"Overall, you have to say the lengths that Josh Tongue bowled to get Imam out, who was set, that was an important wicket because a partnership was developing; once he got a sniff of that wicket, he bowled quite nicely."

Unable to decide who should take home the match ball, the pair had the grounds staff cut it in half. At stumps, England reached 112-2, trailing Pakistan by 59 runs.

The two bowlers had the Headingley grounds staff cut the match ball in two so they could both keep a unique piece.
At the end of the first day, England finished on 112-2, trailing by 59 runs with Joe Root and Jordan Cox at the crease.
Josh Tongue praised Robinson as 'exceptional' following his return to the Test side after more than two years out due to injuries and fitness issues.

df8d9d5e71ded866450f9448.title: Curtis Jones transfer news: Inter Milan close in on Â£30m deal for Liverpool midfielder
df8d9d5e71ded866450f9448.author: Aadam Patel
df8d9d5e71ded866450f9448.content:
![Curtis Jones](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1008/cpsprodpb/3d51/live/eeaadb30-9bd5-11f1-bd98-ed4222d45acc.jpg)
Curtis Jones came through Liverpool's academy and made his first-team debut at 17
- Published
Inter Milan are closing in on a deal worth 35m euros (Â£30m) for Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones.
In June, Liverpool rejected a verbal offer of 25m euros (Â£21.7m) from Italian champions Inter, with Liverpool valuing the 25-year-old, who has one year left on his current contract, at about Â£35m.
The understanding now is that a deal worth Â£30m will likely see an agreement between the clubs. Sources in Italy believe that a verbal agreement is in place but both clubs say that further details need discussion.
Liverpool are open to selling Jones and want something in line with the Â£30m package that Inter paid Tottenham for Djed Spence.
The Serie A side were interested in Jones in January and proposed a loan with a view to a transfer but that was turned down by Liverpool.
Jones has made 228 appearances for Liverpool since making his debut under Jurgen Klopp in 2019. Last season, he played 49 times in all competitions but only made 18 starts in the Premier League and struggled to secure a regular starting spot in midfield under Arne Slot.
Jones, who joined Liverpool's academy at the age of nine, is understood to be keen on pursuing a new challenge and would become the third English player to join the Italian champions this summer, after John Stones and Spence.

02e816c21932b1781de22a26.title: Private mission to save NASA's Swift space telescope fails
02e816c21932b1781de22a26.author: Josh Dinner

![illustration of two satellites meeting up in orbit, with earth in the background](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/coJpWVm3CQM5ViXRGMfSe5.jpg) 
NASA is calling off the effort to save its Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after a private rescue spacecraft couldn't overcome its own problems in orbit.
LINK, the specialized probe from Katalyst Space that NASA contracted for the Swift Boost mission, was delivered to space on an air-launched Northrop Grumman Pegasus XL rocket on July 3. The vehicle was designed to rendezvous with the Swift Observatory in order to grapple and raise it to a more stable orbit, but LINK ran into trouble when it began to spin uncontrollably about three weeks after launch.
Today (Aug. 19), NASA announced an official end to LINK's efforts to boost Swift's orbit, citing ongoing attitude control issues with the private spacecraft, but the agency hasn't canceled the mission outright. LINK will still attempt a rendezvous with Swift in order to practice proximity operations and demonstrate its capabilities other than spacecraft capture, which could aid future missions down the road.
From its inception, the Swift Boost mission was always viewed as a long shot. Increased solar activity had already begun decaying the observatory's orbit faster than anticipated when NASA awarded the $30 million Swift Boost contract to Katalyst in 2025, giving the Arizona-based company less than a year to complete LINK's design, manufacture and testing before time to save Swift would run out.
"NASA should be willing to move quickly and take smart risks when the potential return is worth it, and that is exactly what we did with this mission," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a statement today. "This is not the outcome we were working toward, but it does not change why this mission was worth attempting. The team moved with extraordinary speed to give Swift a chance to carry out more science while advancing capabilities America will need for satellite servicing in the future."
Swift is a one-of-its kind orbital observatory designed to study high-energy phenomena across the universe. It can detect sudden events like gamma-ray bursts and quickly direct its instruments to study them in X-ray, ultraviolet and visible light. The spacecraft is also routinely redirected for rapid response research to study things like newly discovered supernovae, black-hole ejections, fast radio bursts and other short-lived astronomical events.
With LINK now incapable of boosting Swift's orbit, NASA estimates the observatory will dip catastrophically low into Earth's atmosphere before the end of the year. After Swift dies, the agency says it will "continue to prioritize finding new options to react rapidly to cosmic events, using current missions to help fill the gap in the meantime."
Katalyst is working closely with NASA as the Swift Boost mission enters its next phase. Together, the company and space agency are evaluating logistics for LINK's rendezvous and maneuvering demonstration within Swift's vicinity, which will provide data for potential future servicing missions to other satellites, NASA's statement says.

479b0562ea47afbfb7ca5ede.title: Scientists Discover a New Organ Hiding in The Skull
479b0562ea47afbfb7ca5ede.author: Michael Irving
479b0562ea47afbfb7ca5ede.content:
After centuries of medical science, it's reasonable to assume that we have a complete tally of all the organs in the human body by now.
But scientists just keep discovering new ones working thanklessly in the background, performing vital functions like sensing pain or producing saliva.
The latest is all in your head. In a new study published in Nature, biologists at Washington University (WashU) School of Medicine in St. Louis have identified a new immune organ inside the skull.
From that crucial post, it seems to act like a 'security station' to fight brain cancer at the early stages.
So far this organ has only been found in mice, but the researchers say there are signs that humans have them, too. And if we can supercharge these structures, we might have a new weapon against deadly brain cancers.
"This study reveals that the skull bone marrow is far more than just a structural framework – it harbors previously unrecognized hubs for brain-specific immune responses," says Jonathan Kipnis, a brain immunologist at WashU and senior author of the new study.
"Uncovering this localized immune niche changes how we view neuroimmune interactions and opens exciting new avenues for treating brain tumors and other neurological diseases."
![Scientists Discover a New Organ Hiding in The Skull](https://www.sciencealert.com/images/2026/08/brain-lymphoids-2.png)
The human body is patrolled by not one, but two distinct immune systems – one for the central nervous system, including the brain and spinal cord, and one for the rest of the body.
It's long been thought that the two systems were completely separate, and in fact, immune cells from the peripheral system can cause all sorts of trouble if they get into the brain. Some are known to contribute to neurodegenerative diseases because the sensitive tissues in the nervous system can be harmed by the 'reckless' techniques that work elsewhere in the body.
But a growing body of research suggests there's a bit more crossover than previously thought. In previous work, the team behind the new study identified tiny channels running from brain tissue, through the dura mater (the outermost protective membrane around the brain) and into the skull itself.
This time, the researchers used fluorescent tracer proteins to observe how molecules moved along these channels, following them from neurons into the bone marrow of the skull.
Eventually they tracked them into what looked suspiciously like germinal centers – structures that form in lymph nodes and act like training camps for immune cells.
Basically, naive B cells enter these structures, multiply to great numbers, get armed, are handed 'Wanted' posters for particular pathogens by other immune cells, and are sent out into battle.
![Scientists Discover a New Organ Hiding in The Skull](https://www.sciencealert.com/images/2026/08/Germinal-center.jpeg)
In this case, these training camps are strategically located near the brain, so they can fight on the front lines without having to recruit soldiers from further afield in the body.
"We have never seen such structures in healthy bone marrow before," says Jang Hyun Park, cell biologist at WashU and first author of the study.
"It is an exciting discovery that points out that a complex brain requires its own specialized immune structures to defend it."
The researchers tested that idea in mouse models of glioma, a particularly nasty form of brain cancer. They altered the activity of these lymphoid structures by applying a hydrogel laced with either immune-promoting or immune-suppressing compounds under the scalp.
![Subscribe to ScienceAlert's free fact-checked newsletter](https://www.sciencealert.com/images/2026/05/FOMO-1200x628-_Dont-miss-the-next-breakthrough_-cosmic-colourful-642x336.jpg)
Mice with disrupted skull lymphoid structures had much more aggressive tumors and lower survival rates than control mice.
However, mice given a mix of three immune-boosting proteins showed stronger immune responses from their skull lymphoids, fighting off their cancer more effectively and significantly increasing their survival.
Of course, findings in mice don't necessarily translate to humans, but the researchers say that follicular T cells have previously been detected in the bone marrow of human skulls, which could be a clue that these structures are also hiding in our own heads.
If so, it could eventually mark a major improvement in how we fight brain cancer: A hydrogel injected under the scalp is far less invasive than full brain surgery to remove tumors.
"The finding fundamentally changes our current understanding of neuroimmunology," says Kipnis.
"Knowing that the brain relies on first responders in the surrounding skull for defense has the potential to change how we think about developing therapies for many neurological conditions, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, schizophrenia, long COVID, and many others that have an immune component to them.
"Such therapies could access these immune hubs directly through the skull, without major peripheral side effects."
The research was published in the journal Nature.
479b0562ea47afbfb7ca5ede.summary: Biologists at Washington University School of Medicine have identified a new immune organ inside the skull bone marrow of mice, with signs suggesting humans have them too. These structures act as specialized training camps for immune cells, functioning as a security station to fight early-stage brain cancer. Researchers successfully used immune-boosting treatments via the skull in mice to improve survival rates against glioma, potentially offering less invasive treatment avenues for various neurological conditions.
key_points: Washington University researchers discovered a new immune organ inside the skull bone marrow.
The organ acts like a germinal center to train immune cells on the front lines to defend the brain.
Disrupting these skull structures in mice led to more aggressive brain tumors and lower survival rates.
Applying immune-boosting compounds under the scalp helped mice fight off cancer more effectively.
Researchers found clues that similar structures exist in human skulls, which could lead to less invasive brain cancer therapies.

98972e4673fc3708c8d82d43.title: Ridge appoints new project and programme delivery leader for London
98972e4673fc3708c8d82d43.author: Rockwool
98972e4673fc3708c8d82d43.content:
Appointment part of move to grow the function in the capital
Ridge has appointed a new partner for project and programme delivery.
The firm said Giles Heather has been tasked to grow its team in London, handling programme leadership, project controls, project management and portfolio management for clients across the capital.
The appointment comes as the consultant moves to grow its capabilities in the programme delivery of complex projects. Last year it acquired project management specialist Adept Management.
![S_260629_N23_webview](https://d3sux4fmh2nu8u.cloudfront.net/Pictures/480xAny/0/6/5/2036065_s_260629_n23_webview_977904_crop.jpg)
Heather has more than 18 years experience in programme and project delivery across various sectors, with much of his career spent at Turner & Townsend and more recently Linesight.
“Giles’s appointment is a clear statement of intent for our project and programme delivery team in London,” said Jolyon Price, executive group and partner at Ridge.
“London is a market where clients expect specialist expertise, technical depth and clear accountability from day one, and Giles brings all three.”
98972e4673fc3708c8d82d43.summary: Ridge has appointed Giles Heather as a new partner to lead and expand its project and programme delivery team in London. Heather brings over 18 years of experience from previous roles at Turner & Townsend and Linesight. This appointment supports the firm's ongoing strategy to strengthen its capabilities in managing complex projects within the capital.
key_points: Ridge appointed Giles Heather as a new partner for project and programme delivery in London.
Heather's role involves handling programme leadership, project management, and controls for clients in the capital.
He has over 18 years of experience, having previously worked at Turner & Townsend and Linesight.
The move is part of Ridge's broader strategy to grow its complex project capabilities following its acquisition of Adept Management last year.

f1fced5179b11c1018a9b3b2.title: Andy Burnham to donate 15% of PM salary to homelessness fight
f1fced5179b11c1018a9b3b2.author: Liam Geraghty
f1fced5179b11c1018a9b3b2.content:
“There are things that we can do. We proved it in the pandemic. We should do it again now and it should just be what we do all the time.”
Burnham made a pledge to end rough sleeping his first instruction after being unveiled as prime minister last month.
This week he laid out his first steps on how he intends to achieve a milestone that has eluded governments since the New Labour years. Burnham’s approach echoes the Everyone In scheme that saw rough sleepers taken off the streets during the Covid pandemic.
	
	
		
			
				
									
Continue reading for free
													
Registration is free and takes less than 30 seconds.
													
Our supporters make Big Issue’s work possible. Join us to see the impact we’re having together and discover more ways to help people facing poverty access income, opportunity and support.
							 
			
		 
	 
 
Read more:
The prime minister announced that every person sleeping rough in England will be given a route off the streets by Christmas.
New accommodation and support will be rolled out across England this winter based on the A Bed Every Night model he pioneered as Greater Manchester mayor.
Emergency accommodation will be made available alongside help with housing, health and other needs to help people out of homelessness, backed with increased funding of £442 million.
Big Issue founder Lord John Bird said Burnham’s announcement that he will back up his announcement with a personal commitment is significant.
“The prime minister is leading by example by donating 15% of his salary to the fight against homelessness. This gesture reminds us that homelessness is all our problem and eradicating it will need everyone to put our shoulder to the wheel,” said Bird.
“Today he’s backed his ambition with personal and political action, and I look forward to working with him to make this ambition a reality.”

The strategy mirrors the successful 'Everyone In' scheme from the Covid pandemic and builds on the 'A Bed Every Night' model he previously pioneered.

d35ccbff7f61b9dfb8ae3f37.title: Israel admits firing on car carrying Hind Rajab, symbol of Gaza’s suffering
d35ccbff7f61b9dfb8ae3f37.author: Al Jazeera Staff
d35ccbff7f61b9dfb8ae3f37.content:
![Hind](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2025-09-03T155148Z_851274364_RC2FKGAAHC2Y_RTRMADP_3_FILMFESTIVAL-VENICE-THE-VOICE-OF-HIND-RAJAB-1787149476.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
More than two years after Hind Rajab was killed, becoming a symbol of the suffering of children in Gaza, Israel’s military, long accused of the atrocity, has announced a criminal investigation into the death of the five-year-old girl.
At first, Israel denied that its soldiers were even in the area where she was killed. After journalistic investigations, including by Al Jazeera, Israel’s army said it had raided “terror targets” in Gaza City that day. In January this year, Israeli officials said they were reviewing the case.

- list 2 of 3‘Substantial evidence’ of double-tap strike in killing of Hind Rajab

The military said on Wednesday that troops had “fired at a vehicle that was approaching them”. It is the first time Israel has admitted shooting at the car.
But criminal misconduct investigations into Israeli troops over the killing of Palestinians rarely lead to convictions.

Decades of Israeli crimes against Palestinians have not delivered any serious form of justice, according to the president of the Hind Rajab Foundation, Dyab Abou JahJah, who does not believe this case will change that.
The foundation said it had no confidence in Israel’s decision to launch a criminal probe into Rajab’s killing.
“We do not trust the Israeli justice system, not out of an ideological position, but because of the track record,” Abou Jahjah told Al Jazeera. “And in this particular case, the Israeli justice system as a whole has always been complicit in Israeli crimes.”
Rajab’s grandmother, also named Hind Rajab, told The Associated Press news agency by phone that the Israeli investigation is not enough, and called for an international probe into the killing of her granddaughter and all of the thousands of children killed in Gaza during the war.
“An international investigation is required to uncover the truth and hold all those responsible accountable,” she said. “We call for justice, not only for Hind, but for all Gaza children.”
Rajab’s last words, her recorded pleas for help by phone, were widely shared on social media and led to international condemnation. A 2024 Al Jazeera investigation into the killing of Rajab and her family revealed that an Israeli tank was likely 13 to 23 metres (43 to 75ft) away and would have clearly seen the civilians inside the car. A docu-drama on the killing of Hind Rajab was nominated at the 2026 Oscars for best international feature film.
Al Jazeera’s Hani Mahmoud, reporting in Gaza, said this sentiment is shared among Palestinians. “People here who are hearing about the investigation are sceptical that it will bring any justice to Hind and her family,” he said.

Announcing its first criminal probes of troop conduct in Gaza, Israel’s military said the case of Rajab and her family members in early 2024 would be reviewed, as well as the killing of 15 Palestinian medics in March 2025. Both incidents gained international attention.
The announcement followed reviews of 150 incidents of troop conduct during Israel’s war on Gaza, it said, but added that the military would not launch criminal investigations into three other attacks that killed aid workers from the World Central Kitchen and Doctors Without Borders.
“The decision is inconsistent with the full truth and deeply offensive,” World Central Kitchen wrote on its website, disagreeing with the statement by the Israeli forces.
Israel “knew that our team in Gaza was unarmed,” said the non-profit, which provides people in need with fresh food. “The military investigation conflates different timelines and events, muddies the story and shifts the blame for the [Israeli army’s] illegal conduct.”
Australia on Thursday summoned Israel’s ambassador over the decision not to pursue criminal proceedings over the World Central Kitchen killings. Australian national Zomi Frankcom was among those killed.
Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the decision “falls far short of the accountability we expect”, adding that Australia was “outraged” by it.
In April 2024, seven international aid workers and a Palestinian driver were killed by three Israeli air strikes, despite driving in clearly marked cars and sharing their coordinates with the Israeli army.
An Al Jazeera investigation revealed the killings were intentional, directly opposing statements by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that described the targeting as “unintentional”.

980c2564ef55f7ab3d3dba75.title: Healey ‘risks £11bn Budget black hole’ from Iran war
980c2564ef55f7ab3d3dba75.author: Szu Ping Chan
980c2564ef55f7ab3d3dba75.content:
![John Healey](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000496021634_17871419724851_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqLoH7NlioJUgvNGxc7kNJh_4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![John Healey](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000496021634_17871419724851_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqLoH7NlioJUgvNGxc7kNJh_4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
John Healey will have to plug a black hole of up to £11bn in his maiden Budget if Donald Trump escalates his war in Iran, economists have warned.
French bank Societe Generale (Soc Gen) said a major energy price shock would drive up inflation and more than wipe out the Chancellor’s breathing space to balance the books.
In a worst-case scenario based on the Office for Budget Responsibility’s (OBR) modelling, the Chancellor would face a £35bn hit if he failed to water down public spending plans in the face of intensifying conflict.
This would more than wipe out the £24bn of headroom left by Mr Healey’s predecessor, Rachel Reeves.
Such a blow would stem from surging inflation, the bank said, with its forecasts based on an extreme scenario of oil surging past $150 a barrel.
Not only would this drive up fuel bills, but it would also weaken spending plans across Whitehall.
That is because budgets for each government department are set in cash terms, meaning higher inflation erodes their value.
Mr Healey could face demands for billions of pounds to top up existing spending plans, even before accounting for extra pressures on health, social care and defence budgets.
Sam Cartwright, of Soc Gen, warned that the fiscal backdrop was already “constrained” without escalation in the Middle East.
He said: “Even before any policy announcements, fiscal headroom at the autumn Budget could be £11.5bn lower than projected in March, owing to the US-Iran conflict weighing on growth and pushing up interest rates.
“If the Iran-US situation improves, the deterioration in headroom could be as little as £5bn, but could rise to around £20bn to £35bn if it worsens.”
Concerns about the effect of a prolonged war in Iran and governments’ commitment to reducing debt have triggered a sell-off in global bonds.
Mr Trump has said the US had no plans to restart peace talks with Iran after ruling out extending a 60-day ceasefire agreement that expired on Monday.
The Financial Times also reported that Tehran could target US military sites across Europe if Mr Trump escalates the war, a move that would mark a new deadly phase in a conflict that has continued for five months.
Andy Burnham has already been warned that Britain’s economy will grind to a halt if the war rages on.
Officials at the Treasury have told the Prime Minister that the economy will grow by just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked for the rest of this year.
That is far lower than the 1.6pc projection by the OBR in March, before the escalation of the Middle East conflict.
Mr Cartwright, at Soc Gen, also warned Mr Burnham against further increases in public spending.
Both the Chancellor and Prime Minister have signalled they will seek to maximise the flexibility in the fiscal rules, which require them to balance the books on day-to-day spending and bring down debt as a share of the economy.
However, the bank said borrowing £10bn a year more for investment would pile further pressure on government bonds and inflation, limiting the scope for the Bank of England to cut interest rates.
Higher interest rates would spell more pain for households, with many mortgages tied to the Bank’s base rate.
However, faster-than-expected wage growth could also hand Mr Healey a £10bn windfall as the Treasury is boosted by a freeze in income tax thresholds.
It also emerged on Wednesday that almost half of British households want lower personal taxes, even if it means less government spending, according to a poll by Ipsos.
By contrast, just under a third of respondents backed higher spending on public services if it meant they have to hand over more money to the taxman.
It represents a stark reversal of opinion for the Labour government, which has spent the past two years implementing tax and spend policies.
It leaves a challenge for Mr Burnham and Mr Healey, as they seek to identify ways to fund their expensive spending plans at October’s Budget.
Sir Mel Stride, the shadow chancellor, said people’s patience “is rightly wearing thin with Labour taking more and more of their money to spend on welfare”.
“Reeves and Starmer hiked tens of billions of pounds of taxes on working people and businesses, and Healey and Burnham look set to do the same,” he said.
Reform’s Robert Jenrick added: “The British public are sending Labour a very clear message.
“Unsurprisingly, they want lower taxes, not more of their hard-earned money being wasted on illegal migrants, net zero stupidity and a soaring benefits bill.”
980c2564ef55f7ab3d3dba75.summary: Economists warn that John Healey could face an £11bn black hole in his maiden Budget if conflict involving the US and Iran escalates, potentially wiping out his fiscal headroom. A severe energy price shock and surging inflation could severely constrain government spending plans and weaken the broader economy. Meanwhile, polling indicates that nearly half of British households favor lower personal taxes over increased government spending.
key_points: Soc Gen warned that an escalated US-Iran conflict could reduce fiscal headroom by up to £11.5bn, potentially rising to £35bn in a worst-case scenario.
Treasury officials warned the Prime Minister that economic growth could drop to 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked.
Faster-than-expected wage growth and frozen income tax thresholds could provide the Treasury with a £10bn windfall.
An Ipsos poll showed that nearly half of British households want lower personal taxes even if it reduces government spending.

e485b78b7be4b9411ff01f3e.title: 'Subnautica Began With a Love for the Ocean' — Subnautica 2 Dev Makes $100,000 Donation to Ocean Cleanup Charity as It Releases 1.2 Patch
e485b78b7be4b9411ff01f3e.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
e485b78b7be4b9411ff01f3e.content:
Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 is out now, adding the Buddy System to the underwater survival and crafting game.
Developer Unknown Worlds has also announced a $100,000 donation to the appropriately named ocean cleanup non-profit The Ocean Cleanup.
Unknown Worlds previously donated a portion of proceeds from the original Subnautica to The Ocean Cleanup on World Environment Day in 2019, and has continued to support ocean conservation efforts since.
“Subnautica began with a love for the ocean, and it means a great deal to continue the conservation work we started with the original game through this donation to The Ocean Cleanup,” said executive producer Fernando Melo. “We will keep doing our part to protect the ocean we have spent so long bringing to life.”
Unknown Worlds spoke about what to expect from Subnautica 1.2 yesterday, but today's release of the update brings with it detailed patch notes, below, which include a long list of changes and fixes.
1.2 includes the first iteration of Subnautica 2 proximity chat via an in-game voice chat option that you can use with your friends to talk locally with each other. As you get farther away it will switch to a radio-sounding voice that will progressively break up to a point where you can almost not hear your friend.
Also added is player emotes via a small menu that lets players cheer on their friends, clap, or tell them you’re a little annoyed or frustrated. Inventory sharing lets players walk up to another player, access their inventory and quickly swap items between one another, rather than having to drop inventory items out in the world and have them pick them up. Player revives are also added, so if your friend is downed for whatever reason, you’ll have some time to share some oxygen with them and bring them back to life.
Two additional player characters (Grace and Jegna) are added alongside two new suit colors. Also included is the tracking tag, a short-range beacon you can throw out in the environment or put inside an inventory such as a portable locker, so if you ever leave it in a cave you can find your way back to it. If you die holding a tracking tag or have one in your inventory, it will extend your black box signal to help you find the stuff you left behind.
Improved HUD icons means all the icons will not be at full scale by default, but when you mouse over them after a half second or so they will scale up and give you the full details. Alongside that, there are improved pinned recipes, which means the UI should feel a little less confusing, and improvements to the base builder tool that should help make it clearer when you can and can't build something.
The Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 update patch notes, courtesy of Steam, are below:
Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 patch notes
Gameplay
- 🤿Added Cross-Platform Voice Chat. Multiplayer host can choose between Global and Proximity Voice Chat (as players get further away, they become harder to hear). Voice Chat is available as “always on,” “push to talk,” or “always off.”
- Tracking Tag added to the game. Can be placed in carryables (like a locker) as a short-range beacon. If present in hand or inventory when reprinting, will increase black box range.
- Players can now revive each other before reprinting. Revived players will keep their equipment and regain a small amount of oxygen. Downed players can also choose to immediately reprint and respawn back at their assigned Biobed.
- Added Wave, Clap, Thumbs Up, Thumbs Down, and Frustrated emotes. Emotes are selectable from a new radial menu. Triggerable in water or on land, and can be interrupted by gameplay input.
- 🤿Players can now interact with each other to directly exchange inventory items.
- Added Jegna and Grace character options in Character Customization, as well as two new color schemes for characters.
- Interaction text on Upgrade Biobeds changed to clarify their use.
- Added a distinct beep to player upgrade spots within a small radius.
- Added a small flash to screen on Upgrade Biobeds.
Fauna & Flora
- Added flinch animations and VFX to Marrowbreach, Hammerhead, Nibbler, Needlershark, Epicurean, and Twin Eel.
- Adjusted Bulletheads so they deal more damage but can now be dodged (...sometimes).
- Added more Coral Crab animations.
- Revised model and animations for the Bloom Parasite.
- Improved Jelly Ring tentacles.
Resources
- More Carryable Racks added to early game wrecks and human-made sites.
Base Building
- 🤿Improvements made to the base building system’s placement UI, including alignment guide lines.
- Improvements made to how the game handles Move mode for clients in a multiplayer session.
- Updated Tadpole Dock icon to reflect updated model.
- Base edits now account for size snapping, such that it’s possible to fully deconstruct a room with Shrink (among other things).
- Trashcan is now functional as a trashcan. Items added to trashcan will be destroyed one by one after a short, five second delay.
- Bases can no longer be built inside of Great Jaw.
- Items that are preventing an object from being built are displayed in a list.
Vehicles, Tools & Equipment
- Changed Feedback Resonator’s interaction with creatures to stun them instead of causing them to flee.
- Extended duration of the Sonic Resonator creature stun to 10 seconds.
- Sources for Acid now appear as green dots in the Scanner HUD.
- Repair Tool now unlocks after two scans.
- Tadpoles that are destroyed outside of the Early Access fence teleport inside of the Early Access fence so that they can be recovered.
Menus & UI
- Signals adjusted to increase clarity and reduce HUD clutter. Icons get larger as player gets closer, and text will appear on hover for signals further away.
- Save Codes can now be directly pasted into the Cloud Save Download input box.
- Builder menu’s scroll position persists when closing and re-opening the menu.
- Pinned recipes highlight when the player acquires resources relevant to those recipes.
- Items shown in Pinned Recipes are no longer dimmed, to improve readability.
- Improved error language for errors specific to non-Game Pass Microsoft users.
- Audiologs show elapsed and remaining playback time.
Art & Visual FX
- VFX performance improvements to the Graveyard and its Water Slugs, for the players who collect hundreds of Water Slugs.
- Tallshrooms now have an icon in the Scanner HUD.
- Added impact VFX for Tongue Thief.
- Light poles connecting Observatory and Rosetta Stone added.
- Removed odd blue outline that was sometimes visible on Collector Leviathan.
- Improved consistency of sparks VFX across the game.
- Improved consistency of electricity VFX across the game.
- Added shock VFX for Hammerheads impacting objects.
- Added more environmental effects to abandoned outposts and wrecks.
Voice & Narrative
- Previously unlocalized lines are now localized.
- Naming of Carryable Racks is now consistent across the game, instead of sometimes being “Wall Rack” or “Hardpoint.”
- Reduced frequency of NOA alerts.
- Adjusted Welcome Center message in Spanish and Italian.
- Adjusted pacing of dialog to better match the actions occurring during the recordings.
- Added Databank entry for Mod Station.
- Added Databank entries for audiologs that were missing them.
- Further refinements to voice over prioritization, so the most important lines are heard.
Music & SFX
- Music added to Tufa Zona, Thermal Area, and North Coral Gardens.
Miscellaneous
- New Privacy Policy additions from July 15th will pop up on first play.
- New Frame Generation modes 5x and 6x (RTX 5000 series) added.
- New Dynamic Frame Generation added. Will automatically select the appropriate Frame Generation mode to get a good performance (RTX 5000 series).
- VSync and DLSS Frame Generation can be turned on at the same time.
- Added description for Nvidia Reflex in Settings.
- Reorganized order of volume sliders.
- The in-game Feedback Tool now allows attaching a save file.
Bug Fixes

1143d1a2c453e017f865ff13.title: 'Subnautica Began With a Love for the Ocean' — Subnautica 2 Dev Makes $100,000 Donation to Ocean Cleanup Charity as It Releases 1.2 Patch
1143d1a2c453e017f865ff13.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
1143d1a2c453e017f865ff13.content:
Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 is out now, adding the Buddy System to the underwater survival and crafting game.
Developer Unknown Worlds has also announced a $100,000 donation to the appropriately named ocean cleanup non-profit The Ocean Cleanup.
Unknown Worlds previously donated a portion of proceeds from the original Subnautica to The Ocean Cleanup on World Environment Day in 2019, and has continued to support ocean conservation efforts since.
“Subnautica began with a love for the ocean, and it means a great deal to continue the conservation work we started with the original game through this donation to The Ocean Cleanup,” said executive producer Fernando Melo. “We will keep doing our part to protect the ocean we have spent so long bringing to life.”
Unknown Worlds spoke about what to expect from Subnautica 1.2 yesterday, but today's release of the update brings with it detailed patch notes, below, which include a long list of changes and fixes.
1.2 includes the first iteration of Subnautica 2 proximity chat via an in-game voice chat option that you can use with your friends to talk locally with each other. As you get farther away it will switch to a radio-sounding voice that will progressively break up to a point where you can almost not hear your friend.
Also added is player emotes via a small menu that lets players cheer on their friends, clap, or tell them you’re a little annoyed or frustrated. Inventory sharing lets players walk up to another player, access their inventory and quickly swap items between one another, rather than having to drop inventory items out in the world and have them pick them up. Player revives are also added, so if your friend is downed for whatever reason, you’ll have some time to share some oxygen with them and bring them back to life.
Two additional player characters (Grace and Jegna) are added alongside two new suit colors. Also included is the tracking tag, a short-range beacon you can throw out in the environment or put inside an inventory such as a portable locker, so if you ever leave it in a cave you can find your way back to it. If you die holding a tracking tag or have one in your inventory, it will extend your black box signal to help you find the stuff you left behind.
Improved HUD icons means all the icons will not be at full scale by default, but when you mouse over them after a half second or so they will scale up and give you the full details. Alongside that, there are improved pinned recipes, which means the UI should feel a little less confusing, and improvements to the base builder tool that should help make it clearer when you can and can't build something.
The Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 update patch notes, courtesy of Steam, are below:
Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 patch notes
Gameplay
- 🤿Added Cross-Platform Voice Chat. Multiplayer host can choose between Global and Proximity Voice Chat (as players get further away, they become harder to hear). Voice Chat is available as “always on,” “push to talk,” or “always off.”
- Tracking Tag added to the game. Can be placed in carryables (like a locker) as a short-range beacon. If present in hand or inventory when reprinting, will increase black box range.
- Players can now revive each other before reprinting. Revived players will keep their equipment and regain a small amount of oxygen. Downed players can also choose to immediately reprint and respawn back at their assigned Biobed.
- Added Wave, Clap, Thumbs Up, Thumbs Down, and Frustrated emotes. Emotes are selectable from a new radial menu. Triggerable in water or on land, and can be interrupted by gameplay input.
- 🤿Players can now interact with each other to directly exchange inventory items.
- Added Jegna and Grace character options in Character Customization, as well as two new color schemes for characters.
- Interaction text on Upgrade Biobeds changed to clarify their use.
- Added a distinct beep to player upgrade spots within a small radius.
- Added a small flash to screen on Upgrade Biobeds.
Fauna & Flora
- Added flinch animations and VFX to Marrowbreach, Hammerhead, Nibbler, Needlershark, Epicurean, and Twin Eel.
- Adjusted Bulletheads so they deal more damage but can now be dodged (...sometimes).
- Added more Coral Crab animations.
- Revised model and animations for the Bloom Parasite.
- Improved Jelly Ring tentacles.
Resources
- More Carryable Racks added to early game wrecks and human-made sites.
Base Building
- 🤿Improvements made to the base building system’s placement UI, including alignment guide lines.
- Improvements made to how the game handles Move mode for clients in a multiplayer session.
- Updated Tadpole Dock icon to reflect updated model.
- Base edits now account for size snapping, such that it’s possible to fully deconstruct a room with Shrink (among other things).
- Trashcan is now functional as a trashcan. Items added to trashcan will be destroyed one by one after a short, five second delay.
- Bases can no longer be built inside of Great Jaw.
- Items that are preventing an object from being built are displayed in a list.
Vehicles, Tools & Equipment
- Changed Feedback Resonator’s interaction with creatures to stun them instead of causing them to flee.
- Extended duration of the Sonic Resonator creature stun to 10 seconds.
- Sources for Acid now appear as green dots in the Scanner HUD.
- Repair Tool now unlocks after two scans.
- Tadpoles that are destroyed outside of the Early Access fence teleport inside of the Early Access fence so that they can be recovered.
Menus & UI
- Signals adjusted to increase clarity and reduce HUD clutter. Icons get larger as player gets closer, and text will appear on hover for signals further away.
- Save Codes can now be directly pasted into the Cloud Save Download input box.
- Builder menu’s scroll position persists when closing and re-opening the menu.
- Pinned recipes highlight when the player acquires resources relevant to those recipes.
- Items shown in Pinned Recipes are no longer dimmed, to improve readability.
- Improved error language for errors specific to non-Game Pass Microsoft users.
- Audiologs show elapsed and remaining playback time.
Art & Visual FX
- VFX performance improvements to the Graveyard and its Water Slugs, for the players who collect hundreds of Water Slugs.
- Tallshrooms now have an icon in the Scanner HUD.
- Added impact VFX for Tongue Thief.
- Light poles connecting Observatory and Rosetta Stone added.
- Removed odd blue outline that was sometimes visible on Collector Leviathan.
- Improved consistency of sparks VFX across the game.
- Improved consistency of electricity VFX across the game.
- Added shock VFX for Hammerheads impacting objects.
- Added more environmental effects to abandoned outposts and wrecks.
Voice & Narrative
- Previously unlocalized lines are now localized.
- Naming of Carryable Racks is now consistent across the game, instead of sometimes being “Wall Rack” or “Hardpoint.”
- Reduced frequency of NOA alerts.
- Adjusted Welcome Center message in Spanish and Italian.
- Adjusted pacing of dialog to better match the actions occurring during the recordings.
- Added Databank entry for Mod Station.
- Added Databank entries for audiologs that were missing them.
- Further refinements to voice over prioritization, so the most important lines are heard.
Music & SFX
- Music added to Tufa Zona, Thermal Area, and North Coral Gardens.
Miscellaneous
- New Privacy Policy additions from July 15th will pop up on first play.
- New Frame Generation modes 5x and 6x (RTX 5000 series) added.
- New Dynamic Frame Generation added. Will automatically select the appropriate Frame Generation mode to get a good performance (RTX 5000 series).
- VSync and DLSS Frame Generation can be turned on at the same time.
- Added description for Nvidia Reflex in Settings.
- Reorganized order of volume sliders.
- The in-game Feedback Tool now allows attaching a save file.
Bug Fixes
- Fixed Collector Leviathan performing a 360 spin whenever it grabs or throws a Tadpole.
- Fixed an issue where settings menus would sometimes become cut-off while navigating with controller/gamepad.
- 🤿Fixed an exploit where swapping the resource in an occupied Metal Farm caused the new resource to inherit the growth time of the previous resource.
- 🤿Fixed an issue where opened Angel Combs’ cankers could incorrectly appear closed after a game update.
- Pausing the game while sprinting no longer causes the player to permanently sprint.
- Fixed some Axum/Tailings furniture being buildable outside of the player’s base, which caused multiple knock-on problems.
- Tadpole can no longer be docked when there is insufficient space for it, resolving an issue where the Tadpole could become stuck in its dock.
- 🤿Additional fixes to the tool prompts to account for accuracy and recipe-sharing between players in a multiplayer session.
- Fixed Power Transmitter ray visibility and overall appearance, particularly for multiplayer clients who alternately saw extra rays or had rays that should be there disappear.
- 🤿Fixed Hydroturbines stopping their power production after 120-160 mins of gameplay, after the player swam away from them, and for their turbines to stop spinning, even when producing power.
- Fixed music playing in the incorrect region or not playing at all in intended areas.
- Fixed a soft lock where using Unstuck during the Lifepod launch cutscene would cause the player to teleport back to the Deep Start awakening room after the cutscene.
- Fixed an issue where pressing the spacebar during the TOS skipped the step of agreeing to it.
- Fixed an issue where the Collector Leviathan would release a captured player if the Camouflage Biomod activated during the eating scene.
- Fixed an issue where chassis signals could remain visible on screen even when the chassis is equipped to the Tadpole.

Alongside the game update, the studio announced a $100,000 donation to ocean cleanup non-profit The Ocean Cleanup to support ongoing conservation efforts. The Early Access 1.2 update adds proximity voice chat, inventory sharing, and player revives for multiplayer.
The patch introduces new character options, suit colors, and emotes accessible via a radial menu.
Various quality-of-life improvements were made to base building, HUD icons, and pinned recipes.

b9dbd69d4530a2d8cb7388a2.title: Martin O'Neill not fooled by Celtic score as he hails 'real bargain' and reveals player set for scan
b9dbd69d4530a2d8cb7388a2.author: Alan Pattullo
b9dbd69d4530a2d8cb7388a2.content:
Martin O'Neill not fooled by Celtic score as he hails 'real bargain' and reveals player set for scan
O’Neil reserves praise for several Celtic stars after 3-0 win over LASK
Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed his side’s performance against LASK but stressed the tie was “still in the balance” despite what sounds like a comprehensive 3-0 first-leg victory.
Three high-quality goals have put Celtic in a good position ahead of next week’s second leg in Austria. But O’Neill believes Celtic can still improve and they might have to in order to keep LASK at bay and secure the estimated £40 million windfall for clinching a return to the Champions League.
Celtic survived some shaky moments in the opening stages. LASK had a goal ruled offside and also wasted another golden chance before a bravura performance from Camilo Duran took the game away from the visitors. The Colombian struck twice after Benjamin Nygren opened the scoring on 26 minutes. “He has paid for his ticket now, it’s only his fourth game,” smiled O’Neill, referring to Duran. The forward was signed for around £6 million including add-ons from Qarabag of Azerbaijan earlier this summer. “It’s not an awful lot of money when you consider some of the fees talked about for the Premier League," noted O'Neill. "He has been a real bargain."
![Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring to make it 3-0 over LASK in the Champions League play-off first leg at Celtic Park.  (Photo by Rob Casey / SNS Group)](https://www.scotsman.com/jpim-static/image/2026/08/19/22/29/21766947.jpg?trim=0,158,0,158&crop=&width=640&quality=65)
![placeholder image](https://www.scotsman.com/img/placeholder.jpg)
O’Neill described the opening half as “like a basketball game” with LASK passing up other good opportunities to score. “We rode our luck a little bit,” he admitted.
But having steadied themselves, Celtic took confidence from two exquisite finishes from Nygren and Duran to take a commanding 2-0 lead. Duran scored another fine goal - after exchanging passes with Nygren - midway through the second half to put Celtic in the Champions League driving seat. O’Neill, however, is taking nothing for granted.
“They (LASK) started the brighter, it took us time to get going," he said. "But when we did we scored a great goal from Nygren to take a bit of the pressure off, and give us the lead. And then Duran’s two goals were fantastic. But the game is absolutely in the balance.”
O’Neill is not fooled by the handsome first-leg lead. “I didn’t have to say it to the players in the dressing room,” he said. “They absolutely know. I think we are capable of scoring (over there) which we might need to do.
“I am not playing it down at all,” he added. “We are a long way away, genuinely. Next Tuesday will be a big test for us.
“Our goals were fantastic, good enough to win any football match,” he added. “But there is a long way to go yet.”
![Celtic's Camilo Duran (L) with Manager Martin O'Neill (R) as he is substituted during the 3-0 win over LASK in the Champions League play-off first leg at Celtic Park. (Photo by Rob Casey / SNS Group)](https://www.scotsman.com/jpim-static/image/2026/08/19/22/02/21767006.jpeg?trim=0,16,0,15&crop=&width=640&quality=65)
![placeholder image](https://www.scotsman.com/img/placeholder.jpg)
O’Neill described Duran as “exceptional”. He noted his willingness to track back to help 19-year-old right back Colby Donovan, who was also superb. “He (Duran) has been fantastic for us since he arrived at this football club,” said O’Neill. “His goals were terrific, his play was great, his running back, helping Colby out on a number of occasions. It was a magnificent performance. If he stays clear of injury, he is going to be a really, really good player.”
O’Neill also praised Nygren’s performance. The Swede has now scored in every game so far this season. “His form since the start of the season has been terrific, he was brilliant for us tonight,” said the manager.
O’Neill still believes Celtic can improve, in terms of fitness as much as anything. “We had to be at it every single minute, overall we defended strongly,” he said. “(Viljami) Sinisalo was great – he made a big save for us at 2-0. If it goes 2-1 they are in the ascendancy at that stage.”
The teenage Donovan also caught the eye at right back in front of the watching new Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli. “He did brilliantly, he did great,” said O’Neill. “He has a really big heart and that is nice to see. He is a local lad too and loves it, he loves the football club and loves playing. His enthusiasm is boundless and he stuck to his task brilliantly.”
Donovan is standing in for the injured Alistair Johnston, who O’Neill revealed is due to have a scan on Thursday for the leg muscle injury sustained against Kilmarnock two weekends ago. “By the time I meet up with you again, we should have an idea (how long he will be out),” he said.

b9dbd69d4530a2d8cb7388a2.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill warned that their 3-0 Champions League play-off first-leg win over LASK is still in the balance ahead of the return leg in Austria. Despite early scares where LASK missed several chances, goals from Benjamin Nygren and a brace from summer signing Camilo Duran secured the commanding victory. O'Neill praised Duran as a real bargain and highlighted strong performances from teenager Colby Donovan and goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo. Additionally, the manager revealed that injured right-back Alistair Johnston is set to undergo a scan on a leg muscle injury.
key_points: Celtic defeated LASK 3-0 in the Champions League play-off first leg thanks to goals from Benjamin Nygren and two from Camilo Duran.
Manager Martin O'Neill insisted the tie remains in the balance despite the comfortable scoreline, warning that next week's second leg in Austria will be a big test.
O'Neill hailed summer signing Duran as a 'real bargain' following his £6 million transfer from Qarabag.
Teenage right-back Colby Donovan and goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo received praise from the manager for their strong performances.
O'Neill revealed that injured defender Alistair Johnston is scheduled for a scan on a leg muscle injury on Thursday.

The teenage Donovan also caught the eye at right back in front of the watching new Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli. “He did brilliantly, he did great,” said O’Neill. “He has a really big heart and that is nice to see. He is a local lad too and loves it, he loves the football club and loves playing. His enthusiasm is boundless and he stuck to his task brilliantly.”
Donovan is standing in for the injured Alistair Johnston, who O’Neill revealed is due to have a scan on Thursday for the leg muscle injury sustained against Kilmarnock two weekends ago. “By the time I meet up with you again, we should have an idea (how long he will be out),” he said.

7726777897569b7510e4ade1.title: “I started screaming because I know what shelling looks like,” dolphin photographed performing extremely rare behavior
7726777897569b7510e4ade1.author: Mike Harris
7726777897569b7510e4ade1.content:
![Dolphin engaged in shelling behavior](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/nyAvAVJ2DKaRtMRErD5mUB.jpg) 
In a world where many creatives are facing an increasingly uncertain future, it’s nice to be reminded that – in many cases – traditional photography is still as vital as ever.
And while scientific research might not be the first thing that comes to mind, I am constantly reporting on the craft’s role in documenting rare wildlife encounters.
A recent interaction between researchers from the University of the Sunshine Coast and bottlenose dolphins is a prime example.
The encounter happened at Queensland Australia’s Great Sandy Marine Park, between July and October 2025, where a research team led by Dr Alexis Levengood captured imagery of a behavior known as 'shelling'.
The behavior is so rare that it's only been published once before, but this is the first time it's been officially recorded on the east coast of Australia.
According to Dr Levengood, “we spotted a dolphin raising something large out of the water. I started screaming because I know what shelling looks like”.
 ![Dolphin engaged in shelling behavior](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Eb6PABS4jTeU2cLubc29TD.jpg) 
The animal behavioralist and marine mammal expert explained that the dolphins use 'shelling' to hunt for fish; the shell becomes an implement in which to trap prey. The mammals then shake the makeshift tool on the surface until their prize slides into their jaws.
The best camera deals, reviews, product advice, and unmissable photography news, direct to your inbox!
I'm no marine life expert, but I am an avid wildlife lover and I certainly had no idea that dolphins did this.
To make matters even more interesting, the researchers observed both an adult female and its calf engaging in the behavior, leading them to deduce that the juvenile had learned from its mother.
“Our footage provides the first potential evidence of maternal social transmission – a process by which offspring learn behaviour by observing the actions of its mother,” said Dr Levengood. “It challenges the belief that dolphins learn this tool use from their peers.”
In a world of hobbyist and professional photographers aiming to capture the very best photos possible, it can be easy to forget that imaging is also used purely for surveillance, observation and documentation.
It’s not about capturing an attractive image, it’s about clearly capturing the moment for posterity.
If you’re a wildlife enthusiast first and a photographer second, and are looking for a camera to complement your bird or wildlife-watching setup, I’d buy this monster $1000 all-in-one bridge camera.

![Mike Harris](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GGEXGwupYYYnNwLb7XkXx8.jpg)
Mike studied photography at college, honing his Adobe Photoshop skills and learning to work in the studio and darkroom. After a few years writing for various publications, he headed to the ‘Big Smoke’ to work on Wex Photo Video’s award-winning content team, before transitioning back to print as Technique Editor (later Deputy Editor) on N-Photo: The Nikon Magazine.
With bylines in Digital Camera, PhotoPlus: The Canon Magazine, Practical Photography, Digital Photographer, iMore, and TechRadar, he’s a fountain of photography and consumer tech knowledge, making him a top tutor for techniques on cameras, lenses, tripods, filters, and more. His expertise extends to everything from portraits and landscapes to abstracts and architecture to wildlife and, yes, fast things going around race tracks...
