9fb3b1c414f3668f4b384f76.title: Gears of War: E-Day and Gibson Unite for a Custom Guitar Collection
9fb3b1c414f3668f4b384f76.author: Danielle Partis; XBOX Wire Editor
9fb3b1c414f3668f4b384f76.content:
As we count down to the launch of Gears of War: E-Day, Gibson Guitars and The Coalition are teaming up with a one-of-a-kind collaboration that brings together two legendary brands built on craftsmanship, authenticity, and storytelling.
The collaboration is a natural extension of Gears’ musical identity. Guitar-driven scores have helped define the franchise for nearly two decades, and Gears of War: E-Day composer Adam Lastiwka used Gibson guitars in the recording of the game’s soundtrack.
Inspired by the enduring brotherhood at the heart of Gears, the collection features two custom Gibson guitars based on the iconic Les Paul and SG designs. Created exclusively for Gears of War: E-Day, the guitars honor franchise heroes Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago through striking original artwork from acclaimed artist and illustrator Luke Preece.
“These guitars feel like the culmination of a years-long creative collaboration with Luke, who has been part of Gears of War: E-Day from the very beginning,” says Studio Brand Director Nicole Fawcette. “He loves Gears of War as much as we do, and he has a gift for translating the spirit of the franchise into striking art that makes you feel something.”
For artist Luke Preece, the project was a natural fit. “It brought together everything I love – music, metal, guitars, video games, art, and Gears of War,” he says. “All of those influences found their way into the guitars, so the collaboration felt completely natural.”
That sense of shared creative direction shaped the collaboration from the start. “Nicole and I had already established the visual language for E-Day, and we had a clear plan,” Preece adds. “We work well together and are usually on the same page, which gave us the freedom to focus on making the designs as strong as possible.”
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Spare-inline-164d65160610516cac79-1024x576.jpg)
Crafted for Brotherhood
Each guitar began as a hand-drawn concept before being digitally mapped, carefully stenciled, and meticulously hand-painted by Preece. Every detail was designed to capture the spirit of Gears through the lens of two of its most beloved characters.
The collection draws inspiration from two of the games “Emotional Core” pillars, Brutality and Pathos, ideas that reflect both the grit and sacrifice woven throughout the story of Gears of War: E-Day.
“What I love most about Luke’s work is his ability to communicate big, loud, bold ideas,” Fawcette says. “Rather than simply illustrating Marcus and Dom, we had the opportunity to distill their themes and energy into something iconic.”
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Marcus-LP-4d70589545554c8a51bd-1024x576.jpg)
Marcus Fenix | Brutality
Represented on Gibson’s legendary Les Paul, Marcus’ guitar embodies the grit, determination, and relentless spirit that have defined the character for nearly two decades.
At the center sits a weathered skull against a COG Tag backdrop, framed by the unmistakable blades of a chainsaw. Splashes of Locust blood and fractured textures evoke the chaos of Emergence Day and the world-shattering events that changed Sera forever. The result is a bold, aggressive design that celebrates one of gaming’s most iconic heroes while paying tribute to the franchise’s signature imagery.
“Marcus’ Les Paul was the hardest to solve. The hardware interrupted some of the original ideas, so we leaned into the circular saw-blade motif. It gave the piece the aggressive, brutal energy we wanted, and the shape fit the body of the guitar perfectly,” says Preece.
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Dom-SG-4fc8981bb05df225bb8c-1024x576.jpg)
Dominic Santiago | Pathos
Dominic Santiago’s design finds its home on the equally iconic Gibson SG, delivering a more somber and reflective counterpart.
A tearful, battle-worn skull stands against a COG Tag surrounded by barbed wire and vibrant crimson poppies, a powerful symbol of remembrance woven throughout Gears lore. The artwork reflects Dom’s unwavering loyalty, personal sacrifice, and the emotional weight carried by one of the franchise’s most beloved characters.
“Dom’s design came together more naturally through its symbolism,” says Preece. “The wings flowed beautifully with the shape of the SG and connected with the pathos of his story, including the angelic imagery associated with Maria.”
Together, the guitars tell a story of brotherhood, resilience, loss, and fate, themes that remain central to the world of Gears of War.
“Early on, we considered physically distressing the guitars to make them feel battle-worn,” says Fawcette. “In the end, I’m glad we preserved the beauty of the instruments and allowed the artwork itself to carry the weight and intensity.”
See the Guitars at Gamescom
“We can’t wait for fans to see these in-person,” says Fawcette. “Each guitar is already a beautiful object, and Luke’s hand-painted Gears artwork transforms it into something visually stunning – a genuine work of art that feels cool, heavy, and unmistakably Gears.”
Fans attending Gamescom 2026 in Cologne, Germany will be among the first to see the collection in person when they make their public debut at the XBOX booth.
Says Preece, “Only four guitars were made. Each is numbered and signed, and because they were painted by hand, even the repeated designs are not exact copies. Every instrument is a unique, one-of-one piece.”
Win a Piece of the Brotherhood
Starting today, fans can enter for a chance to win three custom guitars in total: two Marcus Fenix-inspired Les Pauls and one Dominic Santiago-inspired SG.

456fa873872552dfc5dc935a.title: Gears of War: E-Day and Gibson Unite for a Custom Guitar Collection
456fa873872552dfc5dc935a.author: Danielle Partis; XBOX Wire Editor
456fa873872552dfc5dc935a.content:
As we count down to the launch of Gears of War: E-Day, Gibson Guitars and The Coalition are teaming up with a one-of-a-kind collaboration that brings together two legendary brands built on craftsmanship, authenticity, and storytelling.
The collaboration is a natural extension of Gears’ musical identity. Guitar-driven scores have helped define the franchise for nearly two decades, and Gears of War: E-Day composer Adam Lastiwka used Gibson guitars in the recording of the game’s soundtrack.
Inspired by the enduring brotherhood at the heart of Gears, the collection features two custom Gibson guitars based on the iconic Les Paul and SG designs. Created exclusively for Gears of War: E-Day, the guitars honor franchise heroes Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago through striking original artwork from acclaimed artist and illustrator Luke Preece.
“These guitars feel like the culmination of a years-long creative collaboration with Luke, who has been part of Gears of War: E-Day from the very beginning,” says Studio Brand Director Nicole Fawcette. “He loves Gears of War as much as we do, and he has a gift for translating the spirit of the franchise into striking art that makes you feel something.”
For artist Luke Preece, the project was a natural fit. “It brought together everything I love – music, metal, guitars, video games, art, and Gears of War,” he says. “All of those influences found their way into the guitars, so the collaboration felt completely natural.”
That sense of shared creative direction shaped the collaboration from the start. “Nicole and I had already established the visual language for E-Day, and we had a clear plan,” Preece adds. “We work well together and are usually on the same page, which gave us the freedom to focus on making the designs as strong as possible.”
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Spare-inline-164d65160610516cac79-1024x576.jpg)
Crafted for Brotherhood
Each guitar began as a hand-drawn concept before being digitally mapped, carefully stenciled, and meticulously hand-painted by Preece. Every detail was designed to capture the spirit of Gears through the lens of two of its most beloved characters.
The collection draws inspiration from two of the games “Emotional Core” pillars, Brutality and Pathos, ideas that reflect both the grit and sacrifice woven throughout the story of Gears of War: E-Day.
“What I love most about Luke’s work is his ability to communicate big, loud, bold ideas,” Fawcette says. “Rather than simply illustrating Marcus and Dom, we had the opportunity to distill their themes and energy into something iconic.”
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Marcus-LP-4d70589545554c8a51bd-1024x576.jpg)
Marcus Fenix | Brutality
Represented on Gibson’s legendary Les Paul, Marcus’ guitar embodies the grit, determination, and relentless spirit that have defined the character for nearly two decades.
At the center sits a weathered skull against a COG Tag backdrop, framed by the unmistakable blades of a chainsaw. Splashes of Locust blood and fractured textures evoke the chaos of Emergence Day and the world-shattering events that changed Sera forever. The result is a bold, aggressive design that celebrates one of gaming’s most iconic heroes while paying tribute to the franchise’s signature imagery.
“Marcus’ Les Paul was the hardest to solve. The hardware interrupted some of the original ideas, so we leaned into the circular saw-blade motif. It gave the piece the aggressive, brutal energy we wanted, and the shape fit the body of the guitar perfectly,” says Preece.
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Dom-SG-4fc8981bb05df225bb8c-1024x576.jpg)
Dominic Santiago | Pathos
Dominic Santiago’s design finds its home on the equally iconic Gibson SG, delivering a more somber and reflective counterpart.
A tearful, battle-worn skull stands against a COG Tag surrounded by barbed wire and vibrant crimson poppies, a powerful symbol of remembrance woven throughout Gears lore. The artwork reflects Dom’s unwavering loyalty, personal sacrifice, and the emotional weight carried by one of the franchise’s most beloved characters.
“Dom’s design came together more naturally through its symbolism,” says Preece. “The wings flowed beautifully with the shape of the SG and connected with the pathos of his story, including the angelic imagery associated with Maria.”
Together, the guitars tell a story of brotherhood, resilience, loss, and fate, themes that remain central to the world of Gears of War.
“Early on, we considered physically distressing the guitars to make them feel battle-worn,” says Fawcette. “In the end, I’m glad we preserved the beauty of the instruments and allowed the artwork itself to carry the weight and intensity.”
See the Guitars at Gamescom
“We can’t wait for fans to see these in-person,” says Fawcette. “Each guitar is already a beautiful object, and Luke’s hand-painted Gears artwork transforms it into something visually stunning – a genuine work of art that feels cool, heavy, and unmistakably Gears.”
Fans attending Gamescom 2026 in Cologne, Germany will be among the first to see the collection in person when they make their public debut at the XBOX booth.
Says Preece, “Only four guitars were made. Each is numbered and signed, and because they were painted by hand, even the repeated designs are not exact copies. Every instrument is a unique, one-of-one piece.”

The winners will be selected at random and announced on October 16, 2026. Check out the full rules, terms and conditions here.

35705cde8bfcc35e5ca3845f.title: Supergirl actor announces shock retirement after becoming 'fed up'
35705cde8bfcc35e5ca3845f.author: Brooke Ivey Johnson
35705cde8bfcc35e5ca3845f.content:
![David Krumholtz](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804371-fdb4-e1787130821269.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Actor David Krumholtz has revealed he is taking an indefinite break from acting after becoming ‘frustrated’ and ‘fed up’ with Hollywood.
The 48-year-old, whose career has spanned more than three decades, surprised fans when he announced he had ‘kinda sorta’ put his acting career on hold in a candid Threads post on Tuesday.
Krumholtz, who played physicist Isidor Rabi in Christopher Nolan’s Oscar-winning Oppenheimer and is also well known for The Santa Clause franchise as well as a recent role in Supergirl, admitted he had been terrified of making the decision for years.
But after finally taking the plunge, he said he was hit with an unexpected sense of relief.
‘I kinda sorta put my acting career on hold the other day,’ he wrote in the now-deleted post.
‘There was a time when being competitive and self-involved really served my pursuit. That time has passed.’
![SUPERGIRL, David Krumholtz as Zor-El, 2026. ph: Parisa Taghizadeh / ? Warner Bros. / courtesy Everett Collection](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804374-6255.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Krumholtz explained that he had long worried about what walking away from the industry could mean for him financially.
He said stepping back had ‘been something I’ve been petrified to do for years,’ admitting he feared he would ‘go broke and not be able to handle being out of the game.’
However, those fears seemingly gave way to relief once he made his decision official. ‘A huge wave of relief washed over me when I sent the definitive email,’ he continued.
‘Not sure what I’m going to do for money instead, or how I’m going to do it, but I just removed a humongous burden, one that I truly didn’t fathom the weight of until it was gone.’
![Publicity Film Still from "The Santa Clause" Tim Allen, David Krumholtz ? 1994 Walt Disney Pictures Photo Credit: Attila Dory](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804436-ae6d.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Summing up his feelings towards the profession, he added simply: ‘Frustrated, fed up, fried.’
The original announcement was subsequently deleted, but Krumholtz returned to Threads after being inundated with messages from fans and fellow actors.
He described the ‘love and encouragement’ he had received as ‘overwhelmingly surprising’ and clarified that he had not fallen out of love with acting itself.
Instead, it was the realities of pursuing it professionally that had apparently lost their appeal: ‘Acting professionally is a very different concept than the exercise of acting itself.
‘I’ve enjoyed every single minute of exercising the muscle. I’ve enjoyed the fanfare.’
He reiterated that the competitive mindset which once helped drive his career was no longer something he wanted to embrace.
![Ben Stiller and David Krumholtz](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804375-36ca.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
‘There will always be great joy in the exercise. But for me, the profession has lost its gleam,’ he said.
Despite the dramatic announcement, Krumholtz later stressed that fans should not necessarily consider his departure permanent.
Responding to fellow actor Geoffrey Blake, who told him he was ‘too good to quit’, Krumholtz clarified: ‘Not quitting entirely.’
Instead, he described his decision as ‘taking a bit of a step back and an indefinite break’.
He added that the pressures surrounding his career had left him questioning whether he might have a different purpose outside the industry.
!["Harold & Kumar Escape from Guantanamo Bay" David Krumholtz, Eddie Kaye Thomas ? 2008 New Line Cinema](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804423-d896.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
‘The stress of the moment has me wondering if there’s a higher calling to pursue,’ he wrote.
Actor Garret Dillahunt was also among those to offer his support, telling Krumholtz: ‘This is sad news for me. But I am happy for you. I understand completely.’
Krumholtz replied that his career was not necessarily ‘over,’ but that he wanted to redefine the terms on which he worked.
‘Hoping to find a new, more rewarding passion,’ he said. ‘Me, my product, and I mentality is not working anymore. I want to try to be of service. No crystal ball.’
His decision comes despite Krumholtz remaining busy on screen in recent years.
![David Krumholtz and Macaulay Culkin David Krumholtz and Macaulay Culkin at the reading of 'Spectacle, Part One of the Mark Rosen Chronicles' at the Nantucket Community School during the 10th Annual Nantucket Film Festival on June 17, 2005. Nantucket, Massachusetts Photo ? Matt Baron/BEImages](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804427-1f2b.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
After appearing in Oppenheimer in 2023, he went on to feature in 2025 Bruce Springsteen biopic Springsteen: Deliver Me from Nowhere and appeared in 2026’s Supergirl.
Krumholtz began acting as a child, landing film roles in Life with Mikey and Addams Family Values in 1993 before appearing as Bernard the elf in 1994 festive favourite The Santa Clause.
- 
	![Susanna Reid nearly unrecognisable raving at Ibiza super club](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308762990-3293.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=38px%2C0px%2C1129px%2C635px&resize=646%2C363)
- Hayden Panettiere's 'unexpected' death triggers criminal investigation
- John Cleese asks who Roman Kemp and Lauren Laverne are in toe-curling live TV moment
- Hayden Panettiere's body was 'found by boyfriend Brian Hickerson's brother'
He reprised the role in its 2002 sequel and, decades later, returned to the character for Disney series The Santa Clauses.
![Joseph Gordon-Levitt, David Krumholtz Director: Gil Junger Touchstone USA Scene Still Shakespeare Comedy](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804364-e229.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
His lengthy film CV also includes Slums of Beverly Hills, 10 Things I Hate About You, Ray, Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle, Superbad and Sausage Party.
On television, he is perhaps best known for starring as mathematician Charlie Eppes in crime drama Numb3rs, which ran for six seasons.
He has also appeared in Freaks and Geeks, ER, The Closer, Monty, Chicago Sons and The Trouble with Normal.
35705cde8bfcc35e5ca3845f.summary: Actor David Krumholtz has announced an indefinite break from acting after more than three decades in the industry, citing frustration with Hollywood's professional demands and competitive nature. Although he initially posted that he was putting his career on hold due to feeling 'fried' and 'fed up,' he later clarified that he is not quitting entirely but stepping back to find a new, more rewarding passion. Krumholtz, known for his roles in Oppenheimer, The Santa Clause, and Supergirl, expressed a strong sense of relief after making the decision.
key_points: David Krumholtz announced an indefinite break from his acting career in a candid Threads post.
The 48-year-old actor stated he became frustrated, fed up, and tired of the competitive nature of the profession.
Despite initial financial fears, Krumholtz felt an immediate wave of relief after sending the definitive email to step back.
He clarified that he has not fallen out of love with acting itself, but rather the realities of pursuing it professionally.
Krumholtz's extensive career includes roles in Oppenheimer, The Santa Clause franchise, Numb3rs, and Supergirl.

7620640e4495e6bb3caf15ca.title: Curtis Jones on verge of leaving Liverpool for Inter Milan
7620640e4495e6bb3caf15ca.author: Dominic King
7620640e4495e6bb3caf15ca.content:
![Curtis Jones of Liverpool during a training session at AXA Training Centre on August 05, 2026 in Kirkby, England](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000497509053_17871584715190_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqBsedz4LlBiBfB5cHH5CXna5vCmi6-QeyJelyftCLduc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Curtis Jones of Liverpool during a training session at AXA Training Centre on August 05, 2026 in Kirkby, England](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000497509053_17871584715190_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqBsedz4LlBiBfB5cHH5CXna5vCmi6-QeyJelyftCLduc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Curtis Jones is on the verge of ending his Liverpool career after Inter Milan returned with a £30m package that shows they want to do business.
Inter have been pursuing the England midfielder for much of 2026 but looked to have blown their chances of doing a deal earlier this summer when they offered £21m, knowing that Liverpool had a valuation of £35m.
It was their second attempt to sign Jones but once Liverpool had rejected it, it seemed likely that he would stay to see out the remaining 12 months of his contract. The Anfield club were relaxed that his deal running down would not see him lose focus.
There was an incident, though, during Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US when Jones was involved in a row on the pitch with Dominik Szoboszlai and Kostas Tsimikas over the captaincy following a 1-0 win over Wrexham in New York.
Jones swiftly apologised for his actions, posting a statement on Instagram, but it was the kind of episode that indicated it would be better if there were a parting of ways. It is well known that he wants to join Inter and relishes the chance to move to a club where he should be a regular starter.
Inter, who have already signed fellow England players John Stones and Djed Spence this summer, contacted Liverpool on Wednesday morning with a bid €30m (£25.7m) with the potential for the fee to rise by €5m (£4.2m) in add-ons.
Liverpool have not accepted that offer but the indications are they are edging towards a situation where they will shake hands if Inter come up with a fee in line with the £35m they paid Tottenham Hotspur for Spence earlier this month.
Should the deal go through, it would be a significant departure as Jones is something of a dying breed – a young boy who grew up in Liverpool city centre, supporting the club and found his way into the first team with perseverance and talent.
He made his debut in January 2019 in an FA Cup tie at Wolves and, in total, has amassed 229 appearances and scored 22 goals – the last of which came in a 1-1 draw with Brentford on the final day of last season. He has won two Premier Leagues, the FA Cup, League Cup and Club World Cup.
Liverpool are yet to secure the right-winger they have been pursuing since Mohamed Salah left at the end of last season and – at this stage – it is unlikely they will follow up initial interest in Ibrahim Mbaye, of Paris St-Germain.
Talks for PSG’s Bradley Barcola remain ongoing, but PSG’s asking price of £120m means Liverpool are assessing alternatives if a deal cannot be done with the European champions. Levante, meanwhile, are hoping to take the highly regarded Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, on loan from Liverpool.
7620640e4495e6bb3caf15ca.summary: Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones is close to leaving the club for Inter Milan after Inter submitted a £30m package. Jones has long desired the move to secure regular starting minutes. Meanwhile, Liverpool continue to evaluate their options regarding wingers, including ongoing talks for Bradley Barcola.
key_points: Inter Milan made a £30m package offer for England midfielder Curtis Jones.
Jones previously had a pitch dispute with teammates during Liverpool's US pre-season tour and wants a move for regular starts.
Liverpool are nearing a potential agreement if the fee meets their £35m valuation.
Liverpool remain in ongoing talks for PSG winger Bradley Barcola amid a £120m asking price.

It was their second attempt to sign Jones but once Liverpool had rejected it, it seemed likely that he would stay to see out the remaining 12 months of his contract. The Anfield club were relaxed that his deal running down would not see him lose focus.
There was an incident, though, during Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US when Jones was involved in a row on the pitch with Dominik Szoboszlai and Kostas Tsimikas over the captaincy following a 1-0 win over Wrexham in New York.
Jones swiftly apologised for his actions, posting a statement on Instagram, but it was the kind of episode that indicated it would be better if there were a parting of ways. It is well known that he wants to join Inter and relishes the chance to move to a club where he should be a regular starter.
Inter, who have already signed fellow England players John Stones and Djed Spence this summer, contacted Liverpool on Wednesday morning with a bid €30m (£25.7m) with the potential for the fee to rise by €5m (£4.2m) in add-ons.
Liverpool have not accepted that offer but the indications are they are edging towards a situation where they will shake hands if Inter come up with a fee in line with the £35m they paid Tottenham Hotspur for Spence earlier this month.
Should the deal go through, it would be a significant departure as Jones is something of a dying breed – a young boy who grew up in Liverpool city centre, supporting the club and found his way into the first team with perseverance and talent.
He made his debut in January 2019 in an FA Cup tie at Wolves and, in total, has amassed 229 appearances and scored 22 goals – the last of which came in a 1-1 draw with Brentford on the final day of last season. He has won two Premier Leagues, the FA Cup, League Cup and Club World Cup.
Liverpool are yet to secure the right-winger they have been pursuing since Mohamed Salah left at the end of last season and – at this stage – it is unlikely they will follow up initial interest in Ibrahim Mbaye, of Paris St-Germain.
Talks for PSG’s Bradley Barcola remain ongoing, but PSG’s asking price of £120m means Liverpool are assessing alternatives if a deal cannot be done with the European champions. Levante, meanwhile, are hoping to take the highly regarded Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, on loan from Liverpool.
c0ea2b469455acf60d58e9b3.summary: Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones is close to leaving the club for Inter Milan after Inter submitted a £30m package. Jones has long desired the move to secure regular starting minutes. Meanwhile, Liverpool continue to evaluate their options regarding wingers, including ongoing talks for Bradley Barcola.
key_points: Inter Milan made a £30m package offer for England midfielder Curtis Jones.
Jones previously had a pitch dispute with teammates during Liverpool's US pre-season tour and wants a move for regular starts.
Liverpool are nearing a potential agreement if the fee meets their £35m valuation.
Liverpool remain in ongoing talks for PSG winger Bradley Barcola amid a £120m asking price.

bfb1d8cf9235a4f745a7bc79.title: The treaty that governs the Moon was written in 1967, bans nations from owning it, and created no court or police force to enforce the rule — and 70 countries are now helping write the practical rules for what happens when humans return.
bfb1d8cf9235a4f745a7bc79.author: Space Daily Editorial Team
bfb1d8cf9235a4f745a7bc79.content:
When Mauritius signed the Artemis Accords on 17 July 2026, it became the 70th country to join a coalition trying to turn broad principles of space law into habits that could work on the lunar surface. The milestone sounds, at first, like the creation of a new legal order for the Moon.
It is not. The legal foundation remains the Outer Space Treaty, opened for signature in 1967. The Artemis Accords do not amend that treaty, and they are not binding international law. They are a political commitment by their signatories to interpret and apply existing obligations in a broadly similar way.
That may sound modest, but the practical questions are no longer hypothetical. Governments and companies are preparing landers, rovers, communications systems and longer stays. The old treaty says a great deal about peaceful use and national responsibility. It says much less about what two crews should do when they want to work near the same ice-rich crater.
What the 1967 treaty actually bans
The Outer Space Treaty opened for signature on 27 January 1967 and entered into force on 10 October that year. Article II says outer space, including the Moon and other celestial bodies, is not subject to national appropriation by a claim of sovereignty, by use or occupation, or by any other means.
That is the basis for the familiar shorthand that nobody can own the Moon. More precisely, no country can extend its territory there. Planting a flag does not convert a landing site into a province, and occupying a crater does not establish sovereignty over it.
The treaty also makes states internationally responsible for their national space activities. That responsibility extends to non-governmental entities, whose work must be authorized and continually supervised by an appropriate state. Article IX adds duties of due regard and consultation when an activity might cause potentially harmful interference.
Those provisions are substantial. They are also broad. The text does not lay out traffic rules for rovers, prescribe the size of a safe operating area around a lander or clearly settle who may own material extracted from lunar soil.
No dedicated court does not mean no consequences
The treaty created no lunar court, police service, inspectorate or automatic sanctions body. There is no treaty official who can arrive at a disputed landing site, order one mission to move and impose a fine if it refuses.
That does not make the agreement meaningless. Compliance works through state responsibility, national licensing, diplomatic pressure, consultation, reputation and the wider machinery of international law. A country can place conditions on its companies, withdraw an authorization, protest another state’s conduct or negotiate after an incident. Disputes may also reach existing international forums when the states involved accept the relevant jurisdiction.
But none of that provides a fast, Moon-specific referee. SpaceDaily has previously looked closely at this enforcement gap in the 1967 framework. The important development now is that the group trying to supply some of the missing operating detail has grown to 70 countries.
What the 70 countries have actually signed
The Artemis Accords began in 2020 with the United States and seven initial partners. They reaffirm the Outer Space Treaty and set out principles covering peaceful purposes, transparency, interoperability, emergency assistance, registration, scientific data, heritage protection, resource use, avoidance of harmful interference and orbital debris.
NASA announced that Mauritius became the 70th signatory on 17 July 2026. That figure is specifically the number of Artemis Accords signatories. It is not the membership of a new world government for space, and it should not be confused with participation in the United Nations committee that discusses space law.
The phrase “helping write the practical rules” needs the same care. The 70 countries are not sitting in a treaty conference and voting line by line on binding lunar legislation. They are working through workshops, diplomatic exchanges and mission partnerships to make general principles more operational. A 2026 workshop in Lima, for example, focused on implementation and coordination among signatories.
That process can matter even without a new treaty. When many states repeatedly use the same notification formats, coordinate similar activities and expect the same conduct from partners, those habits can become influential. They can also reveal which principles fail when tested against real missions.
The difficult test is a crowded landing area
Useful terrain on the Moon is not evenly distributed. Permanently shadowed polar regions may contain accessible water ice, while nearby elevated areas can receive longer periods of sunlight. Those combinations could make a relatively small number of locations especially attractive for power, communications and resource work.
Operating close together creates risks that the treaty never describes in engineering detail. A descending lander can throw dust and fragments across the surface. A rover can cross another mission’s route. Radio transmissions may interfere with instruments. Drilling or excavation could disturb an experiment that depends on a quiet local environment.
The Artemis Accords respond with notification, coordination and the idea of temporary safety zones. In principle, such a zone is not a property boundary. It is supposed to identify the area in which an activity could cause harmful interference, so other operators know when consultation is needed.
The distinction will have to be demonstrated, not merely asserted. A limited buffer around a dangerous landing operation is easier to defend than a large, indefinite perimeter around a valuable deposit. Size, duration, technical justification and access to consultation will determine whether a safety zone looks like prudent deconfliction or territorial control under another name.
Resources remain the most sensitive unresolved issue
The Accords state that extracting and using space resources can be consistent with the Outer Space Treaty and does not inherently constitute national appropriation. The argument separates ownership of removed material from sovereignty over the place it came from. Several countries have reflected a similar view in domestic legislation.
That interpretation is not universally accepted. Critics worry that extensive resource rights could eventually create control resembling ownership even if no flag formally claims the ground. The 1979 Moon Agreement anticipated an international regime for exploiting lunar resources, but it failed to win broad support among the major space powers.
A separate United Nations process is now developing recommended principles for space resource activities. The 2025 draft addresses issues including harmful interference, cultural and natural heritage, benefit sharing, sustainability and the interests of developing countries. Those recommendations are voluntary as drafted.
This parallel work is important because the Artemis coalition is large but not universal. China and Russia, both major space powers, are not Artemis Accords signatories. A practice accepted inside one partnership does not automatically become a rule binding every country on the Moon.
The operating manual will be written through behaviour
The most consequential lunar rules may emerge through ordinary decisions rather than one grand negotiation. Which agency gives notice before landing? How early is that notice issued? What information does a company share about dust, radio emissions or a rover route? What happens when two planned safety areas overlap? How are historic sites protected without turning preservation into permanent exclusion?
NASA’s original 2020 announcement described the Accords as a practical set of principles for cooperation. Six years and 62 additional signatories later, the project has far greater diplomatic weight. Yet its basic limits remain. It creates no court, police force or universally binding code, and countries outside it are not obligated to follow its provisions.
I think the humble way to read the 70-country milestone is neither as a solved problem nor as empty symbolism. It is evidence that a large and varied group wants common expectations before lunar operations become crowded. Whether those expectations deserve wider trust will depend on how the signatories behave when cooperation becomes inconvenient.
If they consistently register spacecraft, share useful information, coordinate close operations and keep safety zones narrow and temporary, the Accords may make the treaty’s broad duties workable. If they use technical language to secure exclusive control over desirable terrain, the absence of a dedicated enforcement institution will become more serious with every landing.
The Outer Space Treaty remains the constitutional foundation. The Artemis Accords are closer to an operating manual being written while the machines are already being built. The practical rules for humanity’s return will ultimately be judged not by the elegance of the documents, but by what countries do when another spacecraft lands nearby.
bfb1d8cf9235a4f745a7bc79.summary: Mauritius became the 70th country to sign the Artemis Accords, joining a coalition attempting to establish practical operational rules for lunar exploration. While the 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans national sovereignty over the Moon and requires states to supervise space activities, it lacks specific traffic rules and a dedicated enforcement court. The non-binding Artemis Accords aim to bridge this gap through coordination, notification, and safety zones as missions prepare for crowded lunar sites.
key_points: The 1967 Outer Space Treaty prohibits nations from owning the Moon or claiming territorial sovereignty.
The treaty established no court, police force, or automatic sanctions body to enforce its rules.
The Artemis Accords are non-binding political commitments signed by 70 countries to interpret and apply existing space obligations.
Major space powers such as China and Russia are not signatories to the Artemis Accords.
Unresolved challenges include managing crowded landing areas, preventing harmful interference, and determining rules for extracting space resources.

2b09601807d4930b53a50f9f.title: Labour under pressure to restore men’s right to prostate cancer tests
2b09601807d4930b53a50f9f.author: Michael Searles
2b09601807d4930b53a50f9f.content:
Labour is under pressure to reinstate middle-aged men’s right to tests that help detect prostate cancer.
Last week, The Telegraph revealed that men aged over 50 were no longer entitled to a blood test to help identify the disease, with GPs instead deciding who is given one.
Previously, any man over the age of 50 had been entitled to a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test via their GP, even if they did not have symptoms.
The Government is now facing increasing pressure to reverse its decision to remove that right, including calls from the Conservative Party.
Stuart Andrew MP, the shadow health secretary, said it “looks like a further restriction of patient choice with a service that was on offer now disappearing”.
“PSA tests are a credible aid for the early identification of prostate cancer. Labour’s restrictions risk leaving men without answers,” he told The Telegraph.
“Requiring information on genetic heritage and family history is particularly concerning when many people simply do not have accurate family medical records. No man with potential prostate cancer symptoms should be denied a test because of poor family records.”
He said the Conservatives would “back the latest evidence and research to ensure patient care remains at the heart of testing guidance”.
2b09601807d4930b53a50f9f.summary: The Labour government is facing pressure from the Conservative Party and other critics to reverse a decision that removes the right of men over 50 to receive a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test without symptoms. Previously, any man in this age group could request the test via their GP, but access is now determined by GPs using criteria that include family history and genetic heritage. Critics argue this restriction risks leaving men without answers and limits patient choice in early cancer detection.
key_points: Men over 50 are no longer automatically entitled to a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test via their GP if they are asymptomatic.
GPs now decide which patients receive the screening test based on factors such as family history and genetic heritage.
The Labour government faces growing pressure, including from the Conservative Party, to reverse the policy change.
Critics argue that relying on family medical history is concerning because many individuals lack accurate records.

725ed02beacdd49783e969da.title: Angela Rayner tells how Treasury to be stripped of powers in blow to London jobs
725ed02beacdd49783e969da.author: Nicholas Cecil
725ed02beacdd49783e969da.content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Burnham To Give Mayors Share Of Income Tax.](https://cdn.ex.co/transformations-account/production/761715bb-261d-4032-af09-a493a82bd926/05fdaf12-51e2-55f3-96b1-9762b64dfd43/thumbnail-360.webp)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
It would retain the responsibility for overseeing the public finances.
![An aerial view of Parliament Square and government buildings including the Treasury in Whitehall (Victoria Jones/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2025/03/21/10/abd716ffc00d27d25d8d3e4753a8f8efY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzQyNjM5MDk2-2.60844096.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Explaining the reforms, Ms Rayner told Times Radio: “It's about the whole of Government recognising that power that is centralised, which we're one of the most over-centralised economies, doesn't always give the best results for all areas.
“We've been keep trying to do that, and some people call it trickle down economics, and you've seen areas which were deindustrialised over the last sort of 50 years that haven't seen that investment and that drive come forward.”
She added: “So we now have an industrial strategy.
“We have a Government framework which is about putting power back in local people's hands, and then it's about delivery.
The devolution announcement came just days after ministers pressed ahead with plans for default planning approval for new homes within 800 metres or ten minutes walk of busy Tube, rail and tram stations.
The reform will be welcomed by many people desperate to find a home they can afford to rent or buy in London or other parts of the country.
But it sparked immediate protests that the policy runs counters to Mr Burnham’s pledge to devolve more powers, by stripping councils of key decision-making, and threatens to lead to more homes on green belt land.
Read More
Ms Rayner was speaking after the Prime Minister said the new No10 North will take responsibility for growth from the Treasury as part of his blueprint for the biggest “devolution of power in modern times”.
![Prime Minister Andy Burnham said ‘we will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need’ (Finnbarr Webster/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/12/fdd383dcf39c0b7597a38f2e4546db93Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3MTM4MDE0-2.85564288.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Mr Burnham suggested the Treasury would focus on controlling the public finances while his outpost of 10 Downing Street based in Manchester would lead the charge on boosting the economy.
In an interview with The Times, he said Chancellor John Healey was fully supportive of the move which he described as part of a “huge transfer of power”.
“There’s a job to be done around control of public finances. It’s just the dual job of growth and control of public finances (that) sometimes clouds the growth mission,” he said.
“And particularly having No 10 leading on that growth mission means you’ve got maximum power to unlock the blockages where they exist in the wider Whitehall system.”
The Manchester branch of Downing Street in Heron House is already up and running and officials claim it will cost taxpayers no extra money.
The Prime Minister is expected to work at the outpost once each week during his premiership, as part of his move to push power out of Westminster.
However, Mr Burnham risks accusations of a power grab with No10 North taking control of the economic growth agenda, rather than this being shifted to the Treasury’s campus in Darlington.
725ed02beacdd49783e969da.summary: Angela Rayner announced reforms that will shift economic growth responsibilities from the Treasury to a new Manchester-based No10 North outpost, as part of a major decentralization of government power. While the Treasury will retain control over public finances, the move aims to address over-centralization and better support deindustrialised areas. However, the policy has sparked debate over potential impacts on local decision-making and council powers.
key_points: Responsibility for economic growth is being shifted from the Treasury to the new No10 North based in Manchester.
The Treasury will retain its core responsibility for overseeing public finances.
Angela Rayner stated that the reforms aim to counter over-centralized economic policies that have failed to invest in deindustrialised areas.
The Prime Minister is expected to work from the Manchester outpost once a week as part of efforts to push power out of Westminster.

![Prime Minister Andy Burnham said ‘we will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need’ (Finnbarr Webster/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/12/fdd383dcf39c0b7597a38f2e4546db93Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3MTM4MDE0-2.85564288.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Mr Burnham suggested the Treasury would focus on controlling the public finances while his outpost of 10 Downing Street based in Manchester would lead the charge on boosting the economy.
In an interview with The Times, he said Chancellor John Healey was fully supportive of the move which he described as part of a “huge transfer of power”.
“There’s a job to be done around control of public finances. It’s just the dual job of growth and control of public finances (that) sometimes clouds the growth mission,” he said.
“And particularly having No 10 leading on that growth mission means you’ve got maximum power to unlock the blockages where they exist in the wider Whitehall system.”
The Manchester branch of Downing Street in Heron House is already up and running and officials claim it will cost taxpayers no extra money.
The Prime Minister is expected to work at the outpost once each week during his premiership, as part of his move to push power out of Westminster.
However, Mr Burnham risks accusations of a power grab with No10 North taking control of the economic growth agenda, rather than this being shifted to the Treasury’s campus in Darlington.
2a862f92f9a84a55d10c6cf8.summary: Angela Rayner announced reforms that will shift economic growth responsibilities from the Treasury to a new Manchester-based No10 North outpost, as part of a major decentralization of government power. While the Treasury will retain control over public finances, the move aims to address over-centralization and better support deindustrialised areas. However, the policy has sparked debate over potential impacts on local decision-making and council powers.
key_points: Responsibility for economic growth is being shifted from the Treasury to the new No10 North based in Manchester.
The Treasury will retain its core responsibility for overseeing public finances.
Angela Rayner stated that the reforms aim to counter over-centralized economic policies that have failed to invest in deindustrialised areas.
The Prime Minister is expected to work from the Manchester outpost once a week as part of efforts to push power out of Westminster.

c4f56487bc93bcb399d5913f.title: Downpours continue for UK with risk of flash flooding
c4f56487bc93bcb399d5913f.author: Ben Rich
c4f56487bc93bcb399d5913f.content:
![A discarded flood warning sign sits in a field of long dry grass](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/097c/live/a609a580-9bd7-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
- Published
Heavy showers and thunderstorms will continue to affect large swathes of the UK on Thursday, bringing the threat of flooding and travel disruption.
A Met Office yellow thunderstorm warning remains in force across northern England and north Wales until 10:00 BST on Thursday.
The downpours will drift southwards and eastwards during the day, affecting other parts of Wales, the Midlands, East Anglia and southern England.
Drivers are being warned that the return to wet weather could lead to slippery conditions as well as the risk of flooded roads.
Temperatures are also forecast to drop with some places expected to remain below the August average over the next few days.
Low pressure drifts eastwards
After a summer that has largely been dominated by high pressure, low pressure has now taken control.
Unstable air underneath the low has allowed big storm clouds to develop, capable of delivering torrential downpours accompanied by hail and thunder.
During Thursday morning, northern England and north Wales will bear the brunt of the thunderstorms.
![A map showing the Met Office yellow warning area, stretching from Newcastle in the north to Holyhead in the south](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/596/cpsprodpb/27a3/live/025d34a0-9bd8-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
The Met Office yellow warning for thunderstorms remains in force until 10:00 BST
Within the Met Office yellow warning area, 15-20mm of rain could fall in just an hour, with 30-50mm possible in a six hour period.
Flash flooding is possible, especially in areas where the ground remains very hard after the prolonged hot, dry spell.
Lightning and hail will bring additional hazards.
Showers are expected to ease from the north during the morning, migrating southwards into other parts of Wales as well as central and southern England where a few downpours could still be heavy and thundery.
As ever with showers, some places will see more rain than others.
Scotland and Northern Ireland will also have showers but they should be less intense, with a lower chance of thunder.
Tricky driving conditions
Motoring experts warn that wet weather after a prolonged dry spell can cause dangerous driving conditions.
RAC road safety spokesperson Rod Dennis says: "Oil, fuel and rubber deposits that have built up over many weeks will now have been mixed together by the light rain, instead of being washed away, which means drivers are at greater risk of skidding on greasy roads.
"If heavier rain arrives, motorists may have to contend with the danger of flash floods in some areas."
Drivers are being advised to reduce their speed and leave extra space between them and the vehicle in front.
No end in sight for the drought
Even as rain has returned, experts are warning that the drought gripping large swathes of the UK will not immediately come to an end.
It will need a sustained period of persistent rainfall to replenish water stocks and we are unlikely to know whether this has happened until late in the upcoming winter.
However, it is worth adding that while most areas have seen rainfall well below normal this summer - with some locations having a two month dry spell - that has not been the case everywhere.
Aultbea in the Scottish Highlands has recorded 389.6mm of rain so far this summer - more than one and a half times the seasonal norm, and only 10.2mm short of its wettest summer on record.
Temperatures fall below average
As northerly winds develop across the UK, temperatures are set to drop.
Thursday afternoon is expected to bring highs of 13-23C.
It is expected to be the first day since 29 June when temperatures will fail to reach 25C anywhere in the UK.
Friday is set to be cooler still with temperatures widely remaining below the August norm.
![A weather chart showing Friday afternoon's temperatures - ranging from 12C in Lerwick to 21C in Plymouth, London and St Helier](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/665/cpsprodpb/a793/live/20358a90-9be2-11f1-ba30-ddd78081057f.jpg)
Daytime highs of 15-23C would be typical across the UK in August
Friday night will also be the chilliest for quite some time with temperatures widely dropping into single digits.
Parts of Scotland and northern England could see lows of 3 or 4C.
Chilly nights will continue to feature over the weekend although daytime temperatures will rebound a little as high pressure tries to build - meaning less rain and more sunshine.
You can keep up to date with your local forecast on the BBC Weather website and app.
c4f56487bc93bcb399d5913f.summary: Heavy showers and thunderstorms are continuing to affect large parts of the UK, bringing risks of flash flooding and travel disruption. A Met Office yellow thunderstorm warning is in place, while low pressure drives the unsettled weather and causes temperatures to drop below the August average. Experts warn that the current rainfall will not immediately end the ongoing drought, and drivers face hazardous road conditions.
key_points: A Met Office yellow thunderstorm warning is in force for northern England and north Wales.
Flash flooding is possible, particularly where ground remains hard from dry weather.
Wet weather following a dry spell creates greasy road conditions and skidding risks for drivers.
Temperatures are dropping below the August average, with chilly single-digit lows expected in some areas.
Experts state that a sustained period of persistent rainfall is needed to end the UK drought.

32895fb22167e898c029be19.title: Seven people, mostly foreign tourists, killed in helicopter crash in Kenya
32895fb22167e898c029be19.author: AFP; The Associated Press
32895fb22167e898c029be19.content:
![Rescue officials work at the site of a tourist helicopter crash that caused multiple casualties, according to the police, in Samburu County, Kenya, August 19, 2026. Kenya Red Cross/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY. NO RESALES. NO ARCHIVES. MANDATORY CREDIT.](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reuters_6a85fcb2-1787165874.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
A helicopter taking tourists on a safari has crashed in a remote part of northern Kenya, killing all seven people on board, including an Ecuadorian official and an American journalist.
The helicopter crashed at 9:13am local time (06:13 GMT) on Wednesday while flying from the Loisaba Conservancy to the Ewaso Nyiro area in Samburu County, according to the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority, which said in a statement that an investigation was under way.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Eleven killed in Kenya plane crash near Maasai Mara National Reserve
- list 2 of 3Medical plane crash in Kenya kills at least six, injures two
- list 3 of 3Bus carrying mourners overturns in Kenya, killing 25 people
Helicopter crashes have happened with increasing regularity in Kenya, which has a vibrant tourism industry that depends on domestic carriers to ferry visitors to distant places like Mount Ololokwe.
Six passengers and the pilot were on board the helicopter, officials said. David Nkoroi, the police commander for Samburu, told reporters that all seven people had died but did not reveal their identities.
Later on Wednesday, Ecuador’s Transport Minister Roberto Luque said the country’s intelligence chief Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife, Stephany Hollihan, were among those killed in the crash.
“Today Michele and Stephany left us too soon. Thinking of their family, especially their children and parents,” Luque wrote on X.
Sensi-Contugi, 42, is a former businessman appointed as head of Ecuador’s National Intelligence Center in 2024. He was a close associate of right-wing President Daniel Noboa, whose country is mired in a security crisis.
US broadcaster NBCUniversal also said its journalist Jose Alberto Suarez – president and general manager of Telemundo 31, Telemundo 49, and Telemundo Fort Myers–Naples – was among those killed.
A spokesperson for the United States Department of State said five US citizens were among the dead.
“The US Embassy is in touch with local authorities and is providing consular assistance,” he said. “We extend our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones on their loss.”
![A rescue official works at the site of a tourist helicopter crash that caused multiple casualties, according to the police, in Samburu County, Kenya, August 19, 2026. Kenya Red Cross/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY. NO RESALES. NO ARCHIVES. MANDATORY CREDIT.](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reuters_6a85fbd0-1787165648.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C579&quality=80)
Recovery operations continue
The helicopter crashed in a rugged area in the foothills of Mount Ololokwe, a popular tourist destination in the country, local media reported.
The helicopter, owned by local company Lady Lori Helicopters, was carrying guests with travel company &Beyond. Lady Lori Helicopters said in a statement that the aircraft was operating a charter flight when it crashed.
Tropic Air Kenya, a local safari operator, said in a statement that it dispatched two of its helicopters to aid search and rescue operations.
The aviation authority said the aircraft was a Eurocopter EC130 B4.
The Kenya Red Cross said that its emergency response teams were “participating in a multiagency response effort as rescue teams work to access the crash site”.
Three bodies were still trapped in the wreckage as of Wednesday evening, with recovery operations to continue on Thursday due to the ongoing flames at the crash site, Kenya’s Daily Nation reported.
In February, a Kenyan legislator was among six people who died after a helicopter crash in a hilly area of western Kenya.
32895fb22167e898c029be19.summary: A tourist helicopter crash in a remote part of Samburu County, Kenya, killed all seven people on board, including foreign tourists and officials. The aircraft went down while flying from the Loisaba Conservancy to the Ewaso Nyiro area. Local authorities and aviation officials have launched an investigation into the incident.
key_points: Seven people died in the helicopter crash, including six passengers and the pilot.
The victims included an Ecuadorian intelligence official and his wife, as well as an American journalist.
The US State Department confirmed that five US citizens were among the dead.
The helicopter was a Eurocopter EC130 B4 operated by Lady Lori Helicopters on a charter flight for travel company &Beyond.

0d0349e0c5e33a6db3a66b9d.title: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School investigated over 'drip pricing'
0d0349e0c5e33a6db3a66b9d.author: Emer Moreau
0d0349e0c5e33a6db3a66b9d.content:
Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School investigated over 'drip pricing'
![Getty Images A young woman sitting at her laptop while holding a credit card](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/eb7b/live/d50ea0f0-9bce-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg.webp) Getty Images
Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School are being investigated by the consumer watchdog over concerns they are not showing full prices upfront to customers.
The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) is examining whether the three companies engaged in so-called 'drip pricing', which is an illegal practice where mandatory fees are not included in the headline price shown to customers.
If the CMA concludes that the firms have broken the law, it can fine them or order them to compensate customers.
The three companies said they were committed to transparency for customers and would engage fully with the CMA.
In the case of Trainline, the CMA said it observed fees of up to £2.79 being added on to headline train fares, and up to £1.50 for coach bookings.
"Both are costs that can add up for frequent travellers," the CMA said.
Virgin Atlantic is being investigated to see whether mandatory resort fees and local taxes were included in the upfront prices shown to customers buying package holidays. The CMA said these fees vary but can go up to hundreds of pounds, significantly increasing the cost of a holiday.
And the watchdog is looking into whether RED Driving School included mandatory booking fees and digital fees in the upfront price shown to people buying driving lessons. The CMA said the fees could be more than £7 per lesson.
Earlier this year, the CMA ordered two other driving schools to give refunds to more than 80,000 customers after they did not disclose the total price for lessons upfront during the online booking process.
Emma Cochrane, the CMA's executive director for consumer protection, said: "The first price customers see should be the price they pay.
"At a time when many households are watching every pound they spend, it is important that people are not surprised by extra fees when booking train and coach tickets, holidays or driving lessons."
A spokesperson for Virgin Atlantic Holidays said it takes its responsibility to customers "incredibly seriously", adding: "we always want to ensure they can make an informed decision when booking a holiday with us.
"Mandatory fees are indicated at multiple stages throughout the booking journey. We are reviewing the points raised by the CMA carefully and will cooperate fully with its investigation."
A Trainline spokesperson said the company was "committed to offering customers a transparent booking experience with clear pricing and genuine value.
"We've proactively engaged with the CMA over several months and we are taking proactive steps to enhance how certain fees are presented to our customers."
Red Driving School said it was disappointed at being included in a wider investigation.
"Red Driver Training always values both transparency and consumer satisfaction in all of our interactions with our customers," a spokesperson said.
"We take any and all of our obligations under consumer law with utmost focus and seriousness."
Since last year, the CMA has had the power to rule that consumer laws have been broken without having to take businesses to court.
Consumer rights group Which? said the CMA should not hesitate to use these powers, "especially after each firm has already received a warning advisory letter".
Sue Davies, head of consumer rights policy at Which?, said: "Following comments made by the Prime Minister last week that unfair pricing practices have no place in our economy, this move sends a clear message to other businesses to follow the rules.
"At a time when household budgets are under strain, consumers must have confidence that businesses aren't there to rip them off and that the regulator is willing to step in to protect their rights."
![Your Voice banner image. Your Voice is written in white against a purple background.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/e71f/live/3e851480-9bb9-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.png.webp)
0d0349e0c5e33a6db3a66b9d.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) is investigating Trainline, Virgin Atlantic, and RED Driving School over concerns regarding 'drip pricing', where mandatory fees are withheld from upfront headline prices. The watchdog is examining additional fees added during bookings for train and coach tickets, holiday packages, and driving lessons. If found to have broken the law, the companies could face fines or be ordered to compensate customers.
key_points: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic, and RED Driving School are facing a CMA investigation over 'drip pricing'.
Trainline is being investigated for added fees on train and coach bookings, while Virgin Atlantic is under scrutiny for resort fees and local taxes on package holidays.
RED Driving School is being investigated over mandatory booking and digital fees added to driving lessons.
The CMA has the power to fine companies or order customer compensation if consumer laws are found to have been violated.

"At a time when household budgets are under strain, consumers must have confidence that businesses aren't there to rip them off and that the regulator is willing to step in to protect their rights."

The watchdog is examining additional fees added during bookings for train and coach tickets, holiday packages, and driving lessons. If found to have broken the law, the companies could face fines or be ordered to compensate customers.

Trainline is being investigated for added fees on train and coach bookings, while Virgin Atlantic is under scrutiny for resort fees and local taxes on package holidays.

c8051402627af49945da261c.title: The iPhone 18 Pro Is Almost Here. These Are The Rumors We Think Are Real
c8051402627af49945da261c.author: Jibin Joseph
c8051402627af49945da261c.content:
![](https://sm.pcmag.com/t/pcmag_uk/news/t/the-iphone/the-iphone-18-pro-is-almost-here-these-are-the-rumors-we-thi_c7ed.1920.jpg) (Credit: PCMag/Apple)
We're reportedly only a few weeks away from Apple's next iPhone event, which is likely to include the launch of a foldable, as well as iPhone 18 Pros.
Customers usually hold off on iPhone purchases right before Apple’s fall event, but the RAM crisis and its associated price hikes may have you wondering whether it's best to buy now and avoid any more increases. Apple already raised prices across several major product lines in June, but the iPhone was not included, helping drive iPhone 17 sales during the last quarter.
To make your decision easier, we’ve rounded up the biggest iPhone 18 Pro rumors we have heard so far. While these features and prices aren’t confirmed yet, they should help paint a picture of what to expect from Apple’s next big smartphones.
iPhone 18 Pro: Revised Lineup
The biggest rumor around the iPhone 18 lineup is its release timeline. Unlike previous years, where Apple released four phones in the same series in one go, Bloomberg reports Apple could take a two-pronged approach to ensure consistent revenue throughout the year.
Flagship phones, such as the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and the first-ever foldable iPhone, could be unveiled in September, while the base iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2, and the iPhone 18e could be launched in spring 2027. We discuss the foldable iPhone in detail in a separate rumor round-up, so we’ll just stick to the Pro models here.
iPhone 18 Pro: Design and Colors
The iPhone 17 Pro models brought a major overhaul to Apple’s smartphone design language, with a new camera “plateau” and two-toned color scheme. This year, Apple isn’t expected to drastically change the device's appearance, but it could add a few bold colors and return to a more uniform color scheme on the back.
Several leakers, including Sonny Dickson and Instant Digital, claim that Apple could go with a never-before-seen cherry red and a new light blue, alongside the regular dark gray. Dickson also shared pictures of potential dummies, including one in light gray.
While the appearance of the rear is expected to remain the same, the in-hand feel could be a lot different. Ice Universe says the battery could get slightly larger on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, contributing to increased weight and bulk. More precisely, the leaker expects the device to be 0.25mm thicker and 7 grams heavier.
iPhone 18 Pro Display
On the front, we might see one significant change. The Dynamic Island, or the camera cutout, could be reduced by 35%, Ice Universe says. This won’t shrink the feature's overall functionality, but it could move the Face ID sensor’s illuminator to one corner below the screen.
When it comes to display sizes, the consensus is that the iPhone 18 Pro will come in its usual 6.3-inch screen, while the Pro Max will have a 6.9-inch screen. Apple, however, has reportedly been pushing suppliers to provide much brighter displays and could use the more power-efficient LTPO+ display tech.
iPhone 18 Pro Cameras
The iPhone 17 Pro lineup bumped all three cameras to 48MP. For the iPhone 18 Pro, the biggest camera-related rumor we have heard is around variable aperture. While the iPhone 17 models had a fixed aperture, the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce a variable aperture. ETNews reports that the modified system has already entered production and would help the cameras deliver more light to the sensors in dark conditions and reduce light in bright conditions.
Apple may also modify its relatively new Camera Control button. Introduced with the iPhone 16, the capacitive button at the bottom right of the phone lets you quickly launch the Camera app, take pictures, and adjust settings for zoom, exposure, depth, and other controls. Mastering the capacitive button, however, has proved difficult, with users noting that they have been accidentally launching the Camera app. Apple may finally fix the problem by removing the touch-sensitive components of the button and delivering a more user-friendly experience, 9to5Mac reports.
iPhone 18 Pro Performance
The iPhone 18 Pro is likely to receive a performance boost with the A20 chip. It will use TSMC’s 2nm technology, an upgrade from the previous generation’s 3nm tech. The transition will allow more transistors on each chip but also raise chip costs by 50%, MacRumors reports.
The chip is also rumored to have TSMC’s Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) technology, which infuses RAM into the same wafer as the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine. Overall, it is expected to be 18% faster and 30% more power-efficient than than previous generations, according to leaker Fixed Focus Digital.
Apple usually reserves the base variant of its chip series for the standard iPhone models, while the Pro models get the corresponding Pro chip. With the iPhone 18 series, Apple is reportedly considering offering just the high-end variant across the lineup.
Another expected upgrade is for the modem. The iPhone 17 Pro models had an unspecified third-party modem, but the iPhone 18 Pro could get the company’s proprietary C2 modem. It will support 5G satellite connectivity and reduce the scope of location data retained by networks, according to MacRumors.
iPhone 18 Pro Battery
Apple never reveals its battery capacities, but multiple leakers have indicated a larger and more efficient battery for the iPhone 18 Pro Max. According to Digital Chat Station, the top variant will have a capacity of up to 5,200mAh, slightly better than the 5,088mAh capacity of its predecessor. With a more efficient modem and processor, the battery life could be significantly longer. The iPhone 18 Pro, on the other hand, could see a minimal bump from 4,252mAh to 4,288mAh.
More recently, leaks posted on Korean and Chinese social media sites tip a US iPhone 18 Pro Max model with a 5,567mAh battery, a nearly 10% increase over the iPhone 17 Pro Max, MacRumors notes.
iPhone 18 Pro: Pricing and Release
This is what much of the decision-making hinges on. Apple has avoided raising prices for its biggest revenue generator, but rising RAM and storage costs are unavoidable, by outgoing CEO Tim Cook’s own admission.
Common sense suggests a price hike for iPhones is inevitable in September. According to The Wall Street Journal's estimate, rising component costs would push the iPhone 18 Pro to start at $1,299. If you couple that with recent Apple trends, the iPhone 18 Pro Max could be priced $100 higher, taking its starting price to $1,399. In comparison, the iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099, while the 17 Pro Max starts at $1,199.
When asked on a recent earnings call about potential price hikes for the iPhone, Cook said it's "too early to come to a definitive conclusion of what happens there. Because it takes a little while for the channels to adjust since there's channel inventory, it takes a while for the consumer to respond. We'll understand that more in the weeks ahead."
The iPhone 18 Pro’s release date hasn’t been finalized yet. Going by previous event dates, Sept. 9, 2026, probably makes the most sense for the announcement, with a ship date the following week, but we'll have to wait for those invitations to hit our inboxes to know for sure.
c8051402627af49945da261c.summary: Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 Pro lineup is rumored to feature a split release schedule, new design colors, and a potential variable aperture camera system. Performance is expected to improve with a new A20 chip utilizing 2nm technology and a proprietary C2 modem. However, rising component costs may lead to higher starting prices of $1,299 for the iPhone 18 Pro and $1,399 for the Pro Max.
key_points: Apple may split the iPhone 18 release, launching Pro and foldable models in September and base models in spring 2027.
The Dynamic Island cutout could shrink by 35%, and the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce a variable aperture camera system.
Performance is expected to be boosted by a new A20 chip built on TSMC's 2nm technology.
Rising component and RAM costs are expected to drive starting prices up to $1,299 for the Pro and $1,399 for the Pro Max.

8171afa8539786c3d8b25c07.title: Sheffield man speaks out on Devon mum who faked childhood illness
8171afa8539786c3d8b25c07.author: Julia Bryson
8171afa8539786c3d8b25c07.content:
![A family of a man, woman and two children, a young girl and boy. The boy is wearing a red top and has a tube which goes into his nose. Chris, Matthew, Laura and Lisa Hayden-Johnson](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/720/cpsprodpb/11f8/live/fce3df00-9bc9-11f1-98c6-93bfcdb08681.jpg)
Matthew Johnson said watching the documentary solidified his decision not to speak to his mother
- Published
As a child, Matthew Johnson was known as "Britain's sickest boy" - but in reality, his illness was just a fantasy made up by his mother to gain publicity and financial rewards.
For six-and-a-half years, Lisa Hayden-Johnson claimed Matthew had a long list of illnesses including diabetes, food allergies, cerebral palsy and cystic fibrosis, but years later it emerged she had made it all up.
Hayden-Johnson, from Torbay, Devon, was jailed and Matthew went into foster care and started a new life in Sheffield.
Both were interviewed for a Channel 4 documentary called Love You To Death but after hearing his mother speak, Matthew said he had "mixed emotions" and it reinforced his decision not to speak to her.
Speaking to the BBC about how it felt to hear his mother's point of view, he said: "It was a lot of disappointment but I think also frustration as almost two decades on, there is still a lack of accountability from her side.
"When I could see, even after two decades... she still holds the same story and believes that she did the best by me... that obviously isn't right."
Hayden-Johnson was 35 when she was jailed for three years and three months by a judge at Exeter Crown Court in 2010.
The court heard her lies began when Matthew was born prematurely in 2001 and given a tube for feeding.
He recovered but his mother insisted that this was not the case.
![A man with dark brown hair wearing a blue shift and dark jumper.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/3090/live/31c21ed0-9bd9-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Matthew Johnson said his mother "still holds the same story" after two decades
Hayden-Johnson lied about her son's health for years, claiming he had symptoms despite doctors being unable to find any.
She also told doctors the child had diabetes and spiked his urine samples with glucose in order to fool tests.
Doctors, friends, family and even the boy's father believed the child was unable to eat or swallow food.
Her actions led to Matthew being operated on and being fed through a tube in his stomach.
She introduced him in a wheelchair to the then Duchess of Cornwall, now Queen Camilla, appeared on television and amassed Â£130,000 in benefits after claiming Â£20,000 a year in disability living allowance.
She was given gifts from children's charities including a new car, a cruise in Tenerife, and also free X-Factor tickets.
It wasn't until 2007 that a paediatrician became suspicious that Matthew's health problems had gone on for so long without a clear diagnosis.
Hayden-Johnson was eventually arrested in October 2007 and jailed three years later.
![A mother and child in a church, the child is a young boy who has a tube in his nose and a red badge which reads 'Women's Own Children of Courage'](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/173d/live/4fba20d0-9bda-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Matthew said he wants to focus on his life now and leave the past behind
Matthew said thinking back to the time his mother's lies unravelled was like a "fever dream".
"I was taken into foster care. I was looked after by a few different people, taken away from my dad and my sister, the family pets. It was quite difficult," he said.
"But as I look back, it was something that happened quite quickly and I was able to draw a fresh slate when I moved to Sheffield and that's how I've sort of managed to move on from it.
"I always like to say that my life mainly started when I was in Sheffield and I can just make the most of that part and leave the other part behind."
![A woman with auburn chin-length hair in a green top and black suit jacket, wearing a silver crucifix.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/3400/live/29b87900-9bd9-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Hayden-Johnson, from Torbay, Devon, said she acted in her son's best interests
He credits his family and friends for helping him through his ordeal.
"My sister Laura has been really supportive throughout the whole process. We've always been side by side."
Matthew's father was cleared of any involvement as he was also duped by Hayden-Johnson.
"My dad's always looked after me," Matthew said.
"His life got turned upside down at the same time, so I really appreciate everything he's done for me throughout the years.
"Also, I think you kind of just have to carry yourself through it because there's only really you that can decide what mindset you choose to have on it.
"I think that's the most important part. It's the decision to not dwell and the decision to look forward rather than in the past."
Love You To Death will be broadcast on Channel 4 at 21:00 BST.
If you've been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via BBC Action Line
8171afa8539786c3d8b25c07.summary: Matthew Johnson, once known as "Britain's sickest boy," has spoken out after his mother, Lisa Hayden-Johnson, faked numerous illnesses for years to gain publicity, gifts, and financial rewards. Hayden-Johnson was jailed in 2010 after a paediatrician grew suspicious, leading to Matthew being placed in foster care and starting a new life in Sheffield. Following a recent documentary featuring both of them, Matthew expressed disappointment over his mother's continued lack of accountability and reinforced his decision to cut ties with her.
key_points: Lisa Hayden-Johnson falsely claimed for over six years that her son Matthew suffered from severe illnesses like cystic fibrosis and cerebral palsy.
Her actions resulted in unnecessary medical procedures for Matthew, £130,000 in fraudulent benefits, and charity gifts before she was jailed in 2010.
Matthew was taken into foster care in 2007 before eventually starting a new life in Sheffield.
After watching a Channel 4 documentary featuring his mother, Matthew stated she still lacks accountability and maintains she did the best for him.
